There have been some early signs that Infantino’s tactics are paying off, with the president of the Jamaican federation, Michael Ricketts, this week backing the status quo and comparing Uefa to spoiled children.

“Infantino might have made a mistake, but the intentions were to help Caribbean countries or help smaller countries,” Rickets told the Jamaica Observer. “Can you imagine Jamaica getting $40m to invest in football? Can you imagine the difference that would make in four or five years?

“I am not supporting Uefa because I think that they always want to be in opposition and always want to oppose. It doesn’t matter who is president, they are going to have issues. It doesn’t matter how well the president does, they are going to have issues and I think that Uefa is behaving like a set of spoilt kids.”

Uefa’s 55 members are believed to be united but the strength of the AFC alliance is unclear, with Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates having defied the confederation by endorsing Infantino.

Infantino last weekend reaffirmed his intention to seek re-election for a fourth term. The deadline for other candidates seeking to stand is 18 November.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
Sports.content:
A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.

Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.

However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.

Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Mika Baur scored his first Celtic goal at McDiarmid Park. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

The German midfielder struck from close range early in the second half after the debutant Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone had produced a stunning first-half save to deny Saints midfielder Joel Cotterill.

It was a night when the Celtic head coach, Martin O’Neill, was able to demonstrate the depth of his squad before Sunday’s Old Firm meeting away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup, with key players such as Camilo Duran, Benjamin Nygren and Kieran Tierney on the bench and defender Cameron Carter-Vickers given the evening off.

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out a sixth consecutive league victory this term and their 13th in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

Sports.title: Rosario ‘grabbed my bottom’ during Manchester City’s win at Porto, claims Haaland
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland has claimed Pablo Rosario “grabbed my bottom” during Manchester City’s 2-0 win at Porto on Tuesday. The incident occurred in the 92nd minute, with Haaland having scored City’s goals. The forward and midfielder grappled, went to ground and were booked after being separated.

“I was really keen on a hat-trick and it seemed like he was very eager to stop me from getting it,” Haaland told Norway’s TV 2. “It was a little interesting, that – you’ll be seeing a picture where he’s grabbing my bottom. It’ll be interesting to see that picture.”

The flashpoint followed one as half-time neared in a niggly encounter. After Marc Guéhi and Gabriel Veiga had a coming together that left the latter with a head injury, tempers frayed. When the teams walked off for the interval a bust-up occurred involving players and staff near the tunnel.

Images showed Rúben Dias placing a hand on what appeared to be Francesco Farioli, the Porto head coach. Uefa will wait for the match report of the referee, Szymon Marciniak, and its delegate, Stéphanie Ford, before deciding whether to bring any action against the defender or City.

Haaland’s 47th-minute opener was a header and the No 9 revealed he had been working on the skill recently with his dad, Alf Inge, a former City player.

“Two days ago I was practising headers with my dad in the garden,” he said. “Over the years, I’ve worked a lot on my heading. I’ve improved it massively and it’s become a strength of my game. I think a lot of it comes down to experience.”

Haaland concurred with his manager, Enzo Maresca, that he may need a break soon. “It’s not easy to get any rest in this business,” the 26-year-old said.

“Like during the international break, we play four games in 10 or 11 days, so it’s not easy. But you have to try to squeeze in a few days here and there and give your mind a bit of a break.”

Sports.title: Champions League roundup: Raphinha shines as Barcelona thrash Feyenoord
Sports.content:
Raphinha let his goals do the talking after being omitted from the Ballon d’Or shortlist, striking twice as Barcelona eased to a 5-1 win over Feyenoord in the Champions League.

The Brazilian was a surprise omission from this week’s 30-strong list of candidates for the prestigious award but brushed any disappointment aside to continue his early season hot streak at a rain-soaked Camp Nou. The forward finished brilliantly in the third minute and added a second just before the hour mark to down the Eredivisie side and take his tally to eight goals in six outings at the start of the campaign.

The summer signing Karim Adeyemi produced a stunning finish, Lamine Yamal stroked a free-kick through a gap in the Dutch wall and recent arrival Gabriel Jesus opened his account for the club just two minutes after stepping off the bench.

There was little to celebrate for Giovanni van Bronckhorst on his Barça return but Sem Steijn gave the visiting fans something to enjoy when he poked in at far post late on.

“The most important thing is we are playing like a team, like one unit,” the Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, said. “We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play.”

Ferran Torres scored a hat-trick and Ousmane Dembélé also starred as Paris Saint-Germain began their quest to win a third successive Champions League title by thrashing Slovan Bratislava 6-1 at the Parc des Princes.

View image in fullscreen Paris Saint-Germain’s Ferran Torres celebrates scoring their fifth goal with Ousmane Dembélé. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembélé had scored twice by the midway point of the first half in the French capital, and then set up Spain’s World Cup final hero Torres to make it 3-0 by the interval.

Torres, a close-season signing from Barcelona, added two more just after the restart to complete his hat-trick before the hour mark, with Suleiman Camara pulling one back for the Slovakian champions and Fabián Ruiz then sealing PSG’s win.

Elsewhere, Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic struck a 12-minute first-half hat-trick to ⁠earn ⁠a ​3-1 victory over Viking Stavanger.

He opened the ​scoring after 20 minutes with a touch at the near post, but Viking, making their first appearance in the league phase of the Champions League, were level two minutes later when Zlatko Tripic finished a ⁠swift counter-attack with his left foot.

Sports.title: Carrick up for ‘magical’ Champions League but derby timing ‘not ideal’
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is excited to lead Manchester United on their return to the “magical” Champions League but admitted playing on Thursday night was “not ideal” with the derby on Sunday.

United welcome Sabah to Old Trafford after a two-year Champions League absence. The Azerbaijani club are making their debut among Europe’s elite, having been in existence for less than a decade.

“It’s a magical competition,” Carrick, who won the competition in 2008 with United, said. “It’s where we all want to be. When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is, and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it. I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years.

“It’s where we want to be, it’s what we want to get back to, and it’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best. We’re delighted to be here, but we’re not here to just enjoy the occasion. We’re here to do business and go as far as we possibly can.

“To win the Champions League for me was the ultimate and was the best feeling I’ve had. Be nice some day to feel that again.”

United have made a mixed start to their Premier League campaign, picking up four points from three games, and this will be a testing period for a club that played just 40 games last season. If United reach the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup, they will not have a free midweek until mid-January.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick won the Champions League in 2008 against Chelsea in Moscow. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

Manchester City visit Old Trafford on Sunday and will have an extra two days to recover from their game at Porto on Tuesday. “I’m not concerned,” Carrick said of the turnaround.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I wouldn’t say it’s ideal in some ways, but it’s not something that we’ve given too much thought about. We’re not in control of that. We’ve got to deal with the cards that we’re dealt and that’s what it is, so we’ll make the most of it.”

United’s only senior left-back, Luke Shaw, did not train on Wednesday after being given a further day of rest. “We’ll see by tomorrow how he is, but it’s not an ongoing thing or a plan,” Carrick said.

Sports.title: Dave Portnoy claims Aryna Sabalenka is 'dead to me' as he reveals bizarre feud with tennis star
Sports.content:
Barstool Sports president Dave Portnoy took shots at reigning and two-time defending US Open champion Aryna Sabalenka over a snub for his content machine.

Portnoy, 49, revealed in a post to X that he was 'not a huge tennis guy' but once was close to the Belarusian star.

'I've bet [tennis] a couple times. I was a big Sabalenka guy,' Portnoy posted to his social media account.

'Sabalenka invited me to sit in her box for the U.S. Open against Coco [Gauff] before anybody f***ing knew who she was.

'And then I asked her to do a pizza review and she's like 'Yes. Yes, yes.' And then she got whooshed up into David Grutman in Hollywood and blew me off. So, she was dead to me.'

Sabalenka, who was the No. 2 tennis player in the world at the time Portnoy sat in her player's box for the 2023 US Open Final, lost that match to Gauff – but moved up to the No. 1 ranking shortly after.

Dave Portnoy says tennis star Aryna Sabalenka is 'dead to me' after she spurned him

Portnoy was in Sabalenka's box for the US Open final in 2023, where she lost to Coco Gauff

Portnoy and Sabalenka even linked up at a nightclub and shared this photo months after

Despite Portnoy's claim that she was 'dead to me,' images emerged of the two of them partying in Miami months later.

Portnoy even posted a snap of them at the time with the caption, 'The Queen of Tennis @SabalenkaA.'

The Barstool president posted multiple images and videos of Sabalenka during her run that year, even sharing bets he placed on her success.

But since the pizza invite fell through, it appears the relationship has soured – especially after Sabalenka and Grutman, a hospitality entrepreneur behind the LIV nightclub in Miami, grew closer.

Grutman hosted a controversial welcome party for this year's US Open, sponsored by DraftKings, which Sabalenka attended alongside fellow tennis stars like Serena Williams, Taylor Fritz, Gauff, Alex Eala and more.

The revelation of Portnoy's beef with Sabalenka came in a larger rant about the lateness of Ben Shelton's five-set thriller over Carlos Alcaraz that went until 3:33am ET on Wednesday morning.

'What is the U.S. Open doing having matches end at 3:30 in the morning? How dumb are you?' he said.

'Like what are you doing? 3:30 in the morning? I've had this rant in years past. Only the Blutmans [Barstool staffer Liam Blutman] are up and it's a huge match. It's Alcatraz losing to Trinity Rodman's boyfriend, Blake [Ben] Shelton.

How stupid are the people running the U.S. Open? https://t.co/dsdWWoCcPk pic.twitter.com/FBJq1ItlaQ — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) September 9, 2026

Portnoy's rant about Sabalenka came amid another tirade about the lateness of Tuesday evening's men's singles quarterfinal match between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz

Sabalenka, meanwhile, is off to the semifinals where she will take on Jessica Pegula

'That is a huge f***ing match. I'm not a tennis person but last night, if that's on at a reasonable hour, which nowadays for me is like 7:30 p.m., I'm watching that. But 3:30 a.m.? Who is watching that besides the Blutmans?'

Portnoy openly suggested the only way fans in the stadium could've stayed up for the nearly four-and-a-half hour match was by taking drugs.

'Like, what are they doing? How are you awake? It's so crazy,' he said. 'Who is running the U.S. Open that you're starting matches at like midnight or one in the morning?

'What are you doing? How stupid are some people? What is the advantage in that? 3:30 in the morning? You got to have rocks in your head.'

Sabalenka is off to the semifinals of the final Grand Slam of the year and will take on American star Jessica Pegula on Thursday.

Sports.title: Why Liverpool were RIGHT not to put a new deal on the table for Alexis Mac Allister... and sprint king Barcola won't be wasteful for long, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Why Liverpool were RIGHT not to put a new deal on the table for Alexis Mac Allister... and sprint king Barcola won't be wasteful for long, writes LEWIS STEELE

Given every win in the Champions League is worth £1.8million in prize money, Alexis Mac Allister has already helped Liverpool pay off a few months’ wages in the new deal he so craves.

The Argentine admirably went on record this week with a truthful missive to the club, saying he was ‘very sad’ they had told him they were not in a position to give him a new contract.

He talked about the pain of seeing midfield colleagues Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch get new deals, while he was left waiting by the phone for his employers to change their mind on his own future at the club he says he loves.

Little over 24 hours on from talking the talk, Mac Allister walked the walk and scored a thunderous goal to help Liverpool to a pleasing win over Atletico Madrid.

It was this fine finish – a shot much easier to skew and miskick into the night sky – that propelled Andoni Iraola to victory on his maiden European voyage.

On a night that looked like a potential banana skin between a team in transition and Diego Simeone’s well-drilled unit, Mac Allister settled it in Liverpool’s favour.

Alexis Mac Allister starred and scored the winner as Liverpool beat Atletico Madrid, a day after he cast doubt over his future

Mac Allister expressed his sadness that he hadn't been offered a new contract by the Reds

For that, his and father Carlos’s hands at the negotiating table have been significantly strengthened.

The Kop sang for Mac Allister, a chant that was not aired too much last season. He did start that campaign with a fitness issue and never looked like he had recovered his confidence. Liverpool’s midfield was bullied most weeks and he was the guiltiest party.

But in speaking up publicly, the player perhaps opened the eyes of some fans and reminded them that he is a human after all.

He loves the club and wants to stay, is keen to fight and ready to prove people wrong. That, it seems, has helped the fans turn back on his side.

It was not just the goal that pleased many on Wednesday night but the overall performance. Mac Allister, as he did at Ipswich last Friday, looked back to his best level after a season where his level dipped significantly.

On his day, Mac Allister can play with a bulldog-like tenacity off the ball, typical of an Argentinian midfielder, along with a guise and class on it. He did that in abundance here against Atletico, a club that has courted him over the last year or so.

So does this warrant a change of heart from Liverpool in terms of his new contract?

The first thing to say is that there is no need to panic over his future just yet. After all, he has the best part of two years remaining on his current deal and it is not like it expires at Christmas.

Two strong performances this week cannot change the fact he will be nearly 30 by the time this contract does expire.

But the early signs are promising that he is slowly reaching the level that saw him be regarded as in the very top bracket of players at the club in their Premier League title-winning campaign in 2024-25.

It was a welcome return to form for the Argentine star, who had his name sung by The Kop

Mac Allister was one of several Reds stars to struggle during a tricky campaign in 2025-26

If he continues like this, though, then he absolutely deserves to extend his stay at his beloved Anfield. Nights like this can only help in that regard and club legend Steven Gerrard had some advice for him too.

‘You let your football do the talking,’ said the former Reds captain on TNT Sports. ‘I thought he was outstanding.

‘He got an early yellow card that could have affected them… but to come up with a stunning strike and to play with composure and discipline after the yellow card, was outstanding.

‘That's the way, speak above, let the football do the talking. Show the experience, show your football, show that you’re a top international player, and trust me, this club… they will reward you.’

Gerrard is right. The door might be shut right now but it is not locked and he can still convince Liverpool to change their mind. Performances like this certainly will help.

How did Barcola’s full debut go?

Bradley Barcola managed to break records within minutes of coming off the bench at Ipswich’s Portman Road on Friday night, smashing the fastest sprint speed clocked in the Premier League this season.

He showed similar bursts of pace on his first start and full debut at Anfield here, and was unlucky not to open his goal-scoring account.

Had the match ended in dropped points for Liverpool, ire might turn to Barcola’s wastefulness in front of goal. He should be doing better but, as Iraola pointed out after the match, the fact he was in the position was pleasing enough for him.

Barcola combined well with Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who put in a fine display. Liverpool fans will hope that is a sign of things to come. If all three are on song, the possibilities are endless for the Reds this term and beyond.

Bradley Barcola made his full debut for Liverpool and showed several promising signs

Iraola’s boys up for the scrap

The first weeks of the Iraola era have had more positives than negatives. They have had things to get excited about and equally some to worry fans. There are still some uncertainties.

But one thing that is not in doubt is their fighting spirit. They came from behind against Newcastle to draw 2-2, they did the same against Nottingham Forest.

In the situation Liverpool found themselves in here, a goal down against a well-drilled Atletico side, they might have wilted last term. Not any more. They put up a fight and have given fans something to get behind.

And they are exhilarating to watch on the ball, too. In one attack in the second half, Liverpool had a six-on-two situation.

The Reds were criticised for being boring last year under Arne Slot. If Iraola has done one thing, it is to make Liverpool fun again.

Sports.title: The five worst cricket teams to tour England in the last five decades - where do Pakistan's 2026 side rank after series from hell?
Sports.content:
The five worst cricket teams to tour England in the last five decades - where do Pakistan's 2026 side rank after series from hell?

Pakistan’s tour to the UK has lurched from one crisis to the next, with horrific on-field performances matched by barely believable events off it.

Babar Azam’s team appear appear to be careering to a 3-0 whitewash after barely laying a glove on an England side that came into this series devoid of confidence themselves, following a winless 18 months in multi-match series and seeking new direction under the new captaincy of Joe Root after the retirement of Ben Stokes.

But how does this set of performances and results compare to the very worst by touring teams here over the past 50 years?

Here Daily Mail Sport ranks the top five worst...

5th: Pakistan, 1978

Series result: England win 2-0

Thrashed in the two 55-over matches preceding the three-match series, a team led by Wasim Bari were regularly sliced and diced by an emerging Ian Botham.

At Lord’s, Botham became the only cricketer in history to score a Test hundred and take an eight-wicket haul in the same match.

Pakistan had two of the three leading scorers in the series in Sadiq Mohammad and Mohsin Khan, but a distinct lack of depth to their travelling party diluted any competitive edge they might have boasted.

The Pakistanis produced an average score of 169, losing the first two Tests by an innings. The highest average among their other top-six players was in the teens. Without Imran Khan, the bowling lacked venom.

Ian Botham (right) was at his explosive best against Pakistan in 1978, dismantling a side captained by Wasim Bari (left)

4th: India, 2011

Series result: England win 4-0

The presence of icons like Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid and Mahendra Singh Dhoni made the chasm between India’s team of 15 years ago and England all the more galling for their passionate fanbase.

Dravid struck three hundreds across the four matches, but all ended in defeat - two by an innings and the other two by margins of 196 and 319 runs.

The bowling offered nothing once Zaheer Khan limped out early, contributing to Dhoni whipping off his pads off to bowl at Lord’s, and Zaheer’s fellow left armer RP Singh being lured from a beach holiday in Florida.

All told they accounted for just 47 of the 80 available England wickets. During two months here, they also lost the one-off Twenty20 international and left winless, following a 3-0 scoreline in the one-dayers.

The great Sachin Tendulkar (pictured) was one of a number of star names in India's team in 2011 - but it didn't stop them getting hammered by England

3rd: Australia, 1985

Series result: England win 3-1

It was the same series result as four years previously, only this 3-1 England win lacked the high quality drama of its Botham-fronted predecessor.

The Australians under Allan Border were in a huge state of flux, although they did not have to contend with the selection restrictions placed upon their 1975 counterparts due to World Series Cricket.

Bob Holland and Murray Bennett were chosen to bowl spin while 20-year-old newbie Craig McDermott was in a seam-bowling cartel including an over-the-hill Jeff Thomson, who turned 35 in the mauling at Edgbaston in the fifth Test of six.

Australia had been level at 1-1 thanks to the heroics of Border, their one world-class talent, at Lord’s, but from the third Test onwards it felt like holding back the dam.

England were hardly a vintage outfit themselves during the 1980s, but innings wins for David Gower’s men in the fifth and sixth matches emphasised what a summer of home dominance it had been.

Allan Border is bowled by Richard Ellison (top right) during the fifth Test of the 1985 Ashes. His side lost comfortably to an England team that were hardly a vintage outfit themselves

2nd: Bangladesh, 2005

Series result: England win 2-0

Michael Vaughan’s England flexed their muscles for the historic Ashes victory later that summer by toying with a team that had only been playing Test cricket for five years.

Conceding runs at 5.13 runs per over and unable to bat for more than 40 overs until the final innings of the two-match series, it was a privilege of which they didn’t look worthy.

England bowled woefully by their own admission at Lord’s, yet were abetted by some questionable shot selections from the Bangladeshis. Such was the gulf in quality between the teams, in fact, that Vaughan declared at lunch on day two at Chester-le-Street, just three wickets down.

Both Tests concluded on their third mornings. The only solace for the tourists came in Cardiff with a triangular tournament win for the ages against Australia.

Steve Harmison celebrates dismissing Bangladesh's Nafis Iqbal in the first Test as Lord's

1st: Pakistan, 2026

Series result: England winning 2-0 midway through third Test

From the removal of Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and the unprecedented sacking of seven players two-thirds of the way into the series, to the resignation of Misbah-ul-Haq as a selector and an investigation into conduct within the squad, there hasn’t been a dull moment.

Amid the chaos came a tongue in cheek observation that the call-ups of Mohammad Imran Randhawa, 29, and Mohammad Imran Jr, 25, had come about because they didn’t know which one to pick.

The latter had only made eight first-class appearances in five years as a professional cricketer, making him in customary Pakistani cricket logic, the obvious favourite.

Babar Azam’s team appear appear to be careering to a 3-0 whitewash after barely laying a glove on an England side that came into this series devoid of confidence

The bowling has thus far bared more teeth in Birmingham, via the inclusion of the slingy Razaullah, but the batsmen are on course to pack an ignominious record with them when they depart.

Since the World Wars, no team has finished a Test campaign here without having reached 200 at least once – Pakistan have so far made 171, 135, 110, 194 and 133.

Only one opportunity for remedy remains.

Sports.title: Inside 'control freak' Benjamin Sesko's fight to start for Manchester United: Bulked-up striker's virtual reality glasses, mind coach, meditation and why Michael Carrick is persisting with struggling front four
Sports.content:
Inside 'control freak' Benjamin Sesko's fight to start for Manchester United: Bulked-up striker's virtual reality glasses, mind coach, meditation and why Michael Carrick is persisting with struggling front four

The media in Slovenia have been bristling with indignation in the build-up to Manchester United’s return to the Champions League over Michael Carrick’s treatment of Benjamin Sesko.

‘The Champions League is back! Is Sesko a victim of the coach’s system?’ asked the country’s rights-holding TV channel 24ur Sport. Leading website Ekipa took aim at Matheus Cunha, the ‘false nine’ who has been keeping Sesko out of the team in the first three games of the season.

‘Sesko flies on the shameful numbers of the Brazilian – fans firmly against Carrick,’ it proclaimed in response to their Slovenian favourite climbing off the bench to score in the 2-2 draw at Everton on Sunday, after replacing a rather anonymous Cunha.

‘He (Cunha) completely failed, showing a catastrophic performance. A total zero. Cunha ended with zero shots on target, zero assists, zero dribbles. He lost the ball 11 times and was beaten in every aerial duel.

‘But Carrick insisting that Sesko is still more effective on the bench, while the Brazilian plays up front, is driving fans crazy. Sesko has to play from the first minute, they’re yelling.’

While the clamour for Sesko to start may still be some way short of a crescendo, at least in Manchester, he will be hoping to get his chance over the next few days as Carrick manages his players’ minutes across Thursday night’s Champions League opener at home to Azerbaijani minnows Sabah and Sunday’s 199th Manchester derby at Old Trafford.

Benjamin Sesko has become adept at scoring goals for Manchester United after coming off the bench, the latest of which came against Everton at the weekend

The Slovenian's form has convinced supporters that boss Michael Carrick should start him - according to the Press in his home country, at least

United’s head coach knows he cannot risk losing on Thursday to a club that only came into existence in 2017 and are managed by Valdas Dambrauskas, a man who paid for his coaching education by winning the present-day equivalent of £2,500 on Lithuania’s version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire? in 2002.

However, United’s below-par start to the season – taking four points from Hull, Ipswich and Everton – has left them with even less margin for error against Manchester City than usual. Whether that means a first start for Sesko after three appearances as a substitute remains to be seen.

It depends if Carrick sticks to the false nine in his 4-2-3-1 formation he has used throughout the summer and in the opening games of the campaign. Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle in pre-season before reverting to the right wing when Amad Diallo was injured before the first game, and Cunha has filled the false nine role since.

Meanwhile, Sesko was given time off to recover from the troublesome shin injury which forced him to miss the tail end of his first season at United following a £74million move from RB Leipzig, and did not feature at all.

The summer began with a private 23rd birthday party for his fan club, an annual affair in the striker’s hometown of Radece. But judging by his muscular physique, he skipped the cake and spent his time largely in the gym.

The man once described as ‘a control freak’ by former United boss Ruben Amorim has bought a house with its own gymnasium, pool, ice bath and sauna so he can continue his workouts and recovery at home, and is known to use the hyperbaric chamber at Carrington, red-light therapy and a personal fitness trainer.

That’s before you get into the virtual reality glasses that help him simulate game scenarios, a mind coach and meditation.

Sesko heads home against Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, giving United a late lead later cancelled out by Ainsley Maitland-Niles

Matheus Cunha, on the other hand, has offered little threat this season and blazed over the bar in the first half against Everton when he should have scored

‘Ben’s obviously getting closer and closer,’ said Carrick on Wednesday. ‘Since the Liverpool game at the end of April is a long time to miss. We’ve had to look after him to get him fit.

‘He’s probably trained three and a bit weeks fully with no restrictions. I think you can see that, coming onto the pitch and getting his rhythm. It was a fantastic goal (against Everton), and what he did an awful lot for us last season.

‘So, he's in a good place. He'll obviously be part of each and every game, and it's just a case of when he takes that next step.’

After scoring just twice for Amorim before the Portuguese coach was sacked in January, Sesko thrived under Darren Fletcher who started the Slovenian in both his games as caretaker coach and was rewarded with three goals. Seven more followed in 13 games under Carrick even though Sesko began the first six of them on the bench.

He had a run of four starts before injury struck and the new head coach reverted to a false nine and Cunha. That has continued so far this season. Interestingly, United’s Under 21s and Under 18s have adopted a similar tactic, suggesting it may be a club-wide shift.

Cunha has offered little threat this season, however, dropping too deep or drifting too wide to give his team a focal point through the middle. Bruno Fernandes can often be the player furthest forward when United attack, or jump out of his No10 position to lead the press when they switch to a 4-2-4 formation out of possession.

The United captain scored a hat-trick against Ipswich and Mbeumo followed up his strike against the Premier League newcomers with an excellent solo effort at Everton on Sunday.

Marcus Rashford has looked bright since his return to United, and was arguably their best player at the Hill Dickinson Stadium before going off when he overstretched a hamstring.

If Rashford is ruled out against Sabah, Cunha could revert to the left flank – if he isn’t rested altogether – and create an opening for Sesko.

Sesko scored 11 league goals last season from 30 appearances - but 13 of those appearances were from the bench

The Slovenian striker is 6ft 5in tall and noticeably more muscular this season

Carrick has a number of options at his disposal, but so far he has struggled to get the best out of them despite fielding a dynamic front four of Cunha, Rashford, Mbeumo and Fernandes. United miss the direct running of Amad, who hasn’t resumed training outside yet and may not re-appear until after the international break.

They were outshot 18-14 by an Everton side desperate for a new striker and had a lower xG than their opponents, with Cunha blazing over the bar in the first half when he should have scored.

As soon as he was replaced by Sesko, United responded to having a more conventional target man who – at 6ft 5in tall and noticeably more muscular this season – presented a greater physical threat to the Everton defence.

They couldn’t stop him when Luke Shaw floated over a cross and he headed in what looked like being the winner before Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored a dramatic late equaliser.

‘It’s nice to be back,’ said Sesko. ‘It’s the best feeling when I’m scoring, especially like that. It’s my job to provide goals and points for the team.’

Will it be enough to convince Carrick that he deserves a start against Sabah on Thursday night? According to 24ur Sport, it ‘seems like the perfect opportunity’.

Sports.title: Inside the Harlequins revamp: From 'chasing points' to emulating Toulouse, how the man who made new All Blacks fly-half will get Marcus Smith back in England No10 shirt, supercharging the academy and putting power first
Sports.content:
Inside the Harlequins revamp: From 'chasing points' to emulating Toulouse, how the man who made new All Blacks fly-half will get Marcus Smith back in England No10 shirt, supercharging the academy and putting power first

A few days before the start of his pre-season, Marcus Smith booked a table at Positano in Guildford and sat down for dinner with Harlequins’ new attack coach, Brad Cooper.

They were joined by Sean Long, the skills coach, and together they drew up plans for the new season over a few bowls of pasta.

There was plenty to discuss. Cooper recently moved to London from New Zealand, where he coached the Hurricanes and worked closely with the All Blacks’ latest No10, Ruben Love. Love has overtaken Beauden Barrett and Richie Mo'unga in New Zealand’s fly-half battle, impressing with his multi-phase attacking game in the ongoing Test series with the Springboks.

Smith has slipped behind Fin Smith and George Ford in England’s playmaking pecking order and, with a World Cup on the horizon, his own international ambitions were brought to the table.

‘Marcus and Ruben are very similar,’ Cooper told Daily Mail Sport. ‘They both take responsibility for their own development. Ruben is one of the first in the building at 6am and one of the last to leave. I’ve seen exactly the same traits with Marcus.

‘We went to this little Italian joint and talked all things attack. I told him I take his development personally. It’s a two-way street. There’s no reason why he can’t be the No1 fly-half for England and a real force at the World Cup. It’s our job to get him there.

Brad Cooper has been brought in as attack coach from the Hurricanes in New Zealand

Cooper worked closely with Ruben Love to turn him into the new All Blacks fly-half

And now Cooper wants to work the same magic with Marcus Smith and make him England's first-choice at No10 ahead of next year's World Cup

‘My goal is to help him achieve that potential and live that out. The way we play will really suit him. At times last year, I don’t think he really got that momentum at Quins to play on top of teams.

'When they line break, it’s the ability to be patient and confident in your phase play. It looked a little bit hectic to me. They were chasing points. As soon as they line break, they want to finish it then and there, rather than go multi-phase and being confident.

'It’s a little bit of shape and structure inside the 22. Like Bordeaux, Toulouse, the Hurricanes. Hopefully we can get Marcus playing really consistently and that will lead to an English jersey.’

Veteran Australian Robbie Deans has joined Harlequins as performance director – often working remotely from Sydney but spending the bulk of this summer at the Holiday Inn beside the training ground.

In recent years, the Harlequins’ coaching group has splintered and that is one of the reasons why results tumbled on the pitch. Former coach Danny Wilson almost came to blows with a player last year and his replacement, Jason Gilmore – who has been backed to continue leading the club – inherited a rudderless operation at the beginning of the 2025-26 campaign.

It ended in a ninth-place finish and missing out on big-ticket Champions Cup rugby for this season, even after a late charge that saw them win three of their final four matches.

In his departing interview in August, former attack coach Nick Evans admitted: ‘I probably became a bit of a lone wolf – along with probably a few other people in the building – around what we felt the identity was. I had to fight my way a little bit internally around what I was doing.’

Cooper, Jordan Turner-Hall and Rob Hunter have all joined the club’s coaching operation, along with a deeper upheaval of the club’s strength and conditioning programme. In a bid to tighten bonds, one of their first assignments was to spend a weekend together on the south coast.

‘We did a bit of a team building trip to Portsmouth,’ said Turner-Hall, a former centre who made more than 100 appearances for the club and won the Premiership title in 2012. ‘We went for a swim, had a few beers and had some deep and honest chats. There are new coaches and a lot of new people coming in so it was good to steal some time together.

‘We played a game called Chase the Chicken. You chase the chicken through different bars and you’ve got to have a drink in each bar. Ed Spokes (head of recruitment) was the chicken.

'It was good to meet people. We had medical, strength and conditioning, coaches, management, interns. It got everyone involved and made them feel like they had a place here. People need to feel valued, whether you’re cooking food, doing analysis or whatever.

A rudderless 2025-26 campaign ended in a ninth-place finish and missing out on big-ticket Champions Cup rugby for this season

Jordan Turner-Hall and Jason Gilmore are among the new faces in a backroom shake-up for this season

Turner-Hall (centre) made more than 100 appearances for Quins as a player, winning the Premiership title in 2012

‘It’s good to have diversity of thought and people that see the game differently. You’re always going to have different opinions, which is a good thing. When you draw a line in the sand, everyone buys into it and supports each other. That’s what I’m feeling in and around this coaching space.’

Time will tell if Harlequins have finally discovered the right formula. The prospect of Smith firing on all cylinders alongside George Furbank, the England full-back who has joined from Northampton, will excite even the most jaded of supporters.

Yet questions remain about whether they have added enough muscle to compete with the likes of Bath, Leicester, Exeter and Northampton.

Deans admitted that late changes to the coaching team meant Quins largely ‘missed the recruitment cycle’. The club decided not to bring in injury cover for influential No 8 Alex Dombrandt, who faces a long spell on the sidelines with a knee injury.

Asked which youngster has impressed him most over pre-season, Cooper named back-row Seb Driscoll. The Welsh youngster is set to enjoy more game time this season as the club look to upskill and up their power on the pitch.

‘We’ve got an identity around our game model,’ said Turner-Hall, who will be focusing on defence. ‘We need to be powerful, we need to apply pressure and withstand pressure better, and we need possession. We will judge ourselves on that.

‘If we’re talking about power, that’s not just down to the coaches on the pitch. It’s aligning everything. It’s strength and conditioning coaches, our power stance, how powerful we can be in our first three steps off the line. It’s understanding your triggers, watching the ball, getting your chest over your toes and that power output in your first three steps. Then you’ve got collision power and carry power.

'We’ve got everyone pushing in the right direction. We’re not a huge team, so you’ve got to coach what you’ve got. We’ve got to be true to ourselves and understand what we are. Defensively, we are good around the breakdown. Technique and speed is big for us if we want to create a contest and move better.

'We probably need to create better pictures at the breakdown so we’re not getting punished with penalties. For me, it’s going to be a long journey but we’ll get after it. I can’t tell you where we’ll be, but we’ll back each other and stay tight.’

George Furbank, the England full-back and former Northampton captain, is the big-ticket addition through the doors at Quins this summer

Asked which youngster has impressed him most over pre-season, Cooper named back-row Seb Driscoll

England internationals Smith, Dombrandt, Cadan Murley, Chandler Cunningham-South and Fin Baxter are already on long-term contracts.

Deans and Cooper will inevitably tap into their southern hemisphere networks as they recruit for next year but there is an equal focus on homegrown stars. Work is being done to improve the talent coming through the academy pathway, having seen their rivals develop more prospects in recent campaigns.

‘When you look at Quins in the academy league, they have good ding-dongs with everyone,’ admitted Turner-Hall. ‘It’s more about the exposure and support when they get in the building.

'Sometimes they can get caught up with being on loan, not playing and getting left behind. We want to have good support around their development and keep them involved. We’ve got some Under 23s friendlies with guys like Sale and a few Champ teams. The big thing is getting them playing in Quins shirts.’

A new training facility has been commissioned at the club’s Surrey Sports Park base. A high-performance centre should be ready for next season, and an additional pitch will also be laid.

With an expectant supporter base who pay big money for tickets, Quins know there needs to be a return on their investment. If there isn’t, there may well be more changes at the top.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers jokingly brands Cole Palmer winning player of the match 'criminal' in video after Chelsea's madcap 6-3 win over Leeds
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers jokingly brands Cole Palmer winning player of the match 'criminal' in video after Chelsea's madcap 6-3 win over Leeds

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Morgan Rogers jokingly labelled Cole Palmer's player of the match award as 'criminal' after being overlooked following his performance in their 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Chelsea had looked at risk of crashing out at the third round stage after trailing 2-0 at Stamford Bridge.

The introduction of Rogers and Palmer among four half-time substitutes had helped the Blues to fight back in the second half.

Palmer scored twice in three minutes, including scoring from the penalty spot, to bring Chelsea back level.

His second was one of three assists from Rogers, with the £117million summer signing also laying on goals for Pedro Neto and Danny Welbeck as Chelsea took charge.

Valentin Barco and a late second from Welbeck, either side of Dominic Calvert-Lewin netting for Leeds – ultimately helped Chelsea seal a 6-3 win to progress.

"Mate, I got four assists!"

"That is criminal!"



Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk — Sky Sports Football (@SkyFootball) September 9, 2026

Morgan Rogers joked Cole Palmer receiving the player of the match award was 'criminal' after Chelsea's 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds

Palmer scored twice as Chelsea came from 2-0 down while Rogers provided three assists

Palmer noted that his penalty sparked Chelsea's comeback as the pair joked post-match

Rogers, who believed he had four assists, had jokingly expressed frustration in a post-match interview after discovering Palmer had landed the player of the match award over him.

'Mate, I got four assists,' Rogers said. 'I can't believe that, that is mental, he scored a pen.'

Palmer responded: 'I started the comeback, I will shout you out, I'll shout you out and say you should have had it.'

Rogers continued with his mock outrage, adding: 'That is mental, don't mention me, I am just a bystander, that is criminal.'

When he was asked whether he would present the trophy to Palmer, Rogers quipped: 'I will unfortunately yes, it is rigged.'

Rogers, who had previously played with his close friend Palmer as a youngster at Man City, did underline his excitement at playing for Chelsea after their impressive start to the season.

'The environment, the players, the coaching staff have allowed me in and let me show what I'm about,' Rogers said.

'To play with this calibre of players makes my life a lot easier. I can show my ability to the best of what's possible, and it's a really enjoyable team to play in.

'You can see it [building something special]. There's a lot to work on and it's early days but seeing these signs so early, it doesn't normally happen quite this early.

'It's exciting but we've still got a long way to go and a lot to achieve.'

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard is on a mission to put himself at top table of elite midfielders as captain's brilliance gives Arsenal the perfect start to Champions League campaign with victory at Napoli
Sports.content:
Arsenal issued a warning to their own fans before kick-off in Naples, strongly advising them not to wear club shirts or scarves, or use public transport to avoid being targeted by Napoli ultras. That was their biggest statement of the day — before Martin Odegaard, whose previous season was tarnished by injury and loss of form, ensured those travelling fans would be heading home in high spirits. As Christos Tzolis’s pass reached the Norwegian just outside the area, his eyes lit up, driving forward on that wand of a left foot. Once he saw a gap, the captain curled the ball with pace and precision into the bottom left-corner to get Arsenal’s Champions League campaign off to a winning start. It’s now four goals in five matches for Odegaard, who has entered this season on a mission to prove himself at the top table of elite midfielders after just one goal across all competitions last term. Runners up in both 2006 and 2026 — either side of a crushing Europa League final loss to Chelsea under Unai Emery — the Champions League remains Arsenal’s last frontier. A September night in Naples doesn’t dictate where the trophy will lie, but builds momentum and helps bypass the dreaded play-off round. They ought to use this result as a lesson going forward. Martin Odegaard score the only goal as last year's runners-up Arsenal began their Champions League campaign with a 1-0 win over Napoli Odegaard scored a stunning effort from outside the area to break the deadlock in Naples Mikel Arteta's side dominated the game but were made to wait for their opening goal Bukayo Saka blazed over from close range in Arsenal's best chance of the first half ‘That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game,’ manager Mikel Arteta said of Odegaard. ‘I feel he has this emotional state that he knows that the ball can go in and he is playing an incredible football match.’ By the 50-minute mark, Arsenal had Napoli camped around their own box, hoping for the pressure to relent. They struggled to get out and, on the rare occasion Napoli did, their attacks were snuffed out. Luckily for them, the Gunners didn’t come bearing a full arsenal — until Odegaard’s intervention. Viktor Gyokeres was given a rare start in place of Kai Havertz, using his physicality to hold up the ball. There was the odd moment of brilliance, such as an instep cross which Bukayo Saka tried meeting with a scissor-kick. MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS NAPOLI (4-3-3): Meret 6.5 (Milinkovic-Savic 46mins, 6.5); Di Lorenzo 6.5, Rrahmani 6.5, Marin 6.5, Olivera 6.5; Gilmour 6, Lobotka 6, De Bruyne 6.5; Politano 6 (Favasuli 58, 6), Hojlund 5, Alisson Santos 5 (Vergara 58, 6). Manager: Massimiliano Allegri 6. ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; White 6.5, Konsa 6.5, Gabriel 6.5, Hincapie 6; Rice 7.5, Merino 6.5 (Guimaraes 66, 6); Saka 6, Odegaard 8, Eze 6 (Tzolis 66, 6.5); Gyokeres 5.5. Goals: Odegaard Manager: Mikel Arteta 6.5. Referee: Glenn Nyberg 6.5. However, a theme of wastefulness ran through Arteta’s side. Chance after chance arrived, the ball either ending up in half-time substitute goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic’s grasp or well beyond the goal frame. Arteta at least showed he’d learned from the previous campaign, making four changes to the side which beat Chelsea on Sunday — Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Gyokeres making their first starts of the season. Saka’s looping cross to the back post reached Eze, who nodded the ball to Merino but his resulting header, with plenty of neck swivel, was palmed over by Alex Meret. Before the first half ended, Odegaard played Saka through, the winger hoofing the ball when one-v-one with the keeper. It was ruled offside, to spare his blushes. The triumvirate of Saka, Odegaard and Ben White were in sync, quick passes constantly exchanged to caused the hosts’ backline many a problem and give Saka avenues to get forward. Hincapie ought to have scored five minutes after the break. Odegaard’s clever, looping chip found White, his header teeing up Hincapie’s wild blaze over the bar. Arteta turned to Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and Havertz later and that soon helped change the game.

Sports.title: Coco Gauff keeps hopes of all-American US Open final alive as she survives thriller against Mirra Andreeva to seal spot in final four
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff overcame the trickiest test of her hunt for a second US Open title so far as she roared back from a set down to beat French Open champion Mirra Andreeva 2-6, 7-6(7), 6-2 - and book her spot in the semifinals.

After the match, she admitted that she had been inspired by fellow American and semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe, who beat Alex Michelsen over five sets on Tuesday.

'I think I had to reset,' Gauff said of her choppy first set, and how she returned to demolish Andreeva. 'I came out not feeling the ball, not giving her too many free points, Mirra was playing great.

'In the bathroom, honestly I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe yesterday, and how he came back (against Michelsen).

'I was trying to leave the court with no regrets.'

The two-time major winner is set to play the newly crowned world No 1 Elena Rybakina next, who beat Zheng Qinwen earlier on Wednesday to claim her spot at the top of the women's game.

Coco Gauff screams with delight after sealing her place in the US Open semifinal

Gauff threw her racket and looked to the heavens after beating Mirra Andreeva on Arthur Ashe

Gauff also keeps hope alive of an all-American final on Saturday, with US No 1 Jessica Pegula due to face Aryna Sabalenka in their semi-final on the opposite side of the draw.

But Gauff was by no means assured of a place in the last four after the first set, which saw the 2023 winner bamboozled by the Russian teenager.

Andreeva hurtled out of the starting blocks to build a formidable 5-1 lead, with Gauff only capable of holding her final service game before the set break.

Although the duo kept pace in the second set, Gauff cut a frustrated figure on-court, at times looking on the verge of tears as she remonstrated herself - and her players' box - over her lack of form.

The 22-year-old swiped the early break of serve to make it 4-2, but was immediately broken back by Andreeva, with neither woman holding onto their game until the match settled at 5-5.

Andreeva was seeded No 5 but did not have enough to overcome Gauff and the partisan crowd

Gauff faced match points but battled back to seal a huge win in front of the New York fans

Forcing a tiebreak, Gauff showed the very best of her level as she set up three match points before eventually sending the match to a deciding set.

Backed by a wildly partisan crowd cheering on their former champion, Gauff didn't slow down in the third as she broke Andreeva for 3-1, with the 19-year-old never again truly comfortable as her game slipped away from her and her error count rose.

At 5-2, Andreeva's frustration bubbled over, with the young star letting her racket fly, the instrument crashing into a pile of her belongings and forcing a cameraman to dodge out of the way. Andreeva then slumped into her chair, appearing to wipe her eyes before she returned to court.

Gauff proceeded to serve out the match in style, once again burnishing her credentials as a favorite for the title.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
