Speaking yesterday on the second day of the 2026 Gender and Inclusion Summit organised by Policy Innovation Centre (PIC) in Abuja, the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Salako, said harmful gender norms continued to constrain the health, safety, education and economic opportunities of young Nigerians.

Salako, who delivered the keynote address at the event, said gender norms were unwritten societal rules and expectations governing how boys, girls, men and women should behave, relate with one another and access opportunities.

He warned that when such norms were rooted in unfair cultural practices and sentiments, they could reinforce discrimination and expose adolescents to violence, early pregnancy, mental health challenges and poor health outcomes.

According to him, transforming gender norms was therefore essential to creating an environment where every adolescent, regardless of sex, could be safe, healthy, empowered and able to realise their full potential.

He explained that such norms shaped how adolescents thought and behaved, as well as their access to healthcare and other opportunities.

“When such norms are based on crude sentiments and cultural fixations that are unfair, they can become harmful and limit adolescents’ choices thus reinforcing discrimination, and increasing exposure to violence, early pregnancy, mental health challenges, and poor health outcomes,” Salako added.

The minister said the federal government, under the administration of President Bola Tinubu, had introduced a number of measures aimed at improving adolescent health, including the institutionalisation of adolescent and school health programmes and the establishment of a dedicated budget line for adolescent health.

He also highlighted the expansion of adolescent sexual and reproductive health services, including access to family planning, sexually transmitted infection and HIV prevention, counselling and other services under the National Sexual and Reproductive Health Policy 2025 to 2030.

Salako said the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare had also integrated gender and adolescent health programming through a dedicated Gender, Adolescent School Health and Elderly Care Division in its Family Health Department.

He said the arrangement was designed to address gender-related barriers to healthcare, gender-based vulnerabilities and the differing health needs of adolescent girls and boys.

The minister further disclosed that the federal government’s national Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign had reached more than 14 million adolescent girls aged between nine and 14 years nationwide, helping to protect them against future cervical cancer.

Salako also welcomed the findings of the Nigerian Survey on Gender Norms, Attitudes, Health and Wellbeing, describing the study as the first nationally representative data on the social and gender norms shaping health behaviours and outcomes among Nigerian adolescents.

He said the survey, which focused on adolescents aged 10 to 14, examined issues including child, early and forced marriage, gender-based violence, sexual and reproductive health, HPV vaccination and women’s economic empowerment.

“The evidence produced will be instrumental in informing policy formulation, programming, and advocacy across sectors including health, education, social protection, and economic empowerment,” he said.

Also speaking at the summit, the Deputy Director, Policy, Advocacy and Communications, Nigeria Country Office of the Gates Foundation, Ekenem Isichei, said the concept of the “last mile” should not be viewed merely in geographical terms, but in terms of the individual who ultimately needed to benefit from a policy or innovation.

Isichei said Africa was not short of policies, pilot programmes, technologies or commitments, but the more important question was whether those interventions were producing measurable improvements in people’s lives, particularly for women, young people, persons with disabilities and historically underserved communities.

He identified three critical shifts needed to turn ideas into impact: moving from commitments to execution, from access to agency and meaningful inclusion, and from successful pilots to systems capable of achieving sustainable scale.

“A policy announcement is not an outcome. A budget allocation is not a service,” he said, stressing that resources had to be released, commodities procured and distributed, frontline workers supported, facilities made ready and data effectively used before citizens could experience meaningful change.

He also cautioned against defining inclusion simply as providing access to technology or financial services, arguing that people must be able to use those services safely, affordably and meaningfully.

Isichei warned that as artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure and digital finance expanded, technology could reproduce existing inequalities if women, young people, persons with disabilities and underserved communities were excluded from the design process.

World.title: King’s College Old Boys Seek Probe of Students’ Involvement in PTA Protest
World.content:
• Accuse PTA of using minors to malign education minister

•Cite possible breaches of child’s rights, cybercrimes acts

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





King’s College Old Boys’ Association (KCOBA) has called for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the participation of students of King’s College Lagos in recent protests by sections of the school’s Parents–Teachers Association (PTA) against the federal government’s concession of the institution.

KCOBA, while acknowledging the right of the PTA and other stakeholders to challenge government policies, condemned what it described as the “weaponisation” of underage students in the dispute, particularly their alleged participation in protests where they chanted against the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa.

In a statement issued in Lagos, the association said the participation of children in the protest raised serious questions about their welfare, dignity, safety and the possible legal implications of recording and disseminating their participation on social media.

The release was signed by Alhaji Lateef Femi Okunnu (SAN), Chairman, KCOBA Board of Trustees; Chief Philip Asiodu, immediate Past Chairman, KCOBA Board of Trustees; Kashim Ibrahim-Imam, President, KCOBA; Dr. Leke Oshunniyi Secretary, KCOBA Board of Trustees and Etigwe Uwa (SAN), General Secretary, KCOBA.

The old boys’ association said it was particularly disturbed by video recordings showing students in school uniform participating in the protests and chanting the words against Alausa, arguing that there was a fundamental difference between challenging a government policy and encouraging children to publicly malign a serving public officer.

“There is a profound difference between voicing a dissent about a policy and teaching children to publicly brand a serving Federal Minister a ‘thief’ without any evidence or justification,” the group stated.

The association also questioned the circumstances in which the students were mobilised, asking who authorised their participation, what they were instructed to say and whether adequate consideration was given to their welfare and dignity.

It said the controversy went beyond the concession of the school, describing it as a question of the character and values being imparted to Nigerian children.

KCOBA further urged the relevant authorities to examine whether the participation and subsequent dissemination of recordings involving the minors breached provisions of the Child’s Rights Act.

According to the association, Section 11 of the Child’s Rights Act protects a child’s right to dignity and prohibits physical, mental or emotional injury, abuse, neglect or maltreatment, including attacks upon a child’s honour or reputation.

It therefore called for an inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the mobilisation of the students and their participation in the protest.

The association also raised what it described as a “serious digital dimension” to the incident, arguing that the recording and online dissemination of material involving identifiable schoolchildren required scrutiny.

KCOBA said the publication of statements portraying an identifiable public official as a thief could raise questions under the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, as amended in 2024, particularly where such statements were allegedly false and disseminated through computer systems.

It stressed that it had not prejudged the criminal liability of any protester but maintained that the circumstances warranted a “painstaking investigation” to determine whether any provisions of the Cybercrimes Act or Child’s Rights Act had been violated.

The association consequently called on the appropriate authorities to investigate the conduct of those involved and sanction anyone found to have breached the law.

Beyond the immediate protest, KCOBA defended its record of supporting King’s College, rejecting what it described as attempts by some protesters to portray old boys as seeking to undermine the institution.

KCOBA argued that its interventions demonstrated that its position on the current controversy was driven by its commitment to the institution and its students rather than opposition to legitimate scrutiny of the proposed concession.

The association said it was not asking the PTA to abandon its concerns over the concession, insisting that stakeholders remained entitled to ask questions and express their views.

“Let nobody misconstrue our position,” KCOBA said, adding that the PTA could express its opinion but should not “take the laws into its hands” or engage in conduct that could contravene Nigerian laws.

It also warned against placing schoolchildren at the centre of adult disputes, stressing that their safety, health, dignity and education should take precedence over the immediate objectives of any protest campaign.

The old boys called for an immediate end to the use of King’s College students in protests or mob action, an inquiry into the mobilisation of the minors and a forensic examination of recordings and their online dissemination.

It also demanded investigation of online publications that may have contravened the Cybercrimes Act and Child’s Rights Act, as well as appropriate sanctions against any teacher or parent found, after investigation, to have breached the law.

KCOBA maintained that King’s College, which opened in 1909, was established to provide young Nigerians with a high standard of education and prepare them for professional and public life.

It said the institution’s legacy required all stakeholders to demonstrate responsibility, discipline and respect for the law in resolving disagreements.

World.title: Will SASSA grants increase before November 2026 elections?
World.content:
Will look into the likelihood of a SASSA Grants increase before the November 4 elections. Image: File

Will South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) grants increase ahead of the November 2026 municipal elections? It is a fair question to ask after government hiked the SRD grant from R350 to R370 just before the May 2024 general election.

Of course, President Cyril Ramaphosa framed it as extended support to the unemployed. But political experts saw it for it was – a not-so-subtle election stunt to try keep the African National Congress (ANC) in power. And we all know how that turned out …

SASSA GRANTS INCREASE BEFORE NOVEMBER ELECTIONS

Now, another SASSA grants increase is making headlines, with EFF leader Julius Malema promising Older Person Grants of R4 500. Along with an allowance for unemployed graduates and free electricity for all SASSA recipients. Unfortunately, the red-bereted politician’s promises do not stand up to the slightest scrutiny.



You see, the Wednesday 4 November poll is a 2026 Local Government Election. It decides who sits on your municipal council, who runs your metro, and who’s accountable for potholes, water outages and refuse collection, that sort of thing. And it most certainly does not decide:

Who sits in the National Assembly.

Controls the Finance or Social Development portfolios.

Who is in charge of national budget allocation.

SASSA grant amounts are set nationally, through the National Treasury, delivered by the minister of Finance. A municipal council has no authority over any of that.

DON’T BANK ON SASSA GRANTS INCREASE

For four years, the SRD grant was stuck on R350. Then two months before the May 2024 general election it was increased. Can the same happen again? Image: File

As SASSA beneficiaries know all too well, any SASSA grants increase is tabled in the February Budget Speech. These take effect each year on 1 April. That cycle has already run its course and 2026/27 grant amounts are set and locked in till February 2027.



Therefore, there is physically no budget event, fiscal mechanism or legislative window between now and 4 November municipal elections for a SASSA grants increase. So, regardless of who promises what on their campaign trail, R2 400 (60-74) and R2 420 (over 75) is it for Older Person Grants, as is R580 for Child Support and R370 for SRD.

At the end of the day, Malema’s pitch is more like: Vote for the EFF locally to strengthen its case for what it can do in national government later. That’s a legitimate campaign strategy. And it handily removes the headache of actually explaining how it would fund a near-doubling of SASSA pension.

But what do you think? Should SASSA Grants increase again between now and the end of the financial year? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: New report: Thabo Cele fails Sundowns medical test
World.content:
Thabo Cele wins a Nedbank Cup match Man of the Match award in Kaizer Chiefs colours. Image: PSL media

The transfer has been placed in doubt after a concern with Cele’s knee emerged during the medical process at Sundowns.

This is according to iDiski Times journalist Joshua Hendricks.

THABO CELE TO MAMELODI SUNDOWNS IN JEOPARDY

“Thabo Cele’s proposed move to Sundowns has hit a stumbling block after a knee issue emerged during his medical,” the report said.



“Cele had previously been due to have knee surgery at Kaizer Chiefs but opted against it.

“The transfer has not collapsed, but the move is now hanging in the balance,” Hendricks concluded.

Despite the setback, the proposed move to Sundowns has not officially collapsed.



The medical concern could still be assessed by the club before a final decision is made. However, according to Hendricks, the transfer is now hanging in the balance.

Cele’s potential move to the reigning South African champions had appeared to be done and dusted.

The latest medical development means there is now uncertainty over whether the deal will ultimately be completed.



WHAT HAPPENS IN MEDICAL TESTS?

A football transfer medical is a detailed health and fitness assessment carried out before a player joins a new club.

It is designed to identify injury risks and help the buying club decide whether the player is a safe financial investment.

1. MEDICAL HISTORY

Doctors review previous injuries, operations, recurring problems and rehabilitation. A player’s concussion history may also be considered.



2. MUSCLE AND JOINT TESTS

Physios assess movement, flexibility, strength and joint stability. They look for weaknesses or muscle imbalances, particularly around areas such as the knees, hips, hamstrings and groin.

3. HEART AND FITNESS CHECKS

Players can undergo an ECG, echocardiogram and stress tests to assess heart health, blood pressure and how the body responds to intense exercise.



4. BLOOD, URINE AND BODY TESTS

Blood and urine samples can be used to check general health, including blood counts, liver and kidney function, bone health, infections and certain conditions. Body composition, including muscle and fat levels, can also be assessed.

5. SCANS

MRI scans, X-rays or ultrasounds can be carried out on areas where there is a known or suspected problem. This is particularly important when a player has a history of surgery or serious injury.



6. FITNESS TESTS

Depending on the club, players may also complete sprinting, strength and football-specific drills to assess their current physical condition and readiness.

WHAT HAPPENS IF A PLAYER FAILS?

A player “failing” a medical does not necessarily mean they cannot play football. It usually means the club has identified a medical risk it considers too high.



The club can walk away from the transfer, renegotiate the fee or contract, or include clauses that protect it against future injury problems.

In other words, the medical is not simply about asking whether a player can play now. It is about assessing the risks that could affect the player and the club in the future.

World.title: Full list: Orlando Pirates have now signed 12 players
World.content:
Orlando Pirates team against Le Cure Waves in the CAF Champions League in Mauritius. Image: Orlando Pirates media

Orlando Pirates have been extremely active in the transfer market as head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou continues to reshape his squad.

The latest addition being Bheki Mabuza who returns to a club where he previously developed.

WHO IS THE LATEST ORLANDO PIRATES SIGNING?

Mabuza originally came through the Orlando Pirates development structure before leaving to continue his career elsewhere.



The winger eventually found his feet at Marumo Gallants, where his explosive performances helped put him back on the radar of the Buccaneers.

The signing of Mabuza takes Orlando Pirates to an astonishing 12 arrivals during the current transfer window.

THREE SIGNIINGS FROM SAME BETWAY PREMMIERSHIP CLUB

The Buccaneers have heavily recruited from Siwelele FC, bringing in Ghampani Lungu, Neo Rapoo, Aphiwe Baliti and Bohlale Ngwato.

Lungu has already made an immediate impact after winning the club’s Player of the Month award, while Rapoo has added another promising option at left-back.

Baliti has returned to Siwelele FC on loan to continue his development, while Ngwato provides another option in the wide areas.

ORLANDO PIRATES SIGN PEDERSEN AND NKOTA FROM ABROAD

Orlando Pirates have also strengthened their attack with the signing of Norwegian striker Sebastian Pedersen from Sogndal Fotball.



The striker brings physical presence and a proven goalscoring record, although the technical team is still working on his match fitness.

Meanwhile, Mohau Nkota has returned to the club on loan from Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq.

TWO MIDFIELDERS FROM STELLENBOSCH FC

The midfield has also undergone significant changes, with Mthetheleli Mthiyane and Thapelo Mokobodi arriving from Stellenbosch FC.

Matome Mmolai has joined from Leicesterford City, while Kabelo Kgositsile arrived from Baroka FC.

At the back, Sbangani Zulu has added further defensive depth following his move from Richards Bay.

Now, Mabuza becomes the latest piece of the puzzle.

With 12 new players coming into the senior squad, Orlando Pirates have made their intentions clear.

They are building a squad capable of competing on multiple fronts, with domestic silverware and the CAF Champions League among their major targets.

The challenge for Ouaddou will now be turning this impressive collection of new arrivals into a team capable of delivering trophies.

World.title: Anele Mdoda’s wedding show coming to Netflix
World.content:
Anele Mdoda is set to share more of her love story in her upcoming Netflix wedding docu-soap.

South African media and radio personality Anele Mdoda will give fans a closer look at her journey to the altar in a new Netflix wedding docu-soap.

Titled Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza, the upcoming series will follow Mdoda and her husband, Bonelela “Buzza James” Mgudlwa, as they navigate their relationship and married life in the spotlight.

Netflix has confirmed that the series will premiere later in 2026, although the streaming platform has not announced an exact release date.



Dopezuluboi Productions produced the project, which will stream exclusively on Netflix.

ANELE MDODA’S LOVE STORY HEADS TO NETFLIX

The streaming giant has already given viewers a glimpse of what they can expect from the highly anticipated series.

According to Netflix, “Stars and Vows: Anele & Buzza | Coming Soon | From a budding romance to bridal bliss under the bright lights of fame, Stars and Vows: Anele & Buzza follows the love story of TV & radio personality Anele Mdoda and Bonelela “Buzza James” Mgudlwa as they navigate the challenges, joy and anticipation on the road to saying “I do.”

The announcement has already sparked excitement among fans who will now get to see a more personal side of the media personality.

Okay guys.



You are getting the visuals 😍 pic.twitter.com/0jC7TK1GJ3 — Anele Mdoda (@Anele) September 9, 2026

A STAR-STUDDED CREATIVE TEAM

The production brings together several prominent names from South Africa’s entertainment industry.



Actress and producer Nomzamo Mbatha is among the creators, alongside Teddy Geldart, Vuyo Sowah and Pet Tasara. Pascual Wakefield directs the series.

Bright Fire Productions also confirmed the project in a joint post with Anele, describing the production as a celebration of their relationship.

“Two souls. Two worlds. One extraordinary love story



Stars and Vows: Anele and Buzza is a beautiful reminder that sometimes love doesn’t arrive quietly — it arrives boldly, beautifully and completely unapologetically. A union of royal hearts and rebellious spirits, choosing each other, choosing love and choosing a life written beyond the rules.

Stars and Vows: Anele and Buzza.”

The production company’s statement highlights the couple’s journey while teasing the emotional story that viewers can expect when the series arrives.



ANELE MDODA’S WEDDING ROOTED IN XHOSA TRADITION

Mdoda and Buzza exchanged vows on 20 April 2025 in a vibrant ceremony that celebrated Xhosa culture and tradition.

Their wedding brought together love, family and heritage, making it a memorable chapter in their relationship.



Now, more than a year after their wedding, viewers will have the opportunity to see more of the journey behind the celebration.

Mdoda marked their first wedding anniversary on 20 April 2026 with a heartfelt tribute to her husband.

“Andonwabe. One year later my love @buzza_james thank you for the safest yet wildest fire of love. God loves us if he keeps doing it like this with us. My royal rebel.”



Her message offered fans another glimpse into the bond she shares with Buzza as they celebrated their first year of marriage.

FANS WILL SEE THE STORY BEHIND THE CELEBRATION

While the couple has already shared moments of their relationship publicly, Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza promises to take audiences much further behind the scenes.



The series will explore the anticipation, emotions and traditions surrounding their wedding while showing the couple navigating a major chapter in their lives.

For fans of Mdoda, the project also offers an opportunity to see her away from her familiar television and radio roles.

The combination of romance, family, culture and celebrity is expected to make the series an interesting watch for Netflix audiences.



Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza is scheduled to arrive on Netflix later in 2026. An official premiere date is still to be announced.

World.title: Checkers brings back discontinued chocolate – for now
World.content:
Checkers has quietly reintroduced a discontinued chocolate brand – Nestle’s Caravan – back onto shelves – for a limited period.

CHECKERS BRINGS BACK CARAVAN CHOCOLATE!

A week ago, Checkers polled its customers on which discontinued chocolate it should bring back to shelves. The options included: Beacon’s New Look and FFWD, Nestle’s Caravan and Cadbury’s 7777.

Although they did not reveal the poll results, consumers have reported finding the Chocolate bar, paired with Nestle’s Tex, on their shelves.



In a viral post, the Facebook page called 1986 Stories shared: “THIS IS NOT A DRILL 🚨🚨. The Caravan Chocolate is back! I bought this today, 7 September, at Checkers [for] R15.99”

According to the Shoprite Group, to which Checkers falls, the chocolate is back as a special-edition offering.

DISCONTINUED TREATS IN SOUTH AFRICA

Caravan was quietly discontinued long before the Covid-19 pandemic hit. According to Nestle, this was to make room for new product offerings.



The chocolate is one of many sweet treats that have ceased production and can no longer be found on shelves.

Others include Nestle’s Chocolate Log, Cadbury’s Tempo, Inside Story, FFWD, and Holey Moleys.

Other household products have also been given the chop – from Nesquik to TaB to Redro Fish Paste andHellmann’s mayonnaise.

World.title: ‘What Duba told me before I scored that freekick’ – Kaizer Chiefs new signing
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs’ newest signing, Faiz Abrahams has revealed what happened before he scored the freekick against Siwelele on Sunday.

Amakhosi won 3-2 at the Dobsonville Stadium and Abrahams was one of the scorers after a sublime freekick.

Leading 2-1, Chiefs were awarded a free kick in the 76th minute deep inside Siwelele territory, roughly midway between the left touchline and the penalty area. The new Amakhosi man lined up to take it and it seem he was going to cross it but went for goal.



“When I went to take the free kick, (Wandile) Duba told me not to cross the ball for anyone but to try and score,” Abrahams was quoted on Kaizer Chiefs website.

“It felt great because I have been working very hard,” he added

“I’m just going to keep working hard and giving my all in training. I aim to stay consistent and always keep my performance levels up.”

Kaizer Chiefs enjoying a good start to the season

After impressing this past weekend, Abrahams will look to maintain the same performance as Chiefs travel to Polokwane City on Saturday

“The coach will set a plan for this weekend, and we will go out and execute it,” he said.

The Betway Premiership encounter between Polokwane City and Kaizer Chiefs kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday, 12 September, at the old Peter Mokaba stadium. A win for the Glamour Boys will see them jump into second place on the log ahead of rivals Orlando Pirates.



Are you impressed with Abrahams?

World.title: Anele Tembe inquest: AKA ordered tequila, hotel said ‘NO’
World.content:
AKA and his entourage reportedly ordered tequila shooters after the death of his fiancee, Anele Tembe at the Pepperclub Hotel in 2021. Images via IG

A manager at the Pepperclub Hotel in Cape Town testified how they refused to serve rapper AKA – real name Kiernan Forbes – and his entourage tequila shooters after the death of his fiancée Anele Tembe just hours earlier. The testimony was heard during an inquest at the Cape Town Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.

Anele fell to her death from the 10th-floor balcony on 11 April 2021. According to witnesses, the couple had argued in their hotel room moments before her death.

Tragically, AKA was shot and killed by masked gunmen in Durban two years later.



ANELE TEMBE INQUEST: AKA DENIED TEQUILA SHOTS

On Wednesday, the inquest into Anele Tembe’s death continued, with the court hearing how a male hotel manager had refused to serve tequila shooters to a room occupied by AKA and his entourage.

The group placed the order at around 9:00 am, a little over an hour after Anele had fallen off her 10th-floor hotel balcony to her death on the pavement below. AKA did not go down to the ground floor to see Anele, but had remained in a neighbouring hotel room. A witness came to Anele’s aid, testifying how he had comforted and prayed over her until emergency services arrived.

The manager – whose identity was one of multiple witnesses the court ruled should remain private – told the court that the group had subsequently ordered alcohol, but he had refused to serve it.



He said, “I said it was not something we should entertain. They were not happy about the restrictions, and I had to speak to them.”

ANELE TEMBE INQUEST:



A hotel manager has told the inquest into Tembe’s death that staff stopped serving alcohol to her fiancé, the late rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes, after she fell to her death from the hotel’s 10th floor @NtuthuzeloNene — EWN Reporter (@ewnreporter) September 9, 2026

He said AKA and the others were unhappy with the restriction, but that the rapper did not become notably angry or upset.



A hotel guest corroborated the claims, testifying that “it did not make sense”, given what had happened moments earlier in the hotel room.

THE GRUESOME HOTEL ROOM

Also heard during the inquest was a detailed account of the evidence found in AKA and Anele Tembe’s hotel room.

According to a police investigator, the room was a “mess”, and evidence found suggested a physical struggle. This included a bloodied champagne bottle, blood on bed linen, towels and on a wall.



The room was also strewn with cans and cigarette butts.

A chair near the balcony was also found, with the investigator claiming that AKA had stated that Anele had climbed over the railing and jumped to her death. However, the Tembe family lawyer questioned why Anele’s fingerprints were not found on the railing.

The investigator shared that AKA had insisted on making a police statement shortly after Anele’s fall.



He told the court of his interaction with the rapper: “He didn’t look any sad or anything like that. He looked, to be honest, looked quite fine.

“I’ve dealt with a lot of cases with people that will cry, and some people will be [sitting] still, don’t talk to you at all. He looked quite fine to me, to be honest.”

ANELE TEMBE’S DAD: ‘WHO DOES THAT?

In 2024, author Melinda Ferguson published her book, When Love Kills, A Tragic Tale about AKA and Anele. In it, Anele Tembe’s father, Moses, questioned AKA’s actions following his daughter’s balcony fall.



He said in the book: “Who doesn’t go down and try to help the woman he loves when he sees her lying in the street?

“No one who saw the body of the woman they loved wouldn’t have rushed down to help her. She wasn’t dead.

“When Rob Stefanutto [an eyewitness] approached Anele, she responded by blinking. Within minutes of seeing his fiancée lying on the road, Kiernan orders tequila. Who does that?”

World.title: Mapisa-Nqakula corruption trial resumes after medical break
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Defence Minister and former National Assembly Speaker Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is expected back on the witness stand as her corruption trial continues.

Proceedings were cut short on Wednesday after Mapisa-Nqakula requested medical assistance. Her legal team told the court she was suffering from exhaustion following the lengthy proceedings.

It remains unclear whether she will be well enough to return to court on Thursday and complete her evidence-in-chief.

Once she has finished giving evidence, the State is expected to cross-examine her.

Mapisa-Nqakula faces allegations that she solicited bribes from defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu.

She has pleaded not guilty and denies receiving any money from the businesswoman.

During her testimony, Mapisa-Nqakula told the court that renovations were carried out at her home to improve security after she received what she described as multiple threats to her life.

She did not provide details about the threats but told the court that the Department of Public Works contributed towards the cost of the renovations.

World.title: Ndodana Tshuma extradition case gets underway
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Prosecuting Authority has entered into a plea and sentencing agreement with Ndodana Tshuma.

The UK national is wanted in Britain in connection with the alleged murders of his wife and two daughters.

In South Africa, however, Tshuma faces charges of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition, as well as contravening the Immigration Act.

READ | Murder accused Ndodana Tshuma pleads guilty

Police allege Tshuma was found in possession of a firearm and ammunition that he bought in South Africa after fleeing the UK.

He has pleaded guilty to the South African charges.

Extradition proceedings will determine whether Tshuma will be handed over to UK authorities to face the murder allegations.

World.title: Breakthrough in DJ Warras murder case
World.content:
DURBAN - Police have made a breakthrough in the murder investigation of popular media personality DJ Warras.

KwaZulu-Natal police have arrested a 40-year-old woman allegedly linked to the killing of Warrick Stock, who was murdered in Gauteng in December 2025.

Last month, police released a photograph of the woman and appealed to the public for information to help locate her.

Police allege she assisted one of the co-accused in identifying and locating the media personality before his death.

READ | Police appeal for help to locate woman wanted for murder

Investigators received information that the suspect was hiding in Msinga, KwaZulu-Natal.

She was arrested at a homestead on Wednesday afternoon.

The woman is expected to be handed over to Gauteng police, where she will face further investigation in connection with the murder.

World.title: Matlala trial resumes after courtroom chaos
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The trial-within-a-trial in the attempted murder case against Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala and his co-accused is set to continue on Thursday.

At the centre of the proceedings is a trial within a trial, a legal process that will determine whether certain evidence can be admitted.

The defence turned up the pressure on Tuesday when it submitted details showing the movements of police vehicles during the arrest of alleged hitman Musa Kekana.

This forced the State to request a postponement to review the document.

But the tension soon spilled over in the courtroom.

Chaos erupted in the dock after police allegedly refused to allow the accused to consult with their lawyers.

The State is considering whether to call more witnesses or close its case in the trial within a trial.

World.title: Trump promises Americans $5,000 if Republicans win Congress
World.content:
DALLAS - President Donald Trump on Wednesday promised $5,000 to every adult American if Republicans retain control of Congress in November, coupling the extraordinary claim with a plea for his supporters to "pretend" he was on the ballot.

"If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000. It will be called the Trump dividend," he told the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, as the party struggles in polls against the Democrats.

The president did not say where the money would come from -- with the theoretical bill likely topping $1 trillion -- citing only that "our country is making so much money."

Doubling down on his bet that he can help Republicans to defy opinion polls and retain both houses of Congress on November 3, Trump said "I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot."

"I'm on the ballot, I'm on the ballot -- just one more time," he told the crowd.

Opinion polls overwhelmingly show that Trump's approval ratings are in the low 30s, as voters become increasingly angry about high prices and the war he launched against Iran.

Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats to win the House 230-205 and the Senate to finish 51-49 in their favour in November.

World.title: As oceans warm, Florida scientists hunt for heat-resistant coral
World.content:
MIAMI - Off Florida's coast, a team of scientists and trained volunteers in scuba gear descends to the ocean floor and begins planting young coral onto a reef and examining how others are faring in the increasingly warm waters.

It is part of a long-running "Rescue a Reef" program run by the University of Miami that aims to advance conservation efforts and raise public awareness.

Part of that work involves researching which coral species are able to better withstand rapidly warming oceans as a result of human-caused climate change.

"Certain species may be more resilient, where they're able to better survive and recover from thermal stress events," program manager Devon Ledbetter explained to AFP during a recent dive to Rainbow Reef about three miles offshore from Key Biscayne.

World.title: Cyberattack ruled out in UK air traffic glitch that hit hundreds of flights
World.content:
LONDON - UK air travellers faced more misery on Wednesday with nearly 400 flights scrapped across the country, as Britain's air traffic control service scrambled to recover from a technical glitch which it ruled out as a cyberattack.

After 1,746 flights were cancelled on Tuesday following the outage, another 399 were axed Wednesday -- the majority to and from London Heathrow, one of Europe's busiest airports -- according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

More than 330,000 passengers were affected over the two days of disruption, with 155,000 seeing their flights cancelled while around 180,000 experienced delays, industry body Airlines UK said.

"We ended up sitting on our plane for just over five hours," Matt Ernster, 28, who was returning to Boston via Heathrow from his honeymoon in Paris on Tuesday, told AFP.

When they were finally allowed to disembark from the plane, "it turned into a gigantic, chaotic scene", Ernster said. The baggage collection "felt like an apocalyptic situation", and there were no hotels available in a two-hour radius.

"It was the worst travel experience I've ever had."

The head of the National Air Traffic Services (NATS), Martin Rolfe, said "we have at this point ruled out cyber" activity as a cause.

World.title: Strong second-half show brings Sundowns win and six-point lead
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A powerful second-half performance gave Mamelodi Sundowns a 3-0 victory over lowly Siwelele on Wednesday and a six-point lead in the South African Premiership.

Sundowns have 19 points from seven matches. Second-placed Orlando Pirates, the defending champions, have 13 with two games in hand.

Kutlwano Letlhaku broke the deadlock after 58 minutes in Pretoria, then substitutes Siyanda Ndlovu and Tashreeq Matthews netted.

Siwelele, who fired coach Lehlohonolo Seema on Sunday after failing to win in their first five matches of the season, defied Sundowns in the opening half through a well-organised defence.

Behind the defenders, goalkeeper Wandile Mthombeni made a string of superb saves in his Premiership debut.

He was finally beaten when a Teboho Mokoena shot rebounded off the crossbar and Letlhaku reacted quickest to prod the ball into the net for his first goal of the league campaign.

Ndlovu pounced on a weak back-pass to score after 79 minutes and Matthews burst forward and chipped the ball over Mthombeni in the second minute of added time.

"Our plan was to drain the energy out of Siwelele and we succeeded. They tired in the second half and we took advantage," said Sundowns' Portuguese coach Miguel Cardoso.
