World.title: Lusangazi civic leaders sworn-in, urged to improve service delivery
World.content:
The newly elected Lusangazi civic leaders led by the Chairperson, Geoffrey Daka, have officially assumed office after taking the Oath of Office.

The swearing-in ceremony was held at Lusangazi Civic Centre and was presided over by Resident Magistrate Misozi Banda, who administered the oath to the newly elected local government leaders.

His Royal Highness Chief Sandwe was also in attendance.

The immediate past Council Chairperson, Blackson Tembo, congratulated the newly elected Chairperson and councillors, urging them to work as a united team in addressing the developmental challenges in the district.

Mr Tembo encouraged the new Council leadership to build on the achievements of the previous administration, work closely with Council Management and staff, and remain committed to improving service delivery.

He further urged the councillors to put the interests of the people above political and personal differences.

Meanwhile, newly sworn-in Council Chairperson Geoffrey Daka described his election as a profound responsibility entrusted to him by the people of Lusangazi.

He thanked the electorate for their confidence and extended a hand of friendship to residents who may not have supported him and other councillors during the elections.

He said the conclusion of the August 13, 2026 General Election should mark the beginning of a new era of cooperation and development.

“We are now one Council, one community, and one Lusangazi,” Mr Daka said.

He pledged to lead the Council based on good governance, transparency, accountability, inclusiveness and dedicated service.

He also said the new administration would prioritise improved service delivery, including roads, water supply, sanitation, health and education infrastructure, markets, waste management and community facilities.

Mr Daka also said the Council would support initiatives aimed at creating opportunities for young people, women, farmers, entrepreneurs and vulnerable groups.

And Mr Daka called on Council Management and staff to serve residents with professionalism, integrity and dedication, while urging residents to participate actively in development programmes, protect public infrastructure and maintain clean communities.

He further pledged to strengthen collaboration between the Council and traditional leaders in promoting peace, unity, cultural values and community development.

Council Secretary Sekani Tembo described the swearing-in ceremony as a significant milestone in the democratic journey of Lusangazi District.

Mr Tembo urged the councillors to recognise their election as a responsibility to serve as voices of their respective communities.

He called for unity across political parties, wards, traditional leadership structures and communities, saying the aspirations of residents could only be realised through collective effort.

The ceremony was attended by Council Management and staff, Government representatives, political and community leaders, members of the clergy, traditional leaders, the media among other invited guests.

World.title: Lawmaker pledges to work with education authorities
World.content:
Nkombwa Constituency’s newly elected area Member of Parliament, Jairo Simbeye, has pledged to work closely with education authorities in Isoka District.

Mr Simbeye committed to working with teachers, parents, and other stakeholders to ensure that government policies being implemented in the education sector yield the intended results.

Mr Simbeye stated that the government has invested significant resources in the education sector through programmes such as free education, school feeding initiatives, health rooms, and the recruitment of teachers.

Speaking in an interview with the media, Mr Simbeye called for concerted efforts if Nkombwa Constituency is to record impressive school results.

He reaffirmed his commitment to ensure that education guidelines and policies are adhered to and that issues which could compromise the quality of education are addressed promptly.

“Every policy should be adhered to, knowing that our President has committed himself to ensuring that every child gets the education they deserve,” Mr Simbeye said.

Mr Simbeye said his office will work with the District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) to monitor the distribution of teachers in the constituency and ensure a balanced pupil-teacher ratio.

He has also urged teachers deployed to remote parts of the constituency to willingly serve the communities where they have been posted.

Mr Simbeye commended teachers who have continued serving in remote areas, saying their contribution towards educating children is highly appreciated.

He further urged parents, teachers and leaders at all levels to work together to ensure that learners receive the care and support required for them to attain quality education.

Mr Simbeye said the government has committed substantial resources towards educating children and all stakeholders should therefore play their part in ensuring that the investment yields positive results.

He said his office will remain open to concerns affecting teachers and learners that require intervention for the smooth running of schools in the constituency.

World.title: Milenge Boarding Secondary School devises plans to improve academic performance
World.content:
Milenge Boarding Secondary School has introduced targeted learning strategies aimed at raising its academic performance from 72 percent recorded last year to more than 90 percent in 2026.

Milenge Boarding Secondary School Headteacher, Bonwell Chama stated that the institution has devised performance enhancement interventions that include starting lessons on the first day of the term, teacher preparation and additional support for learners experiencing academic difficulties.

“First day we go straight into teaching so that we don’t miss an hour. And that in itself is helping the school to get the results,” Mr Chama said.

He said the school also conducts remedial lessons for learners who are struggling academically, with teachers providing additional support based on their educational needs.

Mr Chama explained that Grade 12 learners will have additional lessons from 15:00 hours, with the learners grouped according to their performance to address their specific academic needs.

“We want to concentrate and see what kind of material we should give to those who are at 0 to 30, and what kind of material we should also give to those who are at 30 to 45 and those scoring 45 and above,” he said.

Mr Chama said the targeted approach would help prevent slower learners from falling behind while ensuring that high-performing learners receive appropriate academic support.

He expressed confidence that the interventions would enable the school to achieve its target of more than 90 percent this year.

Mr Chama cited former learner, Doris Mona, who emerged as the best-performing girl-pupil among CAMFED-sponsored learners in last year’s mock examinations and later scored six points at Grade 12, as evidence that the school can produce outstanding results despite being located in a rural district.

World.title: Plans underway to upgrade Lundazi District Hospital to a general hospital
World.content:
Government says plans are underway to upgrade Lundazi District Hospital to a General Hospital, a move expected to bring specialised healthcare services closer to communities in Lundazi and the surrounding districts of Chama, Chasefu and Lumezi.

Eastern Province Deputy Permanent Secretary Lewis Mwape says the upgrade will help reduce costly referrals and ease the burden of long‑distance travel for patients seeking specialised medical treatment.

Dr Mwape noted that the hospital is strategically positioned to serve as a major referral facility once upgraded.

He was speaking during a recent visit to Lundazi District Hospital, where he was accompanied by Eastern Province Provincial Health Director Mathews Ng’ambi.

“We need another general hospital here because we do not have one in the northern circuit, so that our people can have access to specialised treatment,” he said.

Dr Mwape also commended the hospital management for making significant improvements to the facility’s infrastructure, including the installation of an oxygen plant and a modern incinerator.

He said the developments demonstrate the hospital’s readiness to support the planned upgrade and provide improved healthcare services to the growing population.

Meanwhile, Dr Ng’ambi said the hospital currently attends to more than 200 patients daily, indicating an increasing demand for healthcare services in the district and surrounding areas.

He added that transforming the facility into a General Hospital would strengthen the province’s healthcare referral system by bringing specialised medical services closer to communities.

Dr Ng’ambi said this will be achieved by deploying specialised personnel even before addressing infrastructure needs.

World.title: Gambia: Gambian President Declares Power Emergency Amid Protests
World.content:
President Adama Barrow has declared the country's prolonged electricity crisis a national emergency and promised to increase power generation as protests over rolling blackouts intensify ahead of the December presidential election.

Barrow urged citizens to remain calm over prolonged power cuts. He said that the country is not alone in facing an electricity crisis that has affected several parts of West Africa.

Demonstrators in Banjul and surrounding areas burned tyres, erected roadblocks and called for Barrow to resign after some communities experienced outages lasting up to 48 hours during the hot season.

Police used tear gas to disperse protesters gathering near Barrow's residence and the headquarters of the National Water and Electricity Corporation.

Barrow has promised a 24-megawatt generation machine by the end of October. He announced plans for a further 50-megawatt solar power plant. The electricity provider has blamed soaring temperatures, climate change and wider geopolitical disruptions for the crisis.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 9, 2026
World.content:
press review

Kenya Launches Crackdown on Foreign Informal Traders

Kenyan officials have started to crack down on foreign nationals running small businesses in the informal economy. This comes after President William Ruto backed measures reserving activities such as hawking and petty retail primarily for Kenyan citizens. Ruto said that foreign investors should focus on bringing capital, creating jobs and supporting local production rather than competing with citizens in businesses requiring little capital. Kenyans have reacted with mixed feelings to the move, with some welcoming it as a way of protecting jobs amid high unemployment. Others fear it could fuel xenophobia and discourage foreign investment. Political economist Sheila Owigo Olang questioned whether removing foreign traders would create more opportunities for Kenyans, describing the policy as potentially populist ahead of elections. The government has insisted that foreign nationals who comply with immigration, work permit and licensing requirements remain legally protected. Questions remain over who will ultimately be affected and how the policy will be enforced.

Gambia Declares Power Crisis a National Emergency



Gambian President Adama Barrow has declared the country's prolonged electricity crisis a national emergency and promised to increase power generation as protests over rolling blackouts intensify ahead of the December presidential election. Demonstrators in Banjul and surrounding areas burned tyres, erected roadblocks and called for Barrow to resign after some communities experienced outages lasting up to 48 hours during the hot season. Police used tear gas to disperse protesters gathering near Barrow's residence and the headquarters of the National Water and Electricity Corporation. Barrow has promised a 24-megawatt generation machine by the end of October. He announced plans for a further 50-megawatt solar power plant. The electricity provider has blamed soaring temperatures, climate change and wider geopolitical disruptions for the crisis.

Funding Cuts Push Sudan's Health System to the Brink

Sudan's already fragile health system is nearing collapse as international funding cuts force healthcare facilities to close amid the country's devastating civil war, said Médecins Sans Frontières. More than 33 million people now require medical assistance following the conflict between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces. The loss of USAID funding and reductions in European aid have left many humanitarian organisations unable to sustain their operations. MSF reported a sharp increase in patient admissions at facilities it supports and said the closure of dozens of healthcare centres is placing enormous pressure on the hospitals that remain open. In some displacement camps, maternity and surgical services have shut down, forcing patients to travel long distances for treatment. The crisis is compounded by attacks on healthcare facilities, widespread hunger and continuing violence, prompting MSF to urge world leaders gathering at the UN General Assembly to increase support.

WFP Says Food Aid Key to Fighting DR Congo Ebola Outbreak

The World Food Programme has warned that food assistance must form a central part of the response to the rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, where conflict, displacement and severe hunger are making it harder to contain the disease. The outbreak, declared in May and caused by the rare Bundibugyo species, has become the fastest on record, with more than 5,500 cases and 2,642 deaths reported in its first 100 days. WFP said that people struggling to feed their families cannot easily comply with the health measures needed to prevent transmission, particularly in remote areas far from treatment centres. More than 500,000 people in the affected Ituri province are facing severe food insecurity, while poor infrastructure and ongoing conflict complicate efforts to deliver assistance. The WFP is calling for more international funding to expand both food assistance and Ebola treatment services, noting that adequate nutrition in addition to medical treatment can greatly increase a patient's chances of survival.

Nurses' Strike Deepens Pressure on Kenya's Health System

Kenya's prolonged nurses' strike is placing increasing pressure on the country's public health system, with essential services disrupted as nurses demand the implementation of long-standing labour agreements. Hundreds of nurses have demonstrated in Nairobi, calling on the national and county governments to address salary arrears, allowances, staffing shortages, promotions and career progression. At the heart of the dispute is the 2017 Collective Bargaining Agreement, which the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives says remains largely unimplemented despite provisions for nursing service allowances and improved working conditions. The union has said negotiations alone are no longer sufficient and insists that signed agreements must be honoured before members return to work. The government and county authorities continue engaging with the union, including on the permanent employment of UHC workers. Nurses argue that years of unfulfilled promises and poor working conditions have damaged morale and undermined their ability to provide safe and effective patient care.

Zimbabwean Vendors Vow to Defy Harare Street Clearance Order



Zimbabwean authorities have intensified efforts to remove illegal vendors from Harare's Central Business District. They declared that uncontrolled street trading is no longer acceptable and ordered traders to use designated markets and vending bays. Local Government Minister Daniel Garwe said illegal vending was contributing to congestion, blocked pavements, litter, poor sanitation and public health risks, including the potential spread of water-borne diseases such as cholera. The government insists that the crackdown is not a war against informal traders. It argued that significant investment has already been made in designated vending infrastructure that remains underused. The move has, however, been met with strong resistance from vendors, who say informal trading is their only means of survival in an economy with limited formal employment opportunities. The order is a seven-day ultimatum to vacate the streets, and vendors have vowed to resist. Traders' representatives have urged the government to implement reforms guided by the National Informal Economy Formalization Strategy of Zimbabwe, rather than just chasing traders off the streets.

World.title: South Africa: Fake Toys Raise Safety and Job Concerns - South African News Briefs - September 9, 2026
World.content:
press review

Fake Toys Raise Safety and Job Concerns

Concerns are mounting over counterfeit toys flooding the South African market, reports EWN. Fake products are now estimated to account for 25% of sales. Farrel Frank, managing director of the South African Toys and Games Association, warned that counterfeit toys can pose serious health and safety risks and cost jobs. He said the growth of online sales platforms has contributed to the problem. Some major platforms are working with the industry to remove suspicious listings. Consumers are also being urged to remain vigilant after a recent complaint involving a toy with a strong chemical smell that allegedly caused burning and tingling when it touched a consumer’s face.

More Witnesses to Testify in Anele Tembe Inquest

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

More witnesses are set to testify in the inquest into the death of Anele Tembe, who fell from the 10th floor of a Cape Town hotel in April 2021, reports SABC News. Lawyers representing Tembe's family questioned witnesses about whether her fiancé, the late rapper Kiernan "AKA" Forbes, had asked for her family to be informed of her death. Two police officers told the court they had no knowledge of whether the family had been contacted. One officer said Forbes did not ask police to contact them. The inquest has also heard from a nearby resident who reported hearing an argument between a man and a woman shortly before Tembe’s death.

Tshuma Extradition Hinges on Plea Deal

Extradition proceedings against UK fugitive Ndodana Tshuma could depend on whether the Johannesburg Magistrates Court accepts a plea agreement between him and the State, reports EWN. Tshuma, who is accused of murdering his wife and two young daughters in the UK before fleeing to South Africa, pleaded guilty to firearm and immigration-related charges following his arrest in Johannesburg. Details of the proposed plea deal and sentence have not been disclosed. The magistrate must still decide whether the agreement is just and appropriate. A custodial sentence could further complicate his extradition to the UK, where he is expected to face the murder allegations.

World.title: Drake Maye's terrible decision gifts Seahawks opening night win as Patriots left stunned to start NFL season
World.content:
The New England Patriots went into Lumen Field on Wednesday night and watched as the Seattle Seahawks raised a Super Bowl victory banner commemorating a championship won at their expense.

As a result, Drake Maye, an MVP frontrunner last season who led the Patriots to Super Bowl LX, was hoping for some revenge along with his teammates to start the new year on the right foot.

Instead, it was Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe who got his feet down in the end zone on the final play of Maye’s night, notching Seattle’s third interception of the Patriots quarterback and icing a 13-10 victory in a thrilling finish in the Pacific Northwest.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Maye, the Patriots’ offense, had converted on fourth-and-9 to put themselves in field goal range with less than a minute to play in the NFL’s season opener, and he was hoping this fourth-quarter drive ended with some points, because the other two he had in the quarter ended with interceptions – ones that got Drew Lock and the Seahawks’ offense back in the game.

Yes, it was Lock who played most of the game due to Sam Darnold suffering a hip injury just five snaps into the new season. It was looking bleak for a usually raucous "12’s" fan base in the seats, as a dull murmur fell over Lumen Field when Lock took to the field.

But ultimately, his second-half performance turned the tide, making the most of Maye’s mistakes.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Maye’s biggest came on third-and-5 from Seattle’s 16-yard line, where he scrambled out to his right, and instead of going out of bounds or throwing the ball away, he tried to give Mack Hollins a jump ball in the end zone.

Jobe, though, made an incredible acrobatic catch, contorting his body so both his feet remained in bounds and sealed victory. The "12’s" were in rapture when they saw their stellar defense once again save the day, while the Patriots’ sideline couldn’t believe what just happened.

Maye’s opening night was a roller-coaster. He finished 23-of-33 through the air for 178 yards with one touchdown pass to rookie tight end Eli Raridon – the first of the NFL season – while his three interceptions will be a pain point in team meetings later this week after they watch the tape.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks were thankful for the decision of Maye to not throw it away, as they were at least looking at overtime football with a chip-shot field goal in play before that final interception.

They must also be thankful that Lock was ready to go once Darnold was ruled out the rest of the way. He was highly efficient, as the backup quarterback went 16-of-22 for 187 yards with one touchdown and no turnovers.

And it also helps when the reigning Offensive Player of the Year is locked in to help his backup quarterback find some easy pitch-and-catch scenarios. Jaxon Smith-Njigba finished the night with eight catches for 122 yards, including the game-changing 45-yard catch-and-run touchdown on a clever fourth-and-1 call by the Seahawks to pass instead of run.

Smith-Njigba was wide open and all Lock had to do was hit him in the numbers. From there, the Ohio State product used his blazing speed to get past multiple Patriots defenders and tie the game following the Jason Myers extra point.

That touchdown came after Maye’s first interception, which was hauled in by Nehemiah Pritchett on a deep ball intended for new Patriots receiver Romeo Doubs. No, it wasn’t A.J. Brown, the top offseason acquisition by New England, who was targeted after he suffered an ankle injury that knocked him out of the game like Darnold.

PATRIOTS' AJ BROWN EXITS NFL SEASON OPENER AGAINST SEAHAWKS, RULED OUT WITH ANKLE INJURY

With a tie game, Maye was trying to get the Patriots the lead back, but veteran safety Julian Love had other things in mind. This time, it was a target for Pop Douglas, but Love read Maye the entire way, jumping the route and securing a great field position for Lock and company to work with.

Myers knocked through a 26-yard field goal to end the ensuing drive, and it was the game-winning points for Seattle, who now start the season off 1-0 and make their Super Bowl-winning celebration that much sweeter.

However, all eyes will be on what happens with Darnold later this week, considering their Super Bowl hopes for this season ride on their franchise quarterback being healthy. Darnold landed awkwardly on his knee when Dre’Mont Jones sacked him in the first quarter, and he was noticeably limping to the sideline.

After a trip to the dreaded blue medical tent, Darnold limped his way to the locker room where he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald will learn of his quarterback’s diagnosis soon, and like the rest of the franchise, hope it’s nothing too severe.

The same goes for Brown, whom the Patriots traded for from the Philadelphia Eagles before the start of training camp. He finished his debut with three catches for 26 yards before leaving the game.

World.title: Trump makes stunning first-of-its-kind cash promise in bid to rally GOP voters at Dallas midterm convention
World.content:

DALLAS — President Donald Trump delivered the keynote speech on day one of the GOP's inaugural midterm convention, alternating between touting his successes in office and rallying thousands of supporters for Republican candidates ahead of November's general election before making a promise to American voters.

In a stunning move, Trump made a promise unheard of in the history of American politics — offering a cash prize should Republicans keep control of Congress.

"I can make this promise to you, and here is my promise," he said. "If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our economic — tremendous economic success like in history, we've never had anything like what's happening. but because of our tremendous strength and success economically — I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000. Very much like a successful company will do a cash distribution to its shareholders."

TRUMP'S UNUSUAL ROLE AT MIDTERM CONVENTION REVEALED AS SCHEDULE GOES PUBLIC

"It will be called the 'Trump dividend,'" he added.

Trump opened the speech by grading his own performance since taking office for a second time in January 2025, saying he's "doing a great job." He quickly shifted to addressing the historical challenge that incumbent parties rarely retain control of Congress in midterm elections.

JOHNSON DOWNPLAYS GOP'S MIDTERM WOES AS DEMOCRATS EYE HOUSE TAKEOVER: 'I AM VERY BULLISH'

"But I say, why is it that no matter how well you're doing, we see not a president — Democrat or Republican — almost never wins the midterms?' said Trump. "We've got to change that because we have something going that's so good we can't let that string be broken. So I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot. I'm on the ballot, just one more time."

During his effort to rally GOP voters to help Republicans hang onto the House and Senate, Trump made sure to give credit to Republicans on Capitol Hill for their work in passing his agenda.

MILLIONS TAP TRUMP TAX CUTS THIS FILING SEASON AS REFUNDS TOP $3,400

"Our Republican Congress puts thousands of dollars into the pockets of working families with the largest tax cuts in the history of our country," he said. "So we had the largest in history. We gave you no tax on tips, no tax on overtime and no tax on Social Security for our great seniors."

He said his administration's efforts on critical issues will be crushed if the GOP loses majorities in either or both chambers of Congress.

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

"Because if we lose, you're going to lose your border," he said. "You're going to lose your tax cuts. You're going to lose your safety and security. You're going to lose your wealth."

Fox News polling shows Trump is underwater with voters on the economy, cost of living and inflation. Sixty-five percent of voters disapprove of his handling of the economy. The president also defended the military conflict in Iran, saying he has received criticism over rising gas prices tied to the conflict but arguing that "I'm right," because Iran was one month away from securing a nuclear weapon. Inflation has risen from 2.4% to 3.4% since the war began in February, while gas prices have also increased.

RECORD GAS PRICES SQUEEZE AMERICANS AS SUMMER TRAVEL SEASON ENDS, MIDTERMS LOOM AND IRAN WAR WAGES ON

Republicans who spoke to Fox News Digital on day one of the convention weren't concerned with Trump's economic policies.

"I believe that Trump is doing the right thing," one RNC attendee told Fox News Digital. "The tariffs are bringing a lot of money back, you know, correcting the national debt. And that's gonna improve everything across the board."

"I feel like as soon as we bring this conflict in Iran to a close, we'll start seeing the full effects of President Trump and the greatness that he's done as far as the economy, the great thing of tariffs, and some of the products of the Trump economy in the golden age," said Jacquez Jones of Texas.

Later, Trump shifted his sights to Texas' high profile U.S. Senate race between Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democrat state Rep. James Talarico.

"We have to elect Ken Paxton," he said, segueing into border security, a top issue under both Trump administrations. "Together, we're going to continue to have — we have the strongest borders now in the history of our country."

'FAKE' MODERATE TALARICO'S TEXAS SURGE TESTS PAXTON IN FIGHT TO HOLD CRUCIAL GOP SENATE SEAT

"We have the lowest level of illegal immigration ever recorded in our country," he said, adding that zero illegal immigrants have entered the country through Texas in 16 months.

"And therefore zero have been admitted into Texas where they used to be running around, running rampant, killing people, destroying many houses and farms, and ruining property values and creating havoc all over the state of Texas," he said.

During the speech, he also took aim at Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and former Gov. Roy Cooper in North Carolina.

LONGTIME GOP AIDE DEFECTS TO DEM RISING STAR AS TEXAS SENATE BATTLE FOR CORNYN'S SEAT HEATS UP

He also touted what he described as foreign policy wins. After the arrest of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, Trump boasted about "the biggest oil deal" ever, which he said might be "the biggest deal in the history of our country."

"65 billion barrels are ours," Trump said. "And you know what they say it is lifetime 500 years."

Later, Trump transitioned to slamming the GOP's far-left opponents.

"In this election, the Democrats have nominated the most extreme and dangerous group of candidates for the House and Senate ever to seek office," he said. "These people are radical left communists. Many of them. Not all of them, but many of them in state after state. The Democrat establishment has been overthrown and replaced by crazed lunatics and radicals. They call themselves Democrat socialists. But actually they're communists. They're not socialists. They're long beyond socialists."

He noted the DSA has proposed abolishing prisons, ICE, Border Patrol, the U.S. Senate and the presidency.

That message was one Alex Stone of Kansas City, Missouri, hoped for earlier in the day.

"Tell the truth about who they are, what they believe and what they plan on doing," he told Fox News Digital when asked what Trump's message to Americans should be. "Democratic Socialists of America with El-Sayed in Michigan, in particular, these people want to destroy people like myself. They want to destory people like President Trump and many of the other people here. If they get into power, what is going to happen to us?"

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

World.title: Researcher who departed AI role over fears of racing into extinction says people are 'begging' for regulation
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Anthropic researcher who is leaving the company over fears the technology is gambling with human life told Fox News there is hope that we can avoid the chance it could destroy humankind within the next decade.

Speaking exclusively Wednesday on "Special Report," Jacob Coxon, 27, said regulation is key.

He posted his resignation Tuesday on X, writing that companies are not acting responsibly and that the race toward self-improving superintelligence is "gambling with our lives."

Coxon, who said he spent the past three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, noted that it's not a completely hopeless scenario.

ANTHROPIC RESEARCHER SAYS AI HAS OVER 10% CHANCE TO 'KILL ALL HUMANS' WITHIN NEXT DECADE

He told Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier the problem is "eminently solvable."

Evan Hubinger, alignment science lead at Anthropic, expressed his agreement with Coxon's X post.

"Jacob is correct here — we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!" he wrote on X. "I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to."

SANDERS PUSHES 'DEATH PENALTY' FOR CRUCIAL US INDUSTRY THAT COULD GIVE ADVANTAGE TO FOREIGN ADVERSARIES

"To be clear, as we say in our latest Risk Report, I think the risk from present models is low," Hubinger added. "What I am worried about is superintelligence arising from recursive self-improvement, as we have said is happening faster than we thought."

Coxon said he agrees with Hubinger that right now, the threat is "minimal" of artificial intelligence's actual takeover.

"But recursive self-improvement — this AIs making themselves smarter — could happen as soon as next year," he added. "Some people even say six months. So this attitude is shared across the industry, where people essentially are aware that the work they are currently doing, if we don't slow down, could lead to AI takeover by the end of the decade."

He believes there is "definitely" something the country can do to change the dynamic of the "greater than 10% chance" that AI kills all humans.

"I think the problem is not unsolvable, it's not like we think this is some impossible thing — it's just, we're racing so fast, we haven't got time to solve it correctly, we're not being careful, and everyone wants to be careful," Coxon said. "I think it's just — people are begging for regulation. I think it's just a matter of — international — somebody stepping in and being able to ensure that we don't race ourselves into extinction. The problem is eminently solvable."

The technology is being used on the international stage as a "superweapon" in an arms race, Coxon said, calling for the global community to provide oversight.

"This is possibly the most dangerous technology that humanity has ever created," he continued. "It's basically out of science fiction. I think we have no other choice but to cooperate internationally because an arms race would be disastrous in a way that no other human activity has been in the past."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Coxon mentioned that a number of technology leaders have publicly expressed the need for a slow-down agreement, but people are not yet taking them seriously.

"It's not just a marketing stunt," he said. "These people are deadly serious that they think their industry needs to be regulated as soon as possible."

As for AI's benefits, Coxon said we are "on the doorstep of tremendous discoveries," but we're running in too quickly. He emphasized the need for moderation.

Baier asked Coxon if the issue could be figured out.

"I think definitely. I think if we actually try instead of submitting to the inevitability of a doomed race or a hubristic gamble, then we can solve it," he said. "The problem is not unsolvable."

Fox News Digital reached out to Anthropic for comment.

World.title: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold leaves game with a hip injury
World.content:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold’s 2026 season debut lasted just one drive before a hip injury knocked out the Super Bowl champion.

Darnold injured his right hip, and there is no timetable for his return, the team announced.

Facing the New England Patriots in the NFL’s season-opening primetime game — a rematch of February’s Super Bowl — Darnold was playing only his fifth snap when he was sacked on the opening drive and hobbled off the field, though he did not require assistance to reach the sideline.

After he was evaluated in a privacy tent on Seattle’s sideline at Lumen Field, he underwent X-rays in the locker room and was listed as questionable, and he was later ruled out for the game.

ESPN reported that a CT scan on Darnold’s hip returned “inconclusive” and that he was scheduled for an MRI on Thursday. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that the team had received “great news back” from Darnold’s scan, suggesting that a fracture had been ruled out.

Darnold was replaced by backup quarterback Drew Lock, and Seattle’s offense continued to sputter during the first half. Seattle came back to score 13 unanswered points and win the game 13-10. Lock finished with 187 yards and a touchdown while completing 16 of his 22 passes.

“I should have given him the game ball,” Macdonald said postgame. “We love Drew. Guys love him. He’s just a Seahawk through and through, man, and it’s like OK, Drew’s in the game, your heart goes out to Sam, we’re praying it’s minor obviously. ... You also want to feel excited for that player and we had a lot of confidence in Drew.”

Lock said his focus after he stepped in for Darnold was to “take care of the football. I know what kind of defense we have, the kind of playmakers we have on this side of the ball.”

Seattle needed three interceptions of New England’s Drake Maye and eight catches for 122 yards by star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba to pull off its comeback victory.

Darnold is one of six active quarterbacks with Super Bowl wins, and he is the only quarterback ever to win a title for his fifth team or later. Last season, he joined Tom Brady (2003-04) as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to win 14 games as a starter in consecutive seasons.
