World.title: Costa Rica Sharks Get Cameras Built by Stanford Students
World.content:
Scientists at the University of Costa Rica have strapped small cameras to nurse sharks in a protected Guanacaste bay, and what the animals are showing them is upending the long-held idea that this species barely moves. The work is happening in Bahía Santa Elena, a bay on the northern Pacific coast inside Santa Rosa National Park, near the Nicaraguan border.

A team from UCR’s Centro de Investigación en Ciencias del Mar y Limnología (CIMAR), has been studying Pacific nurse sharks there for about a decade using underwater listening stations, and is now adding wearable cameras and drones that measure the animals from the air. Mongabay Latam accompanied the team on a field trip and published an account of the work on Monday.

The species itself is a recent addition to science as until about 10 years ago, biologists lumped Pacific and Caribbean nurse sharks together as one animal. In 2015, Latin American researchers showed they were different, splitting off the Pacific version, Ginglymostoma unami, which has a shorter, stockier body, flat teeth and a higher tolerance for cold water than its Caribbean relative. It is listed as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, and much of what was assumed about it was borrowed from studies done in Florida and the Bahamas on the other species.

Mario Espinoza, a researcher and professor at CIMAR, drives roughly six hours from San José to the bay every three or four months to work on the animals. The camera his team is now using was designed by engineering students at Stanford University. An earlier version had to be drilled into the shark’s dorsal fin; the current design uses a small chest harness instead, and costs eight to 10 times less to build than comparable commercial devices. The July trip was the first time the UCR team fitted one without the engineers on hand.

The cameras record video, but they also carry sensors that log water temperature, depth and swimming speed. They stay on the animal for an hour or two, then release automatically and float to the surface, where a radio transmitter lets the team find them. “The idea of this project with cameras is to have the sharks as mobile monitoring platforms,” Espinoza said. “They’re going to be our eyes underwater.”

The routine on the water is quick. Researchers drop a bottom line with 19 hooks near a mangrove where the sharks are known to gather. On the July trip they expected two animals and had four — three females and a male — within an hour. Each shark stays in the water alongside the boat while the team inserts or checks a small identification chip, measures it and draws blood. Turning a shark belly-up puts it into a temporary, trance-like state called tonic immobility that researchers use as a natural sedative.

The movement data is where the picture has changed most. A first analysis of acoustic tracking from 2018 to 2022 showed Pacific nurse sharks spend more than 40% of their time inside the bay, with females staying far longer than males. Some individuals almost never leave; others come and go, or disappear for years and return.

The peer-reviewed version of that work, published in Marine and Freshwater Research in 2024, documented a 176-centimeter male that covered more than 390 kilometers in 46 days along the North Pacific coast — a round trip Espinoza described as more than 400 kilometers. The team has also filmed groups of 40 to 50 animals in the mangroves, which contradicts the assumption that the species is solitary and sluggish.

The bay works as a natural laboratory for a second reason. Trade winds between December and May pull cold, nutrient-rich water up from the deep, a seasonal process called upwelling. Espinoza said water that sits at 28 to 29 degrees Celsius (82 to 84 Fahrenheit) in July has been recorded as low as 14 C (57 F) during that window. Because Costa Rica has no fishery targeting the species, researchers can watch how the animals handle those swings without commercial fishing pressure muddying the results — useful for predicting how they will respond to a warming ocean.

The project also leans on two local boat captains, brothers Minor and Steven Lara from the nearby town of Cuajiniquil, who have turned a family adventure-tourism business into a year-round support operation for the science. They recently logged a large lemon shark in the bay, a sign it may serve as a nursery for other threatened species including blacktip and bull sharks. Visitors who snorkel or dive with them get a briefing on what the researchers are looking for, and often come back reporting unusual sightings

World.title: Route 1 at Cambronero Closed for up to Two Months After Bridge Damage
World.content:
If your drive west runs through Cambronero, plan on going another way for a while. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport says the temporary bridge on Route 1 took enough damage in Monday night’s crash that it cannot be repaired in place. It has to come out and a new one has to go in.

Officials estimate the crossing could stay closed for up to two months. Pablo Camacho, vice minister of infrastructure, put the cost of the replacement at close to ₡300 million, roughly $661,000 at the Central Bank reference sell rate. That changes the calculation for anyone traveling between the Central Valley and Puntarenas, the Nicoya Peninsula or Guanacaste. This is no longer a delay you wait out over a long weekend.

You have three ways around it, and the right one depends on what you drive. Route 27, the toll road between San José and Caldera, takes everything, including buses and tractor-trailers. It is the only alternate that heavy vehicles should be on, so expect it to be busier than usual in both directions and budget extra time even outside rush hour.

Route 3 over Monte del Aguacate works for cars, pickups and small trucks. Articulated vehicles should stay off it. The road climbs and descends through tight switchbacks with no room to swing a trailer, and a truck that gets stuck on a curve there closes the whole road for everyone behind it.

Light vehicles have a third option, the cantonal road between Río Jesús and Piedra Blanca. It is narrow and local, so treat it as a way to skip a queue rather than a highway substitute, and do not attempt it in heavy rain without checking conditions first.

The picture only became clear yesterday afternoon as crews pulled the trailer’s container off the structure around 2 p.m., which was the step that had to happen before anyone could assess the damage properly. Earlier that morning, Conavi director Mauricio Sojo had said engineers would draw up an inventory of the parts needing replacement and announce a timeline afterward. By the end of the day the ministry had concluded the modular structure itself was beyond salvaging.

The driver has given his own account of the crash. Luis Miguel Larios, who was hauling the load toward Guatemala, said he lost his brakes roughly 500 meters (about 1,640 feet) before reaching the bridge and considers himself lucky to have survived. His truck was carrying nine reels of paper weighing about 2.5 tons each, roughly 5,500 pounds apiece, and part of that load ended up scattered across the roadway.

Timing makes the repair more awkward than it would otherwise be. The Independence Torch relay passes through this way in the middle of the month, which has added pressure to clear the site and settle on a plan quickly. There is an additional wrinkle as the bridge was done in November 2025 as a temporary fix after a landslide destroyed part of the highway, and it was in the middle of a scheduled week of preventive maintenance when the truck hit it.

A structure meant to hold the line until a permanent solution arrived now needs replacing itself, and the permanent fix for this stretch of Route 1 remains unresolved. Traffic police are stationed at the closure to keep vehicles out while work continues. The ministry has not yet published a firm reopening date, and the two-month figure is an estimate rather than a commitment.

Until it reopens, the safe assumption is that Route 1 through Cambronero is unavailable. Check road conditions before you leave, allow more time than the map suggests, and if you are driving a tractor-trailer, Route 27 is your only option.

World.title: Two Detained With 125 Sea Turtle Eggs During Costa Rica’s Ostional Arribada
World.content:
Two people were detained after allegedly removing 125 olive ridley sea turtle eggs without authorization from the Ostional National Wildlife Refuge in Guanacaste during one of the largest mass nesting events of the year. The arrests occurred Monday morning, September 7, during a surveillance operation at the refuge involving Costa Rican environmental officials and members of the Ostional community.



The two suspects, identified by the surnames González Vázquez and Carrillo Villarreal, were found carrying 125 olive ridley turtle eggs, an amount believed to have come from approximately two nests. Neither person belonged to the Ostional Integral Development Association nor had authorization to collect eggs from the beach.

Both were turned over to prosecutors through Costa Rica’s flagrancy procedure, which is used in cases where suspects are allegedly caught while committing an offense or immediately afterward. The arrests came as thousands of olive ridley turtles were arriving at Ostional for the September arribada, one of the most impressive wildlife events in Costa Rica.

The latest arribada began September 4 and was expected to continue for several nights. September traditionally produces some of the largest gatherings of turtles at Ostional, when large numbers of females emerge from the Pacific within a relatively short period to dig nests and lay their eggs.

The situation surrounding turtle eggs at Ostional can be confusing for visitors because Costa Rica allows a limited and closely controlled legal harvest at this particular refuge. Members of the local community participating in the authorized conservation program are permitted to collect a portion of olive ridley eggs during the early stages of certain arribadas.

The program exists because nesting density at Ostional can become so high that turtles arriving later frequently dig up and destroy nests deposited earlier. Under the management system, a controlled number of those early eggs can be collected and sold legally, while the community participates in protecting the beach and nesting turtles.

That exception does not mean anyone can collect turtle eggs. The legal harvest is restricted to the authorized community program and is subject to environmental controls, permits and traceability requirements. Removing eggs outside that system remains illegal. Ostional is one of the most important olive ridley nesting sites in the world. During an arribada, tens of thousands of turtles can reach the beach, with exceptionally large events bringing far greater numbers.

The Ostional National Wildlife Refuge protects approximately 468 hectares (1,157 acres) of land and 8,000 hectares (19,768 acres) of marine territory. It includes the beaches of Ostional, Nosara, Pelada and Guiones. The mass nesting also attracts visitors from around Costa Rica and abroad.

During nesting periods, visitors entering the protected beach are required to be accompanied by an accredited local guide. Flash photography, motor vehicles, horseback tours, fires and domestic animals are prohibited in protected sections of the refuge. Officials increase surveillance during the largest arribadas because the concentration of turtles and eggs can also attract unauthorized collectors.

The seizure of the 125 eggs highlights the distinction between Ostional’s internationally known community egg-management program and illegal collection from the nesting beach. The investigation involving the two suspects is now in the hands of prosecutors.

World.title: Costa Rica Tourism Drivers Protest Possible Airport Access for Ride-Hailing Apps
World.content:
Tourism transportation operators plan to demonstrate outside Casa Presidencial tomorrow over a possible change to legislation that could allow Uber-type ride-hailing services to operate at Costa Rica’s airports. The protest is scheduled for 1 p.m. in Zapote. Organizers said participants will gather on foot rather than bring tourism vans or buses, in an effort to avoid creating additional traffic problems for the public.

At the center of the dispute is legislation that would create a legal framework for transportation services offered through digital platforms such as Uber and DiDi. The current version of the bill would keep platform drivers from picking up or dropping off passengers at airports, ports, docks and certain other terminals unless the appropriate authority specifically authorizes the service.

That restriction, however, could change before lawmakers vote on the legislation. It’s been reported that discussions surrounding the bill produced an informal agreement to remove the airport restriction and stressed that the proposed change has not yet been incorporated into the official updated text, meaning airport access for ride-hailing platforms has not been approved.

That distinction is important since for now at least, there is no newly approved rule allowing ride-hailing platforms to freely operate at Juan Santamaría International Airport or Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport in Liberia under this legislation. Tourism transport operators say their concern is not simply competition but they argue that allowing platform drivers to work at airports without facing the same requirements imposed on licensed tourism transportation companies would create an uneven playing field.

Organizers said they have sought meetings with government officials to explain their concerns and want to be heard before lawmakers make any change affecting airport transportation. They maintain that formal tourism transportation companies have spent years operating under government licensing and other regulatory requirements.

The dispute comes as Costa Rica moves closer than it has in years to creating formal rules for app-based transportation. The bill was originally introduced in May 2023. In late July, the Legislative Assembly’s Government and Administration Committee finished considering 282 proposed amendments to the legislation, approving nine of them before sending the updated bill back to the full legislature for further debate.

Among other provisions, the proposal would establish requirements for digital transportation companies, drivers and vehicles. Platforms would have to register in Costa Rica, comply with tax requirements and obtain authorization to operate. Drivers would also face registration, insurance, vehicle inspection and other requirements.

The airport issue has become particularly sensitive within our tourism industry. Earlier this year, tourism organizations objected after the Esencial Costa Rica brand announced a promotional arrangement involving Uber. The initiative was withdrawn following complaints from tourism transportation companies, while the National Tourism Chamber, Canatur, called for greater coordination with established tourism businesses when working with ride-hailing platforms.

For visitors, airport transportation has long included authorized airport taxis, private tourism transfers, rental cars and other prearranged services. Ride-hailing platforms are widely used elsewhere in Costa Rica, making the question of whether they should receive clearly defined access to airport passengers one of the more visible issues in the broader debate over regulating the industry.

Tomorrow’s demonstration is intended to pressure the government before any airport provision changes. For the moment, the most important point for travelers is that nothing has changed yet. The legislation remains under discussion, and the language that would potentially open airports more broadly to ride-hailing platforms has not been formally added to the bill

World.title: US Open Celebrates Hispanic Heritage During 2026 Quarterfinals
World.content:
The US Open is putting Hispanic and Latin American tennis in the spotlight today with its annual Hispanic Heritage celebration at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. The event is part of the tournament’s Be Open program, which uses the Grand Slam stage to recognize communities that have helped shape tennis in the United States and around the world.



The US Open says the annual celebration brings Hispanic and Latin American communities together while honoring pioneers of the sport and players helping carry that legacy forward. This year’s celebration falls during one of the biggest days of the tournament. The men’s and women’s singles quarterfinals began today at Arthur Ashe Stadium, with another full day of quarterfinal play scheduled Wednesday.

The timing puts Hispanic heritage alongside the championship stages of a tournament with a long connection to Spanish-speaking tennis. Latin America has produced some of the US Open’s most memorable champions. Argentina’s Gabriela Sabatini won the women’s singles title in 1990, defeating Steffi Graf in the final. Nearly two decades later, another Argentine, Juan Martín del Potro, produced one of the tournament’s most famous upsets when he defeated Roger Federer in the 2009 men’s final.

Players from across Latin America have continued to make New York an important stop on the tennis calendar. Argentina again supplied one of the strongest Latin American runs at this year’s tournament. Francisco Cerúndolo reached the fourth round after rallying from two sets down to defeat American Taylor Fritz in the third round. His run ended Monday when Belgium’s Alexander Blockx beat him 6-3, 4-6, 7-5, 7-5.

Other South American players in the 2026 men’s draw included Tomás Martín Etcheverry and Mariano Navone of Argentina, Alejandro Tabilo and Marcelo Tomás Barrios Vera of Chile, Ignacio Buse of Peru and several others who came through qualifying or the main draw. Spanish tennis also remains prominent during today’s celebration. Carlos Alcaraz, the 2022 US Open champion, is still competing for another New York title and is scheduled to face American Ben Shelton in the quarterfinals Tuesday night.

The heritage celebration is one part of a broader series of events staged by the US Open during the tournament. The Be Open program has also featured events recognizing Historically Black Colleges and Universities, the LGBTQ+ community and U.S. military members. An Asian American and Pacific Islander heritage celebration is scheduled for Wednesday.

The initiative began in 2020 as a campaign aimed at giving greater visibility to underrepresented communities in tennis. It has since expanded into a year-round message centered on representation, access and the different cultures that make up the sport. That connection is especially visible at the US Open.

Unlike the other Grand Slam tournaments, the event is held in Queens, one of the most culturally diverse parts of New York City. Fans arriving at Flushing Meadows regularly bring flags from Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Spain, Brazil and other countries, turning outside courts into home crowds for players thousands of miles from home.

The tournament has leaned further into that connection in recent years through music, cultural performances and community events around the grounds. During 2026 Fan Week, for example, the Calpulli Mexican Dance Company performed at the National Tennis Center as fans watched qualifying matches and player practices.

Today’s Hispanic Heritage celebration continues that approach, placing the cultural history surrounding the sport alongside the tennis itself as the US Open moves into its championship week.

World.title: Buttonwood Bay construction worker charged with harming woman he says he does not know
World.content:
Buttonwood Bay construction worker charged with harming woman he says he does not know

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 21-year-old Buttonwood Bay resident has been charged with harm after a woman alleged that he injured her along the Philip Goldson Highway.

Marvin Mikael Lopez Leal, a construction worker of 4th Street in the Buttonwood Bay area, appeared before a Senior Magistrate in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, where he was read a single charge of harm.

Police allege that on September 5, 2026, Leal intentionally and unlawfully caused harm to a woman.

During the arraignment, the Senior Magistrate asked about the relationship between Leal and the complainant. Leal told the court that he did not know the woman, while the prosecutor indicated that the case facts did not specify any relationship between them.

There was no objection to bail, and Leal was granted bail in the sum of $1,000.

As part of his bail conditions, he must remain at least 100 feet away from the woman and is prohibited from contacting her directly, indirectly or through a third party.

Leal met bail and is scheduled to return to court on November 9, 2026.

World.title: Tafaree Sanchez remanded over $8,214 armed robbery at Crooked Tree business
World.content:
Tafaree Sanchez remanded over $8,214 armed robbery at Crooked Tree business

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 26-year-old call center agent has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after being charged in connection with an armed robbery at a Chinese businessman’s establishment in Crooked Tree.

Tafaree Rohan Sanchez, a resident of Flamboyant Street and an employee of Transparent BPO, appeared unrepresented before a Senior Magistrate in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, where he was read a single charge of robbery.

Police allege that on September 2, 2026, Sanchez and other persons who have not yet been arrested, while armed with a firearm and using force, robbed businessman Jian Jue Shi of cash and other items valued at a total of $8,214.

The stolen property reportedly included $800 in cash, three bottles of Johnnie Walker Black Label rum, three iPhones and two Toyota Hilux pickup truck keys.

Sanchez pleaded not guilty to the charge.

Due to the nature of the offence, bail was denied at the Magistrate’s Court level and Sanchez was remanded to the Belize Central Prison until November 9, 2026.

During his arraignment, Sanchez asked whether his case could be dealt with expeditiously. The Senior Magistrate explained that disclosure must first be provided before the matter can proceed toward trial.

Sanchez is scheduled to return to court on November 9.

World.title: One dead in major traffic accident near Armenia outside Belmopan
World.content:
One dead in major traffic accident near Armenia outside Belmopan

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A major traffic accident has been reported near Armenia, just outside Belmopan, with one person confirmed dead.

Preliminary information indicates that the crash involved an 18 wheeler reportedly carrying sand and gravel.

Reports from the scene indicate that at least one person became trapped following the collision, with the heavy truck coming to rest on top of another vehicle or person.

The accident happened along the highway near the Palenque area while travelling south from Belmopan.

Emergency responders are at the scene and efforts are reportedly underway to assist those trapped.

Details remain limited at this time, including the identity of the deceased and the total number of people involved.

Motorists travelling through the area should expect delays and exercise extreme caution.

This is a developing story and more information will be shared as it becomes available.

World.title: ‘Always have my knife because yuh neva know’: Belize City man fined $155 after police find 4-inch knife in waistband at 4 a.m.
World.content:
‘Always have my knife because yuh neva know’: Belize City man fined $155 after police find 4-inch knife in waistband at 4 a.m.

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 58-year-old Belize City man was fined $155 after pleading guilty to possession of an article with a blade when police allegedly found him riding a bicycle with a four-inch knife tucked into his waistband in the early morning hours.

Basil Willis, a car washer of Black Orchid Street, appeared unrepresented before a Senior Magistrate, where he pleaded guilty to the charge.

Police say Willis was spotted riding along Mahogany Street at approximately 4:50 a.m. on Friday, September 4, when officers on mobile patrol approached him.

According to the prosecution’s account, an officer noticed Willis move a hand from the bicycle handle toward his waist, where police subsequently found a knife with a four-inch cutting edge.

Police say that after being informed of the offence, Willis told officers: “I always have my knife on me because yuh neva know.”

In court, Willis disputed the officer’s claim that he had reached toward his waist when police approached him, telling the Senior Magistrate, “Dat dah nuh really deh truth.” He nevertheless admitted that he had the knife and said he did not want to waste the court’s time by contesting the matter.

The Magistrate accepted his guilty plea and imposed a fine of $150 plus $5 cost of court. Willis has until October 30, 2026, to pay the $155 or face one month in prison in default.

Under Belize’s Crime Control and Criminal Justice Act, a person may commit an offence by having a bladed or sharply pointed article in a public place between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. The law exempts folding pocket knives with cutting edges not exceeding three inches and also provides a defence where a person can show the item was being carried for work, lawful authority or another good reason.

Willis’ knife was reported to have a four-inch cutting edge.

World.title: Sydney Peyreffitte gets full disclosure in ‘Big Tom’ murder case; PI set for November 13
World.content:
Sydney Peyreffitte gets full disclosure in ‘Big Tom’ murder case; PI set for November 13

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Sydney Peyreffitte, the tour guide and businessman charged with the murder of Kenneth “Big Tom” Flowers, has finally received full disclosure in the case, clearing the way for his Preliminary Inquiry to begin in November.

Peyreffitte appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, September 4, where he was provided with a total of 115 pages of disclosure, eight photographs and four DVDs.

His Preliminary Inquiry, which will determine whether there is sufficient evidence for him to stand trial in the High Court, has been set for November 13, 2026.

The development comes after several delays in the disclosure process. In July, the Chief Magistrate declined to set a PI date because prosecutors had not yet provided Peyreffitte with the complete evidence against him. The court was told that a forensic officer previously assigned to complete outstanding material had left the jurisdiction and another officer had been tasked with the work.

Interestingly, during an earlier court appearance in June, Peyreffitte specifically asked whether he would receive a DVD because police had reportedly indicated that the fatal shooting was captured on video. A prosecutor told the court at the time that there was no DVD. Friday’s disclosure, however, included four DVDs, although it is not yet clear what material they contain.

Peyreffitte, who is represented by attorney Bryan Neal but appeared without counsel on Friday, has been on remand since October 8, 2025, when he was arraigned for Flowers’ murder.

Flowers, 47, was shot on October 6, 2025, after multiple shots were fired at the Chevrolet Equinox he was driving in Belize City. He later died at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital. Police subsequently arrested Peyreffitte and charged him with murder.

Peyreffitte remains on remand pending the November 13 Preliminary Inquiry.

World.title: Stevedore charged with stealing pens, glasses, face masks, mosquito repellent and other items worth $280
World.content:
Stevedore charged with stealing pens, glasses, face masks, mosquito repellent and other items worth $280

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 51-year-old Belize City stevedore was arraigned Wednesday on a theft charge after he was accused of stealing an assortment of items valued at $280.

Lynton Gilbert Sutherland, of Fabers Road, appeared unrepresented before a Senior Magistrate in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, where he pleaded not guilty to theft.

Police allege that on September 9, 2026, Sutherland stole 20 ballpoint pens valued at $50, four reading glasses valued at $25, 20 face masks valued at $50, two cans of mosquito repellent valued at $30, two pairs of sunshades valued at $100 and a spanner valued at $25.

The items have a combined value of $280.

There was no objection to bail and Sutherland was granted bail in the sum of $1,500. As part of his bail conditions, he was placed on a curfew requiring him to remain indoors between 8:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

The court was also informed that Sutherland owed $795 in outstanding court debt. He was ordered to make a payment before being granted additional time to settle the balance.

Sutherland paid $85 toward the outstanding amount and was given until October 9, 2026, to pay the remainder.

He is also due back in court on October 9 in relation to the theft charge.

World.title: Jaidyn Brown charged with aiding alleged gun attack on Rio Bravo Crescent; granted $1,500 bail
World.content:
Jaidyn Brown charged with aiding alleged gun attack on Rio Bravo Crescent; granted $1,500 bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 21-year-old Belize City man has been charged with allegedly helping another man carry out an armed attack on Rio Bravo Crescent last month.

Jaidyn William Brown, a car washer and construction worker, was arraigned in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on a single charge of abetment to commit aggravated assault.

Police allege that on August 25, 2026, Brown purposely aided Gareth Hemmans in committing an aggravated assault upon a 32-year-old man.

Brown, who was unrepresented, pleaded not guilty to the charge and was granted bail in the sum of $1,500 plus one surety of the same amount.

As a condition of his bail, Brown is prohibited from contacting or interfering with the complainant or any prosecution witness, either directly or indirectly. He is due back in court on November 5, 2026.

The charge stems from a shooting incident reported at around 7:30 p.m. on Rio Bravo Crescent. The complainant told police he was standing in front of a yard when a maroon Nissan Murano approached and slowed down.

According to the complainant, a passenger inside the vehicle allegedly pointed a firearm in his direction and fired several shots. He ran behind a cement fence and escaped without injury.

Police processed the scene and reportedly recovered two 9mm expended shells and a fragment. The Nissan Murano was later located on Jimmy Dyer Street, where police allegedly found another 9mm expended shell on the front passenger seat.

Hemmans, 35, was subsequently charged with aggravated assault with a firearm and remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison until October 29, 2026.

Brown’s case is scheduled to return to court on November 5.

World.title: Daniel Meighan remanded for alleged sexual assault of a minor
World.content:
Daniel Meighan remanded for alleged sexual assault of a minor

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 43-year-old security technician was remanded to the Belize Central Prison following his arraignment in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on a charge of sexual assault involving a minor.

Daniel Vincent Meighan, a resident of La Democracia Village, appeared before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2 to face a single count of assault of a child by penetration. The charge stems from allegations that in June 2026, Meighan intentionally penetrated and fondled a female child who was 12 years and 4 months old.

Due to the severity of the allegation, no plea was taken from Meighan during the proceedings.

The prosecution strongly objected to granting bail, emphasizing the young age of the victim, the gravity of the charge—which carries a potential sentence ranging from 12 years to life imprisonment upon conviction—the strength of the evidence, and the risk that the defendant might attempt to interfere with the ongoing police investigation if released.

In an unexpected turn of events, Meighan told the court he was willing to forgo a bail application at that time. He stated that he understood everything happening, maintained his innocence, and requested a quick trial while offering to go on remand in the interim. He added that prior to a police interview conducted while in custody, he had not been given details regarding the case against him.

After considering the prosecution’s arguments, the Senior Magistrate denied bail and informed Meighan that he maintains the right to apply for High Court bail through an attorney. Meighan was subsequently remanded to the Belize Central Prison, with his next court appearance scheduled for November 13, 2026.

World.title: CASINO CAUTION
World.content:
AS the Casino Gaming Commission (CGC) shores up its anti-money laundering defences ahead of the planned opening of Jamaica’s first casino at Princess Grande Jamaica Resort in Hanover early next year, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has issued a warning on key red flags to look out for.

FATF, the global illicit-finance watchdog, published a list of new gaming scams in a report on Wednesday, which it said was based on surveys conducted and included contributions from more than 80 jurisdictions.

The document titled ‘Red Flag Risk Indicators, Risks of Gaming and Gambling’, stated that the industries have changed significantly over recent years and continue to evolve through the expansion of online, cross-border, multi-product, and multi-payment platforms.

FATF said the work offers an updated analysis of money laundering risks posed by the casino sector as well as risks posed by the broader gambling and gaming sectors.

Red flag indicators in customer behaviour at brick-and-mortar casinos included attempts to influence or bribe venue staff to ignore their activities or bypass thorough customer due diligence checks and offering tips and other incentives.

Some casino customers were found to only want to deal with one staff member and avoid other staffers. These schemers use third parties to place cash into redemption terminals and purchase gaming chips, or place bets in an attempt to anonymise gambling.

The report outlined that the schemers also tend to request that winnings be paid in cash up to the threshold amount, but they never return to collect the balance. They also make purchases or attempts to purchase winning claim instruments from another customer and then present it as their own.

The report warned that eyebrows should raise if a player attempts to present a casino value instrument from an unknown source or if they are behaving in an unusual way on premises. It also warned of players acting on behalf of a third party and taking instructions from mobile phones or other customers on the premises.

Other red flags include customers who are reluctant or refuse to provide up-to-date identification documents or inconsistencies in personal information.

The report pointed out that some casino customers also opt to produce documents that are unclear or doctored and prove difficult to authenticate.

Where betting patterns are concerned, some customers were flagged for inconsistent spending that do not match their customer profile, including their known income and background.

In the report, FATF said it examined the scope of the risks associated with brick-and-mortar casinos, sports and novelty betting, other non-casino gambling — including scratch cards, arcades, bingo, lotteries, and slot machines outside of casinos.

“Findings indicate that certain payment methods associated with gaming and gambling activity such as cash, e-wallets, mobile money, and virtual assets are vulnerable to a range of money laundering risks. The variety of payment methods accepted by online gaming and gambling operators increasingly allows rapid, anonymous, cross-border transactions and conversion of value into different forms,” read page two of the 10-page document.

The operators and platforms covered in the report varied in nature and most of the risk indicators provided were related to land-based and online casinos and, to a lesser extent, betting. It was found that land-based operators have similar indicators as do online platforms.

In a statement on Wednesday, Giles Thomas, the president of FATF, said without robust safeguards, these sectors can attract gateways for fraudsters, professional money launderers, and organised criminal networks.

“I urge all governments to take note of the risk factors we have set out today, and put in place appropriate risk-based responses — from strengthening oversight and cracking down on illegal and offshore operators to boosting international co-operation and deepening public-private collaboration,” the FATF president said.

At a recent Jamaica Observer Monday Exchange officials of the CGC declared that they have been engaging in training with the Major Organised Crime and Anti-Corruption Agency (MOCA), the Financial Investigations Division (FID), and the Jamaica Customs Agency in an effort to ensure that strong anti-money laundering guardrails linked to casino gaming are in place when Jamaica gears up to claim its stake in an industry that generated more than US$320 billion worldwide last year.

The partnership with MOCA and FID is one based on capacity-building and information-sharing, support, and investigations.

Damion McKenzie, senior director of enforcement and investigations at the CGC, told Observer editors and reporters the entity recognises that, “Casino gaming is unique here, so some of the typologies and some of the crimes that happen in casinos, they might not be familiar with them. Our initiatives are to ensure that they are aware of those types of instances that can happen in a casino,” said McKenzie as he pointed out that the training of the law enforcement agents included them acquiring an understanding of the workings of slot machines and vulnerabilities.

The commission’s Chief Executive Officer Cleveland Allen emphasised that the entity is committed to properly regulating the casino gaming industry by ensuring that a multi-pronged approach is taken towards monitoring the sector in order to better protect the financial ecosystem.

“We operate in a space where we don’t have all the resources and all the knowledge, but remember, we operate in a large financial ecosystem. Our approach is focused on keeping us off the blacklist and on the right side of FATF,” Allen said.

He underscored that with Jamaica no longer being on the FATF list of countries that are assessed as having strategic deficiencies in their anti-money laundering/countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) regimes, dubbed a grey list, the CGC is prepared to do all in its powers to help to ensure Jamaica does not find itself back on that list.

In June 2024, then Minister of Finance Dr Nigel Clarke said he was proud to share that FATF, at its plenary in Singapore, welcomed Jamaica’s significant progress in improving its AML/CFT regimes.

As a result, FATF said that Jamaica was no longer subject to an increased monitoring process. With the island acknowledging the importance of remaining off the grey list, the CGC said it plans to ensure there are tight guardrails to protect Jamaica’s good standing with FATF.

Jamaica was placed on the FATF grey list in 2020, which signalled to international financial institutions to take special care when transacting with entities and individuals from the island.

One of the drawbacks of this is that it is more expensive to carry out transactions with countries on the list.

Other red flag indicators to look out for at casinos and other gaming establishments:

*Sudden changes in customer’s betting patterns.

*Co-ordinated or unusual betting activity, including hedged bets, betting on all outcomes and consistent losses to other players in peer-to-peer settings.

*Structuring of deposits into smaller amounts to fall under reporting thresholds.

*Use of short-odds bets and other low-risk mechanisms to justify withdrawals.

*Players making numerous large withdrawals without engaging in significant gambling activity.

*Customers appear to play frequently together, with one always winning and the other always losing.

*Suspected collusion in gambling activities, including gambling on both likely outcomes.

*Customer tries to circumvent note insertion limits by playing multiple machines simultaneously.

*Customer frequently plays games with low returns but with lower risks and a higher chance of winning.

*Customer repeatedly collects winnings just below a customer identification threshold.

*Non-genuine play patterns – wagers are low while large sums are deposited and withdrawn.

World.title: Gov’t looking to add speed to school repairs
World.content:
This file photos shows some of the damage Hurricane Melissa did to Edwin Allen High School last year.

THE Government could look overseas for contractors to speed up the repair and rebuilding of schools devastated by Hurricane Melissa last October.

More than 600 educational institutions sustained damage from the Category 5 storm with 309 severely damaged and ranked priority one for repairs and reconstruction.

At a post-Cabinet media briefing at Jamaica House in St Andrew on Wednesday officials of the Ministry of Education said 57 of those severely damaged institutions were fully repaired when the new school year began on Monday. The ministry said another 95 schools will be fully repaired by the end of September, and another 34 repaired by the end of December.

Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon told the media briefing that school repairs were hampered by a shortage of grade one contractors and the ministry will, among other things, explore hiring external contractors to fill gaps while ramping up efforts to upskill local contractors.

Morris Dixon admitted that the current situation is far from perfect and argued that the need for contractors was even more imperative given the mandate placed on the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority (NaRRA) — the specialised body established to coordinate and accelerate post-disaster rebuilding and long-term infrastructure resilience after Hurricane Melissa.

She pointed out that while the Administration is committed to continue the work to rebuild schools it has been constrained by the number of grade one contractors available in Jamaica.

“When the budget for the project is above a particular amount, you have to use a grade one contractor, and we’re limited with the number of grade one contractors, so that’s a constraint,” Morris Dixon explained.

“We need those contractors for the schools, we need them for the homes, we need them for the businesses, we need them for that beautiful vision that Prime Minister [Dr Andrew Holness] laid out in his budget presentation. And so, one of the things that we are working on, separately, in a different part of the ministry on the skills side, is an initiative between HEART NSTA/Trust and the Development Bank of Jamaica (DBJ)…we have to work to get those who are at grade two up to grade one through financing and otherwise, because that’s a key element of it. And so DBJ is at the table with us, trying to work through that, because our goal is to give the money to the Jamaicans,” Morris Dixon disclosed.

“What we’re looking at is, how we can work with young people who want to be contractors, put them in groupings, provide funding, and provide incubation to them so that we can get more in the pipeline of grade one contractors. Using external sources is something that we’ll have to look at. For example, for the STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) schools, we have done international tenders, and so in some of the big projects, we’ll have to do some international tendering. We’ll see what comes out of that…but right now, our commitment is to our local contractors using them. But of course, they have to show that they can deliver,” Morris Dixon said further.

The education minister, in the meantime, said work was continuing apace to rehabilitate schools listed as priority one which were severely damaged by Melissa with almost continuous afternoon rain in Westmoreland slowing down the process.

“It’s not perfect. Where we are now is not perfect, and we have a lot of people working. We have many contractors. For our very severely damaged schools, which is about 309 schools that were severely damaged… the bills are high. A lot of them are over $100 million, $200 million, $300 million, a billion dollars almost in some instances,” Morris Dixon said.

According to Morris Dixon, the hurricane is being used as an opportunity “to get better school plants, at least in the west”.

Meanwhile, permanent secretary in the Ministry of Education Dr Kasan Troupe said the new school year got off to a fair start on Monday with 92 per cent of schools having all students while two per cent of schools will have to be augmented with temporary learning spaces and utilise some amount of rotation.

“That’s tremendous given what we have been through, and I want to thank all my principals, all my chairmen and board members, and of course, all the teachers,” Troupe said.

She told the media briefing that the ministry has ensured that all schools have been given their operational funds along with furniture and other resources.

“We sent out 30 per cent of the increased grants into our schools in June. The second tranche of that is due in September, the first Friday in September and two weeks ago, we ensured that all the funds were out in all our schools, so we are ahead of time because we understand what it means for our principals to have monies to get the work done. That amounted to $3.05 billion that we have disbursed to our schools, and that will treat with the operations, that will treat with the nutritional support for the learners, and of course, an additional $75 million we sent out to our schools to impact 275 schools to treat with canteen repairs,” Troupe said.

“As it relates to furniture, 41 schools indicated that they need additional support. We are responding to that, but in preparation for this year, we spent $300 million to get furniture out into our schools. So before we started, we distributed over 17,000 pieces, and whilst we were wrapping up on the last weekend, there were 8,000 pieces that we were distributing across our schools,” added Troupe.

According to the permanent secretary, another 20,000 pieces of furniture are being prepared for distribution to the system.

She said the ministry is spending more than $700 million in resourcing high schools with books and more than $300 million in primary schools, making that approximately $1.1 billion of expenditure in providing books for public schools.

World.title: 450 set for Caribbean Music Awards performance
World.content:
450...preparation has been good. We’ve been putting in the work and making sure everything is right.

Dancehall artiste 450 is gearing up to make his debut performance at the highly anticipated Caribbean Music Awards (CMA).

The fourth annual ceremony and showcase will take place on Saturday, September 19 at the National Academy for the Performing Arts (NAPA) in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago.

For 450, the opportunity to perform on the regional stage represents another significant moment in his career.

“It feels like a big moment for me. The CMA is a major platform for Caribbean music, so it feels like another chapter of the story that my team and I are grateful for,” 450, who is also nominated for Album of the Year, told the Jamaica Observer.

V’ghn, Freetown Collective, Jah Mason, 1T1, and Theomaa are among the artistes slated to perform. The line-up represents a cross section of Caribbean music, spanning soca, reggae, dancehall, bouyon, and contemporary Caribbean sounds.

After three years of staging the awards in New York City, organisers are bringing CMA to the Caribbean for the first time since its inception. The move will also see the celebration expand beyond a single awards night into an immersive weekend of activities.

The weekend is expected to feature networking opportunities, industry discussions, cultural showcases, and opportunities for fans to interact more closely with artistes and other players in the Caribbean music industry.

450 said preparations are well under way for his performance, with his team focused on ensuring his CMA debut makes an impact.

“Preparation has been good. We’ve been putting in the work and making sure everything is right,” he shared.

While not revealing too much about what he has planned, the entertainer promised a high-energy performance featuring some of the songs that have connected with his fan base.

“Energy, good vibes, and some of the songs they know and love. I’m representing Jamaica and dancehall music,” 450 said.

The appearance comes during what the artiste describes as a strong year of career growth, particularly as he continues to introduce his music to audiences outside Jamaica.

“It’s been a really good year. I’ve been able to reach new audiences, perform on bigger international stages, and continue growing the music. There’s still more to accomplish, so mi nah slow down,” he said.

With the final quarter of 2026 under way, 450 has no plans to ease the pace. Beyond his upcoming CMA performance, the dancehall artiste is working on new material and further expanding his international presence.

“I’m working on new music, more visuals, and some exciting international projects. More to come soon,” he added.

World.title: Contractor says all his 7 school jobs almost complete
World.content:
Inside a newly completed grade six classroom with a new roof, ceiling, lighting and ceiling fans at Petersfield Primary School in Westmoreland..

PETERSFIELD, Westmoreland — While several schools in western Jamaica still have a long way to go to repair damage inflicted by last October’s Hurricane Melissa, Petersfield Primary in Westmoreland is now 98 per cent complete. There are only a few doors and windows left to be installed.

The Petersfield project is one of seven being undertaken by Archistruct Limited. Others include William Knibb High in Trelawny and five schools in St Ann. According to owner and managing director of the 14-year-old company Chadwick Lawrence, all the schools are almost 100 per cent repaired.

“The minister [of education] did say she’s holding us accountable, so I take that one seriously. I couldn’t afford to disappoint her,” he told the Jamaica Observer Wednesday.

With a degree in engineering and a master’s in construction project management, Lawrence is supported by a team of qualified construction professionals.

“It is no secret sauce; it’s just a matter of management and execution of tasks based on schedule and procuring materials on time. That is what I do. We use a lot of people from the area, as well as people from different areas, as needed. At Petersfield, we did a lot of night and day work to get it finished,” Lawrence explained when asked the secret to his success in having the schools ready for September.

“It boils down to one expression: Construction is about the joy of creating. It is nice to just see the students inside the classroom; it’s a genuinely nice feeling to see the students in the classroom learning and the teachers teaching in a comfortable space. When you talk with the teachers and the principals and they tell you that they are happy with the product they have received because it’s better than it was before… that really brings the joy of creating,” he said.

The company has been strategic in its approach.

“In terms of the scheduling and procurement of materials, we had ensured that we did that beforehand as we went along. We were doing seven schools, so we were able to buy in bulk and to get everything on spot before we needed it. Now we are at 98 per cent complete and we are happy to say that it is a good September morning. All the kids are out and about, parents and teachers are happy, and we’re just glad to see a satisfied customer,” Lawrence told the Observer.

School board chairman and Custos of Westmoreland Reverend Hartley Perrin, who had initial concerns, is among those pleased with the results at Petersfield Primary.

“I had my doubts. I was very concerned about the progress, or lack thereof… But then, all of a sudden, it started to pick up as if they stepped on the accelerator. They were working longer hours and they seemed to have employed more people. I’m pleased to see the work that has been done and the quality of it. Even the painting is of good standard,” the Custos beamed.

But it has not all been smooth sailing. The type of windows needed for the school projects is not available in Jamaica. The original structures had aluminum window blades.

“We’re doing some… we discussed with the principals and they have agreed to other options for the type of windows,” said Lawrence.

At all seven schools, his team is now adding little touches that make a world of difference.

“We work closely with the principals and teachers. Even now, we are at different locations doing what we call commissioning. There are little things that might be needed — a teacher may need a nail there or a piece of board there for a pin-up board [to place teaching aids] — and we’re there now putting those things in place to make the space as comfortable as possible,” said Lawrence.

At Petersfield, his company has a separate contract to build a new administrative and classroom block. Lawrence confirmed that all materials are on-site and the bending of steel began Wednesday morning.

World.title: THE ULTIMATE TEST
World.content:
World 100m champion Oblique Seville headlines Jamaica’s team for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest, Hungary. (Photo: AFP)

Technical Leader Maurice Wilson says Jamaica’s athletes will be ready for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships which starts tomorrow at the National Athletics Center in Budapest, Hungary.

A 32-member team, with 27 athletes set to contest individual events for Jamaica, was named by World Athletics on Monday, based on world rankings for the first of what is set to be an annual end-of-season all-star competition.

Wilson described the event as “a fantastic initiative”, which he said has the potential to take the sport to another level.

“There are changes to the arrangements,” he told the Jamaica Observer, where athletes’ representatives will have “a more hands-on” duty, as national federations such as the Jamaica Athletics Administrative Association (JAAA) will only be responsible for naming relay coaches.

Wilson and Michael Frater have been named by the JAAA to take charge of the mixed 4x100m and 4x400m teams, with the athletes being able to have their personal coaches with them.

“Every major professional sport has annual championships,” Wilson said. “So track and field should not be an exception, and this is something we need.”

Winners of the individual events will receive a bye to the 2027 World Championships as well as US$150,000 (over $23 million) while winning relay teams will share US$80,000 (just over $12 million). Just about every participant will take home a cash prize.

There will also be a US$100,000 ($15.5 million) bonus for breaking a world record, while the champions will get a trophy rather than the traditional gold, silver, and bronze medals.

Newly crowned Diamond League 100m champions Oblique Seville and Tina Clayton have been included in Jamaica’s 32-member team that will compete at the three-day event.

In addition to Seville on the men’s side, Commonwealth Games champions Navasky Anderson, Romaine Beckford, and Demario Prince were also named.

Commonwealth Games champion Sanique Walker and women’s 4x100m relay gold medallists Jodean Williams and Lavanya Williams were also named.

Navasky Anderson, Romaine Beckford, Orlando Bennett, Ackeem Blake, Bryan Levell, Tyler Mason, Demario Prince, Oblique Seville, Christopher Taylor

Women

Rushell Clayton, Tina Clayton, Lamara Distin, Brianna Lyston, Ashanti Moore, Ackera Nugent, Nickisha Pryce, Demisha Roswell, Shiann Salmon, Megan Simmonds, Ackelia Smith, Jonielle Smith, Sanique Walker, Danielle Williams, Jodean Williams, Lavanya Williams

Relays

Zandrion Barnes, Kadrion Goldson, Rohan Watson, Assinie Wilson, Shana Kaye Anderson

World.title: ‘My heart broke’: Education minister orders probe after student denied restroom
World.content:
Minister of Education, Skills, Youth and Information, Senator Dr. the Hon. Dana Morris Dixon, addresses the post-Cabinet press briefing held on September 9 at Jamaica House. (Photo: JIS)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth and Information is to receive an official report from the school where a student was denied the opportunity to use the restroom and soiled herself.

Portfolio Minister, Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon, made the disclosure during the post-Cabinet press briefing on Wednesday at Jamaica House.

“When I saw that story, of course, as many Jamaicans did, my heart broke,” Morris Dixon said. “My heart was breaking for that student when I heard the story, and so I understand the outrage. I understand how Jamaicans feel and how they feel it as if it were their child, because I felt similarly that that was my child.”

“As minister, I have to have all the facts, and it’s for that reason that I’ve asked for an investigation of what took place, so that I can get an official report on it with all the facts on the table. And then we will take action after that,” she added.

The minister said she spoke with the child’s father on Wednesday, noting that the ministry will provide the necessary support needed.

“I had a good conversation [and] noted that all of Jamaica feels concerned and that we’re worried about his daughter. We conveyed our love for her and that at the ministry we’ll provide whatever support she may need. There was indication that there may be need for some emotional support and some counselling support,” Morris Dixon said.

“In the ministry we’ll do that. We have psychologists on retainer, so any child in our system that needs support, we in the ministry, we pay for the psychologist or if they need a psychiatrist, we also pay for it. So, we’ll provide whatever support that child needs, and the children of Jamaica are at the centre of our decision-making,” she added.

The minister also revealed that she spoke with the principal of the school on Wednesday, adding that it was important to listen to all sides.

“I had a good conversation with the principal, and she assured me that the children are at the centre of all of her policies. And that everything she does is with them in mind. She also went through what happened on the day. She’s indicated we will get the official report from the school, and as I said, we’ll meet with the Board, we’ll meet with the parent, with the school, and in the ministry we’ll get to the bottom of it, and we will take action that is needed,” she added.

Morris Dixon pointed out that many schools have a difficult balancing act, noting that “out of safety for the children and out of other incidents that may have happened, you have to make a call as a teacher”.

“So, I understand the difficulty in that call. But when there are emergencies, we have to act differently. So even when we have the set bathroom breaks, if a child is ill between those bathroom breaks, we have to give them the time to go to the bathroom. And the good thing is when I spoke to the principal, the official rules at the school match with the ministry’s expectations and so what we have to do as a ministry, is to check if the rules were broken,” she said.

— JIS

World.title: Grand Marshals Buju, Kes join Mamdani for New York Caribbean Carnival Parade
World.content:
Trinidadian social artiste Kees Dieffenthaller (left) and dancehall icon Buju Banton (left) with Mayor of New York City Zohran Mamdani (centre) at the 59th Annual New York Caribbean Carnival Week and Parade.

NEW YORK, United States — Grammy Award-winning Reggae artiste Buju Banton proudly represented Jamaica as an Honorary Grand Marshal of the 59th Annual New York Caribbean Carnival Parade.

Held on Labour Day, September 7, along Brooklyn’s Eastern Parkway, the event saw Buju sharing the honour with Kees Dieffenthaller of ‘Kes The Band’, bringing together two of the Caribbean’s most influential musical voices.

Representing Jamaica’s reggae and dancehall traditions alongside Kes’ Trinidadian soca and Carnival roots, the artistes reflected the spirit of “One Caribbean” and the cultural connections that unite the region and its diaspora.

The day began with the West Indian American Day Carnival Association’s annual VIP Breakfast at the Carlos Lezama Netball Court in Lincoln Terrace Park, where Buju Banton and Dieffenthaller were formally recognised as Honorary Grand Marshals.

The gathering brought together elected officials, community leaders and cultural ambassadors, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, New York Governor Kathy Hochul, New York Attorney General Letitia James, United States (US) Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, New York City Public Advocate Jumaane Williams, New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso, New York City Council Member Farah N Louis and Irvington, New Jersey Councilwoman Charnette Frederic.

Following the breakfast, Buju Banton took to Eastern Parkway alongside Dieffenthaller and Mamdani, greeting spectators as the parade moved through Brooklyn in a vibrant celebration of Caribbean music, heritage and identity. His presence drew an enthusiastic response from paradegoers, many of whom carried Jamaican flags and celebrated the opportunity to see one of reggae and dancehall’s most respected voices representing the island on the Parkway.

Throughout the procession, Buju Banton also made stops to join the PIX11 crew for live on-camera moments, sharing the energy of the parade and the significance of the occasion with television audiences across New York.

The appearance marked another major cultural moment for Jamaican music in New York and reflected Buju Banton’s enduring connection with Caribbean communities across the diaspora.

His appointment also recognised a career spent carrying the sound, messages and cultural identity of Jamaica to audiences around the world. The honour comes as Buju Banton continues to promote his latest studio album, Too Too Bad, released on July 17 through Gargamel Music/VP Records. The 13-track project includes collaborations with DJ Khaled, Ari Lennox and Gramps Morgan.

For nearly six decades, the New York Caribbean Carnival Parade has transformed Eastern Parkway into one of North America’s largest celebrations of Caribbean culture.

Buju Banton’s participation as Honorary Grand Marshal stood as a proud moment for Jamaica while reinforcing reggae and dancehall’s lasting place within the wider Caribbean story.

World.title: SLB apologises for email distribution error
World.content:
The Students’ Loan Bureau head office in Kingston.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Students’ Loan Bureau (SLB) is advising customers of an inadvertent email distribution error that occurred on Tuesday, September 8, during the dissemination of its SLB Insights newsletter.

According to the SLB in a statement on Wednesday, the newsletter was being distributed to customers as part of its ongoing communication regarding loan repayment obligations. It said during the distribution process, a customer email distribution list was inadvertently attached to one batch of the mailing in place of the intended newsletter.

“This was an error on the bureau’s part in the execution of that distribution. The affected file contained a list of customer email addresses only. It did not contain separate fields with customer names, loan account numbers, loan balances, Taxpayer Registration Numbers (TRNs), dates of birth, residential addresses, telephone numbers, banking information, passwords or other account credentials,” said the SLB.

SLB said the error affected only one batch of the distribution.

“The file was not published on SLB’s website, social media channels or other public platforms. The bureau is continuing to verify the final scope of the affected distribution and whether there is any evidence of further dissemination. The incident did not alter any customer’s loan account, balance, repayment obligation or account status. There is currently no indication that the incident resulted from unauthorised access to SLB’s systems or from malicious activity. The matter was identified and escalated for investigation on the same day it occurred,” the bureau added.

The bureau said it has initiated a review of the incident and of the controls governing bulk customer communications, including confirmation of the scope of the affected distribution and the implementation of additional safeguards to reduce the possibility of a recurrence.

“Bulk email distributions using the affected process have been suspended while additional safeguards are implemented. The matter has been reported to the Office of the Information Commissioner in accordance with applicable requirements. Customers identified as affected are being contacted directly by the bureau,” the SLB said.

It noted that as a precaution, customers should remain vigilant for suspicious or unsolicited communications that may appear to originate from the bureau.

“SLB takes seriously the responsibility entrusted to us to safeguard customer information,” said Nickeisha Walsh, executive director. “Customers should not disclose passwords or one- time passcodes in response to unsolicited emails and should verify any suspicious communication directly with SLB through its official channels.”

The executive director added: “This was an error on the bureau’s part, and we apologise to the customers affected. Our customers are entitled to expect that information entrusted to SLB will be handled with appropriate care. We are addressing the immediate incident and strengthening the processes and system controls governing bulk customer communications to reduce the risk of a recurrence.”

The SLB said it remains committed to communicating transparently with affected customers while ensuring that information released about the incident is accurate and based on verified findings.
