World.title: Madrid se mueve al ritmo de la Fórmula 1: entradas agotadas, hoteles más caros, casi 9.000 empleos y un impulso para hostelería y ocio
World.content:
45 años después, la capital acoge este fin de semana una carrera del Mundial, lo que provoca quejas entre los vecinos de Hortaleza por el ruido y las restricciones de movilidad. “Estoy encantado de ver a la ciudad volcada”, dice Carlos Sainz

Desde el viernes, Madrid se moverá durante tres días al ritmo de la Fórmula 1. El regreso del Gran Circo a la capital del país 45 años después de su última carrera en la ciudad ha generado una fiebre que ha llevado a que se agoten las entradas pese a su elevado precio —el aforo previsto es de 350.000 personas—, a que los hoteles registren subidas notables por la alta demanda y a que una parte relevante del sector de la restauración y el ocio se vuelque con un evento que se prevé que atraiga a decenas de miles de turistas extranjeros. El madrileño Carlos Sainz Jr., piloto de Williams e hijo de Carlos Sainz, respondía ayer a EL PAÍS que se quedó sorprendido con la acogida que tuvo la presentación de su coche en la plaza de Callao: “Y era martes, imagínate cómo va a estar esto el fin de semana. Estoy encantado de ver a la ciudad volcada”.

El Gran Premio de España se celebra del 11 al 13 de septiembre en el nuevo Madring, un circuito semiurbano levantado por Ifema junto a sus pabellones en el distrito de Hortaleza que también ha provocado quejas entre los vecinos por el ruido que generan los coches —muy superior a los 35 decibelios que fija el límite legal del Ayuntamiento— y por los atascos y limitaciones que se prevén para salir y moverse por la zona. El impacto de la carrera en términos económicos, deportivos y de visibilidad, en cambio, se prevé que sea formidable tras el acuerdo anunciado el 23 de enero de 2024 para atraer el evento a la capital. La anterior vez que los monoplazas de la Fórmula 1 circularon en Madrid fue en el circuito del Jarama en 1981, cuando ganó el Ferrari del canadiense Gilles Villeneuve. “Medio siglo casi. A mí, mi padre me habló de cuando la Fórmula 1 vino a Madrid. Mi padre y mi tío Juanjo me dijeron que fueron a esa última carrera en Madrid, y parece mentira que haya tenido que pasar medio siglo para que Madrid vuelva a tener una carrera. Hemos conseguido que vuelva, y es una ciudad muy especial, muy apta para hacer eventos de estas características”, apuntaba ayer Sainz.

Al circuito, que cuenta con 5.417 metros y 22 curvas —la más destacada de ellas la Monumental, con más de 500 metros de cuerda y un peralte del 24%—, llega como favorito Kimi Antonelli, el líder indiscutible del Mundial que hace solo unos días triunfó en Monza después de una remontada memorable desde la 19ª posición gracias al poderío de su Mercedes.

Carlos Sainz, el miércoles en una rueda de prensa en Callao, en el centro de Madrid. AFP7 vía Europa Press (AFP7 vía Europa Press)

A la competición deportiva se une la económica. En la ciudad habrá simuladores en hoteles y restaurantes, pantallas gigantes para retransmitir las carreras, promociones inspiradas en las 57 vueltas del circuito y menús especiales para prolongar la jornada después de la bandera a cuadros. Un informe elaborado por PwC sitúa “en 467 millones de euros y 8.850 empleos el impacto económico estimado” asociado a la celebración del Gran Premio. El estudio calcula también una recaudación cercana a los 83 millones en impuestos y cotizaciones sociales. Según los datos de compradores incluidos en el informe, se han vendido “más de 120.000 entradas de grada y hospitalidades”; se estima que más de 80.000 asistentes llegarán desde fuera de la Comunidad de Madrid y alrededor de 45.000 procederán de otros países.

La presión ya se nota en los hoteles. Según la plataforma de comercio hotelero SiteMinder, las habitaciones alcanzan una tarifa media diaria de 485 euros, un 69,6% más que los 286 euros registrados durante el mismo periodo del año pasado. Los datos de Amadeus también reflejan un aumento de las reservas aéreas coincidiendo con la celebración del Gran Premio. Las procedentes del Reino Unido han crecido un 46%; las de Corea del Sur, un 45%; las de Francia, un 32%; y las de Uruguay, un 31% respecto a 2025.

Las cifras dibujan un escenario favorable, aunque los expertos piden prudencia. Albert Guivernau, investigador de OBS Business School y director de la Fundación Civismo, advierte de que todo el dinero movilizado alrededor de un acontecimiento de estas dimensiones no puede considerarse automáticamente riqueza nueva para la ciudad. “La Fórmula 1 tiene un impacto económico muy relevante para Madrid, tanto por el gasto directo que genera como por su capacidad para reforzar la posición internacional de la ciudad. Las estimaciones hablan de unos 450 millones de euros de impacto y 8.000 empleos directos, aunque debemos ser rigurosos: impacto económico no significa necesariamente riqueza neta creada. Parte de esa actividad vendrá desplazada desde otros sectores”, explica Guivernau.

Para el economista, la aportación adicional más clara procede del gasto de las personas que llegan desde otros lugares. “Los hoteles alcanzan tarifas medias de 485 euros, casi un 70% superiores a las del mismo fin de semana del año pasado. Y una parte importante de los visitantes llega de fuera de Madrid, que es precisamente el gasto que más claramente podemos considerar adicional”, añade. El principal retorno, sostiene, puede producirse a medio y largo plazo.

Madrid permanecerá al menos durante 10 años en el calendario de la Fórmula 1, lo que proporcionará a la ciudad una exposición internacional continuada. “Si consigue convertir esa visibilidad en turismo, inversión y actividad económica, el efecto irá mucho más allá de los tres días de competición”, afirma.

Vista de un fragmento del circuito Madring. Mark Thompson (Getty Images)

Frente a las previsiones sobre el dinero que dejará la carrera aparece la factura del proyecto. Según los datos facilitados por Más Madrid, 200 millones de euros se han destinado al circuito y otros 277 millones corresponden a los derechos durante 10 años. A esas cantidades se suma el paquete promocional denominado Destination Signage Package, aprobado por Madrid Destino. El Ayuntamiento aporta 1,9 millones; la Comunidad de Madrid, otros 1,9 millones; e Ifema, 700.000 euros.

La suma asciende a 481,5 millones de euros, aunque agrupa conceptos de distinta naturaleza y correspondientes a periodos diferentes: la inversión en el circuito, los derechos durante una década y una partida promocional concreta. Tampoco puede compararse directamente con los 467 millones estimados por PwC. Esta última cifra mide la actividad económica que se estima que generará el acontecimiento, no los beneficios netos ni el dinero que ingresarán directamente las administraciones.

Más allá del debate sobre el coste y de la competición y su retorno, los empresarios del ocio nocturno se preparan para uno de los fines de semana más señalados del año. La Asociación de Empresarios de Ocio y Espectáculos de la Comunidad de Madrid, Noche Madrid, calcula que el Gran Premio dejará unos 30 millones de euros en la vida nocturna de la ciudad. El sector valora con un 7,7 sobre 10 la capacidad de la Fórmula 1 para promocionar Madrid internacionalmente. Dos de cada tres empresas consideran que su impacto será bastante o muy importante para la actividad económica. En conjunto, los locales esperan aumentar su facturación un 5% respecto a un fin de semana normal de septiembre. En los establecimientos con mayor proyección turística, el incremento podría superar el 30%.

Hostelería Madrid amplía el cálculo al conjunto del comercio, la restauración y el ocio nocturno. Su presidente, José Antonio Aparicio, señala que estos sectores podrían concentrar alrededor del 25% del impacto general, equivalente a un negocio directo superior a 112 millones de euros. “Hay además un segmento de alto poder adquisitivo y de hospitalidad muy significativo en la Fórmula 1, pero sería un error pensar que el beneficio se limitará a la alta cocina o a los establecimientos de lujo”, sostiene Aparicio. La patronal espera que el efecto llegue a hoteles, restaurantes gastronómicos, establecimientos de precio medio y alto, bares, cafeterías, negocios de restauración informal y locales nocturnos.

Hoteles y restaurantes ya han diseñado sus propias estrategias para aprovechar la llegada de visitantes. Los hay que ofrecen un menú especial, otros cuentan con simuladores de conducción y máquinas recreativas. Soluciones, al fin y al cabo, para subirse al carro del evento del año en Madrid. “La llegada de la Fórmula 1 supone uno de los grandes acontecimientos que vivirá la ciudad y creemos que la hostelería tiene un papel fundamental a la hora de ampliar esa experiencia más allá del propio circuito”, explica Sara Cruz, directora de ventas y marketing de Grupo RosaNegra en España.

World.title: Qué hacer en Madrid el fin de semana de la Fórmula 1: el motor toma Callao, Colón, Serrano, Gran Vía y la Puerta del Sol
World.content:
El alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, junto al piloto Carlos Sainz, durante la presentación del monoplaza de Atlassian Williams F1 Team en la plaza de Callao, este martes.

Para los que quieran huir de la competición, hay propuestas como la XII edición de Directed by Women Spain, MagiCéltica y el festival Back to the Book

Tanto si viene a Madrid del 11 al 13 de septiembre a asistir al flamante regreso de la Fórmula 1 ―o a olisquearlo más bien, porque las entradas, caras, están agotadas― como si ya vive aquí, la ciudad ofrece este fin de semana toda su potencia de fuego en cultura, entretenimiento y gastronomía. Entre todo lo que se puede hacer gratis en la capital, el Ayuntamiento, convertido en una guía del ocio, destaca las tres fanzones montadas para la ocasión en Callao, Colón y Gran Vía y actividades no ideadas ad hoc al calor de los motores, como la XII edición de Directed by Women Spain, la MagiCéltica en Vallecas, las fiestas de los distritos de Barajas y Ciudad Lineal y el festival Back to the Book.

Las actividades municipales son gratuitas, aunque algunas tienen aforo limitado o requieren registro. Para empezar, el visitante y el madrileño reconvertido en turista tienen a su disposición tres fanzones para los aficionados del motor:

plaza y los Cines Callao acogen “una gran experiencia participativa que incluye simuladores de conducción, exposiciones de vehículos, espacios educativos y actividades familiares” (y una zona de merchandising ). Pasarán por allí Carlos Sainz, Luke Browning y James Vowles. Atlassian Williams Racing Fan Zone : laplaza y los Cines Callao acogen “una gran experiencia participativa que incluye simuladores de conducción, exposiciones de vehículos, espacios educativos y actividades familiares” (y una zona de). Pasarán por allí Carlos Sainz, Luke Browning y James Vowles.

La Monumental, F1 City Experience : “gran espacio dedicado a la historia de la competición y al desarrollo tecnológico de la industria del motor” instalado por Audi en la plaza de Colón. Incluye una muestra de vehículos históricos y una gran estructura inspirada en la curva del nuevo circuito.

Espacio Alpine : en Alcalá con Gran Vía, Alpine muestra varios de sus modelos más representativos junto a una réplica a escala real de un monoplaza de Fórmula 1.

Además, se proyectará un “innovador videomapping” sobre la Real Casa de Correos en la Puerta del Sol, que “combinará la historia de Madrid con la emoción de la Fórmula 1″. También hay espacio para iniciativas solidarias como Cash & Rocket Car Tour 2026, que llegará el domingo y reunirá a mujeres emprendedoras de distintos países junto con la exhibición gratuita de deportivos rojos.

Por último, en la calle de Serrano, una exposición fotográfica dedicada a la historia del automovilismo y del Circuito del Jarama convivirá con la exhibición de un monoplaza oficial. Las escuderías y otras empresas se han desplegado por la ciudad: McLaren Pop-Up en el centro comercial La Vaguada, merchandising de Williams en El Corte Inglés de Castellana y una Pop-Up de ElevenLabs en la calle Belén 4 en la que se podrá entrevistar a un piloto de F1 con IA. Hasta Visit Qatar, país al que llegará el campeonato a finales de noviembre, ha montado su sarao: La Parada, en la plaza de Santiago, con gastronomía, automovilismo y regalos. También de pago, en el paseo de la Castellana se encuentra F1 Arcade con más de 70 simuladores.

En cuanto a eventos exclusivos, Isa, el restaurante y coctelería del hotel Four Seasons organizará una experiencia para grupos reducidos que incluirá el uso de un simulador de carreras y una degustación de gyozas y cerveza, mientras que el Only YOU Boutique Hotel, con Red Bull Curates, ha montado una zona de juegos con simuladores de conducción y máquinas recreativas y en su terraza podrá seguirse la competición. Los restaurantes Mamazzita y Chambao retransmitirán el GP en pantallas gigantes.

Fuera de la capital, el Gobierno regional ha querido sumarse a la fiesta con más de una decena de actividades gratuitas en ocho municipios, que van desde la exposición del Fórmula 1430 de Santiago Martín Cantero en Paracuellos, a un concurso de pintura infantil en Villa del Prado, a un fanzone en Las Rozas, cuatro simuladores de F1 en Arroyomolinos, otros tres en Alcobendas y otros dos en La Cabrera, que tendrá además un photocall, música en directo y una pantalla gigante para seguir la carrera.

Si busca planes culturales al margen de la Fórmula 1, la Casa del Lector de Matadero Madrid (plaza de Legazpi, 8) acoge la tercera edición de Back to the Book Festival con libros, clubs de lectura, cafés de especialidad, charlas, podcast, presentaciones, dj set, cerveza, exposiciones, talleres, catas literarias y más. Entre sus citas más destacadas están la cantante Julieta Venegas, que presentará su primera novela, el historietista Paco Roca y la escritora Lucía Solla Sobral.

También Matadero, pero en la Cineteca, se celebrará la XII edición del festival de cine Directed by Women Spain con la proyección de 50 cortos dirigidos por mujeres y nueve largometrajes. En cuanto a exposiciones gratis, destaca Revolución cuántica, que reúne en el Espacio Fundación Telefónica (Fuencarral, 3) más de 120 obras, entre piezas científicas históricas, instalaciones inmersivas, audiovisuales, infografías y desarrollos interactivos. En la sala Alcalá 31, está Mitologías modernas: Ouka Leele & Co, con obras de la artista junto a otras figuras clave como El Hortelano o Sigfrido Martin Begué. Y Matadero acoge Bailad, bailad, malditos, instalación del artista Carlos Aires en la que anima al público a entrar en una pista de baile dentro de un espacio apuntalado.

Si busca planes con niños, el Espacio Abierto Quinta de Los Molinos (en Juan Ignacio Luca de Tena, 20) invita a pasar el día allí en pijama y ver una boutique de trajes de noche imposibles, escuchar conciertos de nanas, ver sesiones de cortos y participar en talleres de creación dadá. En el capítulo musical, la gran apuesta gratuita del Ayuntamiento es una nueva edición del ciclo Flamenco en el Templete José Menese (ubicado en la plaza de Huarte de San Juan) por el que pasarán figuras reconocidas como Paco del Pozo, Esther Merino o Elena Andújar.

Si prefiere salir del centro, en el Mirador del Cerro del Tío Pío (Benjamín Palencia, 1) se celebra MagiCéltica, un festival familiar de temática fantástica organizado por el distrito de Puente de Vallecas con pasacalles, teatro, personajes mitológicos, espectáculos circenses, música y danza tradicional.

También de paseo por los distritos, este fin de semana coinciden las fiestas patronales de dos. Por un lado, Barajas celebra sus fiestas patronales en honor a Nuestra Señora de la Soledad con un recinto ferial en la calle de Ayerbe. Las fiestas, que tienen hasta chupinazo, incluirán conciertos, como el de Nil Molinera, DJ´s, pasacalles, un encierro infantil, fuegos artificiales, chocolatada, paella o aperitivos populares. En segundo lugar, Ciudad Lineal está también de fiestas, con conciertos como Cepeda, Nacha Pop y La Década Prodigiosa, pasacalles, competiciones, talleres y propuestas para toda la familia.

World.title: Fórmula 1 en Madrid: todos los cortes de tráfico para el fin de semana
World.content:
La EMT pondrá en marcha cinco servicios especiales gratuitos para facilitar la llegada y salida al circuito Madring entre el 11 y el 13 de septiembre

La Fórmula 1 volverá a rodar en Madrid después de 45 años. La pista que aquel 21 de junio de 1981 estuvo dentro del Jarama se trasladará este 2026 a las calles de la capital. El Madring, un circuito semiurbano de carreras de 5,4 kilómetros, recibirá a más de 330.000 personas entre el 11 y el 13 de septiembre. El evento tendrá mucho impacto en la movilidad, con cortes de tráfico en diversas calles. Para mejorar los desplazamientos, se recomienda utilizar el transporte público, que pondrá en marcha cinco servicios especiales gratuitos para llegar y salir del circuito.

Cortes del 10 al 14 de septiembre

Las modificaciones y cortes anunciados por el Ayuntamiento de Madrid comenzarán desde un día antes de la carrera y acabarán hasta un día después, es decir, irán del 10 al 14 de septiembre, en las inmediaciones del recinto ferial Ifema, en el distrito de Hortaleza.

La circulación estará restringida a lo largo de la calle de la Ribera del Sena, entre la glorieta de Luxemburgo y la glorieta de la vía de Dublín. En el mismo tramo, estará prohibido el tránsito desde la glorieta de Edimburgo hasta la M-40, así como desde la confluencia de la calle Ariadna hasta la glorieta del Sintra. También aplica para la glorieta de la vía de Dublín y su acceso desde la calle de Ariadna.

Al otro lado de la calle Ariadna, la circulación vehicular estará prohibida a lo largo de la calle de Francisco Umbral desde la vía de Dublín y hasta antes de la glorieta de Isidro González Velázquez. En ese tramo permanecerá abierto el acceso a la gasolinera de la glorieta de Francisco Umbral desde la conexión con la M-11, pero estará cerrado el acceso a la glorieta de Pascual Bravo desde el camino Alto de Hortaleza. También se permitirá la circulación en el sentido de bajada desde la glorieta de Isidro Velázquez hasta la de Manuel Muñoz Monasterio. La calle Alejandro de la Sota tendrá cambios en su ordenación: desde el 11 de septiembre se cortará la calzada en dirección sur y la norte permitirá la circulación en doble sentido.

Coronas entre el 11 y el 13 de septiembre

Durante el fin de semana del Gran Premio de España, habrá dos coronas de movilidad con puntos de regulación y vigilancia para filtrar y controlar el tráfico, así como desviar, cambiar el sentido de la circulación o implementar nuevas restricciones de ser necesario. Los dispositivos en la corona exterior estarán ubicados en la avenida de Logroño, M-11, M-12, la glorieta de Aníbal González, la avenida de las Fuerzas Armadas, la avenida de Manuel de Fraga Iribarne, la avenida de Francisco Javier de Oiza, Bet Figueras, R-2 y M-40. Según el Ayuntamiento, se prohibirá el acceso por estos puntos a quienes no tengan un destino autorizado al interior de la corona, busquen estacionamiento en zonas no habilitadas y vehículos pesados o logísticos sin acreditación.

La corona interior será un espacio de tráfico restringido y acceso controlado al entorno inmediato del recinto. Los puntos de vigilancia serán más estrictos y se encontrarán en la calle Vía de Dublín, el camino de Sintra, la vía de servicio de la M-11, la avenida de Alejandro de la Sota, la de las Fuerzas Armadas, las calles de Francisco Umbral, Antonio López Torres, Tomás Redondo, vía de los Poblados, Ribera del Sena, Ribera del Loira, la M-40, la avenida del Consejo de Europa y glorieta Don Juan de Borbón y Battemberg. A esa zona no podrán acceder “vehículos privados sin acreditación, aquellos que busquen estacionar, taxis o VTC fuera de los recorridos, vehículos de reparto sin pase, ventana horaria u autorización, vehículos de trabajadores sin acreditación y vehículos en tránsito sin destino operativo”.

En caso de elevada saturación, se podrán hacer cortes preventivos en los carriles de incorporación procedentes de los kilómetros 5, 6 y 7 de la M-40, los de incorporación desde la M-11 y al carril de incorporación de la M-12 hacia la vía de servicio de la M-11. También podría afectar ambos sentidos la avenida de las Fuerzas Armadas y hacia el barrio de las Cárcavas, así como las vías principales que comunican la zona urbana del interior de Hortaleza hacia la M-40, la avenida de los Andes y la calle de Silvano. No se descarta la ampliación de los cortes a viales cercanos.

Además, habrá una zona de protección vecinal en el barrio de las Cárcavas con puntos de control a cargo de la Policía Municipal para “preservar la tranquilidad en las áreas residenciales cercanas al circuito”. También se hará la zona próxima a la glorieta de Don Juan de Borbón y Battemberg y en el campo de golf.

Servicios especiales gratuitos en Madrid: cinco en total

La Empresa Municipal de Transportes de Madrid (EMT) pondrá en marcha cinco servicios especiales gratuitos de autobús entre el 11 y el 13 de septiembre. Los 49 autobuses previstos recorrerán las siguientes rutas:

MR1. Conectará el entorno del estadio Metropolitano (en la avenida de Arcentales) con Valdebebas (en la avenida de Alejandro de la Sota) y hará una parada en Ifema. Pasará cada cinco minutos y funcionará de las 7.30 hasta las 21.00, cuando saldrá el último bus desde Valdebebas.

MR2. Hará recorridos sin paradas intermedias entre Canillejas (en el área intermodal, entre la calle de Alcalá y la avenida de América) y la Feria de Madrid (en la Vía de Dublín, antes de la glorieta de Hamburgo) con una frecuencia de siete minutos entre las 7.30 y las 21.00.

MR3. Conectará Ifema (junto a la glorieta de Hamburgo, en la Vía de Dublín) y Valdebebas (junto a la glorieta de Antonio Perpiñá, en la avenida de Alejandro de la Sota) sin paradas intermedias. De 6.00 a 8.00 y de 20.30 a 22.00, la frecuencia será de 10 minutos. De 8.00 a 20.30, de cuatro.

MR4. Recorrerá una ruta entre la plaza de Castilla (junto al monumento a José Calvo Sotelo) y Valdebebas (junto a la glorieta de Isidro González Velázquez, en la avenida de las Fuerzas Armadas) sin paradas intermedias. Entre las 7.30 y las 21.00, cada siete minutos.

MR5. Correrá desde Ifema hasta la avenida de América en su cruce con Francisco Silvela. No hará paradas intermedias y circulará en un solo sentido. La frecuencia será de siete minutos y comenzará a operar a las 17.00.

El Ayuntamiento de Madrid ha anunciado que más de 1.000 policías municipales, que serán apoyados por 60 agentes de movilidad, participarán en el operativo. Samur-Protección Civil también enviará a 250 sanitarios que operarán 12 ambulancias, así como bicicletas, motocicletas y andarán a pie para moverse entre la multitud. Además, instalará dos puestos sanitarios avanzados en Valdebebas e Ifema.

World.title: La jueza ordena rastrear los gastos y las llamadas de Jonathan Andic en su viaje a Ecuador
World.content:
La jueza que investiga el caso Andic ordenó a los Mossos d’Esquadra, el pasado julio, un informe detallado sobre el viaje relámpago a Quito (Ecuador) en el que Jonathan Andic, investigado como presunto autor del homicidio de su padre, Isak Andic, perdió presuntamente el teléfono móvil. En un auto a cuyo contenido ha accedido EL PAÍS, la jueza Raquel Nieto ordena a la policía que averigüe los gastos con tarjeta de crédito en los que incurrió el primogénito de la familia durante el viaje, que entre la salida y el regreso a Barcelona duró apenas 48 horas. Nieto ha pedido también el registro de las llamadas telefónicas que hizo desde ese país, así como si accedió a una aplicación específica de iPhone que permite localizar el dispositivo en caso de pérdida.

El 24 de marzo de 2025, cuatro meses después de la muerte de Isak Andic tras caer desde una altura de cerca de cien metros durante una excursión a la montaña de Montserrat (Barcelona), Jonathan Andic se fue de Barcelona en un viaje con destino a Quito. Regresó apenas dos días después, el 26 de marzo. Durante su estancia, según la versión de la defensa, el teléfono le fue sustraído en una plaza pública de la capital. Jonathan, que no presentó denuncia, comunicó esa circunstancia a su secretaria en Mango.

La pérdida del móvil “en extrañas circunstancias” es uno de los siete indicios que recoge el auto de prisión provisional bajo fianza dictado por la jueza el pasado 19 de mayo, tras la detención de Jonathan Andic como sospechoso de parricidio. Después de declarar y defender su inocencia, el hijo mayor del fundador de Mango depositó el millón de euros de fianza que había solicitado la Fiscalía y quedó en libertad. En la resolución, la jueza, que hace suyas las conclusiones de los Mossos, subraya que la fecha de desaparición del terminal (un iPhone 14) “coincide con la información dada por los medios de comunicación de la reapertura del expediente judicial”.

Los investigadores sospechan que Jonathan Andic se desplazó a Quito con la intención de hacer desaparecer su terminal, o que incluso el terminal no llegó a subir al avión, de forma que los mensajes comprometedores con su padre y otros miembros de la familia quedaran a salvo. Los Mossos comprobaron que la mañana de su viaje, todavía en España, la aplicación de la Salud del teléfono móvil de Jonathan Andic no se activó en ningún momento y tampoco lo hizo ya en Ecuador, algo que jamás había ocurrido antes. Se trata de una aplicación que cuenta pasos, y que ha sido uno de los elementos clave de la investigación. Las comunicaciones entre Isak Andic y su hijo, sin embargo, constan en el sumario, puesto que se conservaban (las de los últimos diez años) en el teléfono del fundador de Mango. Algunos de esos mensajes, aunque no todos, revelan episodios de mala relación entre ambos y también cómo se sometieron a una terapia intensa y extraña para tratar de reflotarla.

Los Mossos d’Esquadra hicieron gestiones para comprobar si constaba el terminal como sustraído, pero el resultado, recordó la jueza, fue “negativo”. No podía ser de otra forma porque, como la defensa admite, Jonathan Andic jamás denunció el supuesto robo. Meses antes, el primogénito ya había solicitado el nuevo terminal, un iPhone 16, a la empresa (los directivos como él los cambian de forma periódica), pero no pasó a recogerlo y solo lo hizo una vez que se vio forzado a ello, tras perderlo en Ecuador. Los investigadores consideran que, con esa maniobra, Jonathan logró que parte del contenido del móvil fuera eliminado.

La defensa de Jonathan Andic replicó con vehemencia esa tesis. Considera que no es cierto que borrara contenido del móvil, sino que sencillamente “no se recuperó la copia de seguridad de las conversaciones de WhatsApp”; apunta además que no consta que el primogénito tuviera activadas esas copias en la aplicación de mensajería. En su escrito de apelación ante la Audiencia de Barcelona —cuya decisión, que está pendiente, ponderará la solidez de los indicios acumulados hasta ahora—, el abogado Cristóbal Martell rechazó también que se tratara de una circunstancia “extraña”. No es raro, arguyó, sufrir un hurto del móvil en una plaza de Quito, “basta acudir a fuentes abiertas sobre las estadísticas de robos y hurtos en la vía pública”.

Que el viaje fuera, efectivamente, “relámpago”, tampoco resta ni suma nada, siempre según la defensa. Es habitual que altos directivos tengan que viajar a un lugar remoto “para reuniones muy puntuales de horas, que requieren de su presencia física”. Fuentes cercanas a la familia mencionan que, en este caso, Jonathan se desplazó a Quito por un proyecto vinculado al mundo editorial. También critica la defensa la idea de que se marchara, de forma apresurada, ante las noticias aparecidas en los medios, puesto que éstas son del día 4 de marzo y el viaje no se produjo hasta veinte días más tarde. “No parece una reacción causalmente ligada a un pánico preprocesal”.

El detective contratado por la defensa, Paco Marco, también habló de ese viaje en la defensa cerrada que hizo de Jonathan Andic en una entrevista en la emisora Rac1, días después de su detención. Según los Mossos, el terminal no se conectó en Ecuador. Pero Marco rebatió esa sospecha aportando, en la emisora, un listado de llamadas que prueban, según la defensa, que el número estuvo activo y que Jonathan hizo llamadas a través de una compañía del país latinoamericano.

La jueza, en cualquier caso, ha querido aclarar por sí misma las dudas para depurar uno de los indicios que acumula una investigación en la que no hay prueba directa de lo ocurrido en Montserrat: un homicidio a ojos de la Fiscalía, un desgraciado accidente en la versión de la defensa.

World.title: Hidden weapons found near primary school in Overasselt
World.content:
Military police have found multiple weapons hidden near a primary school in Overassel following last week’s gun attack on a property in the Gelderland village, which resulted in the murder of one man and serious injury on two police officers.

Investigations have been ongoing since the attack, with 35 people arrested – all but two of whom are being held for murder or manslaughter – and extensive searches in the surrounding areas. It is suspected the attack was part of a feud over cocaine dealing linked with a resident of the village, who has been targetted before.

Police would not say how many weapons were found near the school or other details. In the day after the attack, dozens of men – who were seen heavily armed on CCTV footage – were caught hiding in the countryside, on the motorways and near rail stations as they fled the scene.

After the events unfolded, a video surfaced on social media of masked men holding automatic weapons and reading out a threat message to Jan G. Jr., the Overassel resident linked to the attack. They said he owed a “Belgian friend” 1,283 kilograms of “goods” and had to return it within 12 hours or they would kill his family.

They spoke in a heavy Spanish accent and said the goods had never left Spain as they were supposed to.

On Tuesday, Spanish police intercepted a shipment of exactly 1,283 kilograms of cocaine in a transport truck carrying coconuts. It is not yet clear whether the two cases are connected.

The shock of the attack on Overassel pushed justice minister David van Weel to warn that “unprecedented” violence is occurring due to international drugs smuggling, though he dismissed the idea of the Netherlands becoming a so-called “narco state”.

Reports of gunshots in nearby Nijmegen on Monday night drew in heavily armed police, who closed off several streets before determining no shots were fired. A relative of Jan G. Jr, who lives in the city, was moved for his own protection.

World.title: Five inburgering exam myths, tested against real exams
World.content:
A lot of people preparing for the inburgeringsexamen run into advice: “pick the longest answer”, “choose B if you are stuck”, “expect it to get harder as you go up a level”. Most of it is passed on in good faith. Almost none of it has ever been checked. Inburgeringscursus.nl coded 881 questions from 35 official exam sets – three years of the Staatsexamen NT2 plus the DUO practice exams.

Here are the myths that came up most often:

“Pick the answer with words you recognise from the text”

This is the most repeated piece of exam advice there is and it does not hold up against the data. We checked it on 288 reading questions. In four of them there was exactly one option that shared words with the text. The rest of the time it pointed at two or three answers at once.

The reason is simple once you see it. The most common wrong answer quotes the text accurately and then answers a different question. Both the right answer and the wrong ones borrow words from the passage, roughly 86% against 95%. A feature that shows up in nearly every option cannot tell them apart.

“Answer B is more often correct”

This one looked real. Across 176 items B came up more often than chance and it held up under statistical checking. So we tested it on all the available exams and there it landed at 31.7%. That is what guessing gets you.

Even if it had been true, it would not have helped. Answering B every time scores between 10 and 19 points across the six exams we measured. The pass mark is 24. It does not pass a single one. So when in doubt, choosing “B” is not the safe bet.

“The exam gets steadily harder from A2 to B1 to B2”

Half true. The half that is wrong matters if you are planning your study time.

A2 really is a different exam from B1. But B1 and B2 do not separate cleanly. The individual exams overlap, and the gap between them is relatively small.

There are two groups here, not three steps on a ladder. Moving from B1 to B2 is a smaller jump than the label suggests. Moving from A2 to B1 is the real one.

“The reading exam is the same task from start to finish”

Not true, and this is the most useful thing we found. It applies to the Staatsexamen NT2 at B1 and B2 level.

Above every reading text sits one line of instruction. Five of them say roughly the same thing: “Answer the question”. The last one says something different: “read the question first, then find the answer in the text”.

That line appeared on the final text of every exam we looked at, 34 items out of 34, across six exams at B1 and B2. And there the answer sits almost word for word in the text 47% of the time. Everywhere else it is 9%. The exam board is telling you to stop reading and start searching.

One warning. It is not the easy section. Half-correct answers appear twice as often there, 24% against 12%. In 13 of those 34 items the information you need sits in two separate articles. The difficulty moves from understanding to locating. Searching faster without checking is how you walk into it.

“KNM is mostly about Dutch customs and etiquette”

Not really. KNM covers eight themes across 40 questions, and they are nowhere near equal in size. Work and income runs to eight or nine questions. Institutions get seven. Together they are about 40% of the exam. Manners and education get three each.

This held across all official practice exams. It tells you where to start, not where to stop. Those two themes leave 60% elsewhere, and the pass mark is well above that.

Why we counted all this

Patterns like these are only useful if you can practise them. That is what Inburgeringscursus.nl is for: an online course for the inburgeringsexamen and the Staatsexamen NT2. The platform is built on this research so you practice exactly what the real exams ask of you.

It covers all five parts at A2, B1 and B2. It starts with theory on what each part asks, then you move on to practice questions that follow the real patterns and finally the mock exams. These mock exams are timed and marked on the official criteria. The practice never runs out either. You generate new questions yourself whenever you want them, on exactly the points you keep getting wrong. This way you can practise until you know you are ready instead of hoping you are.

World.title: Intelligence watchdogs warn new spy powers threaten rule of law
World.content:
Independent watchdogs responsible for monitoring the Netherlands’ secret service agencies are sounding the alarm about potential new powers that would allow them to surveil citizens far more easily with far less oversight.

The plans, which were set out by defence minister Yesilgöz recently, include allowing the domestic and military (AIVD and MIVD) intelligence services to track and collect data on anyone considered a threat without gaining prior permission.

This is intended to fight “obvious adversaries” she said, referring to foreign states like Russia and China and non-state attackers conducting cyber attacks on Dutch infrastructure.

But Hugo Hillenaar, chairman of the CTIVD, which checks whether the services have acted lawfully, has said the changes could threaten the democratic rule of law itself.

Currently the AIVD and MIVD must request permission to track individuals every three months. If the proposed changes go through, they will be able to designate entire organisations as enemies. This would extend to any other body seen to be collaborating with them, like universities.

“If a university collaborates with an organisation designated as an adversary, it is no longer separately assessed whether an investigation into, for example, an employee of that university is actually necessary,” Hillenaar told broadcaster NOS.

The watchdogs are also worried about what the law calls bulk datasets: large collections of data on many people, most of whom are not under investigation. The services can get hold of them by tapping an undersea internet cable, or by buying data that hackers have stolen and put up for sale.

“Think of the data from a national health screening programme, or from the Odido hack,” Hillenaar said. “That includes information about a great many people who have nothing to do with espionage or terrorism. You should not want that data to be used without limit in investigations, or shared with foreign intelligence services.”

The bill would also let the services run AI over a bulk dataset before anyone has decided whether the services’ own staff are allowed to look at it.

“The supervisors are really sounding the alarm,” said former AIVD officer and supervisor Bert Hubert. “I have never seen them so critical and I understand very well that they are concerned about human rights.”

World.title: Non-EU doctors face €7,000 bill for Dutch medical test
World.content:
Doctors trained in non-EU countries will have to pay more than three times as much to sit the medical test needed to practise in the Netherlands, under a draft regulation put forward by the health ministry.

The fee for the professional competence test will rise from €1,700 to €5,371.50 in March 2027, and to the full cost of running the test – just over €7,000 – a year later, the ministry says.

People already on the waiting list will have to pay the higher fee as the price is determined by the date of the exam, not the application. Non-EU trained dentists are also seeing their fees rise by almost double to help cover government expenses for organising the tests.

The ministry justifies the cost rises by saying that they will fund more test places. Currently only 72 doctors a year can take the test, which has caused waiting lists of up to two years. There are currently no places available.

Under a new contract with universities, up to 120 people will be able to take the test in 2027, cutting the waiting times by about a year.

More than 6,000 doctors and nurses from outside the EU came to the Netherlands in the past eight years, but only about 38% of doctors and 20% of nurses obtained the papers they need to work here, according to CIBG figures obtained by Trouw. Just over a third of dentists succeeded.

Candidates must first pass a Dutch language test at academic level before they can apply for the competence test, and most then work under supervision for several months before they can register.

“The route for international doctors is tough and takes a long time,” Paul Herfs of the association for foreign-trained doctors VBGA told Trouw. While waiting, he said, they cannot work as doctors, their Dutch language skills deteriorate and they can struggle with their mental health.

The number of non-EU dentists working in the Netherlands has doubled in five years, and the cabinet said in June it wants to steer refugees with medical qualifications into care jobs faster.

World.title: Setback for asset tax plan as BBB threatens to force senate vote
World.content:
The cabinet’s wealth tax reforms are in jeopardy after the farmers’ party BBB threatened to block them in the senate unless the coalition parties agree to a major overhaul.

MPs voted in favour of a new “box 3” tax on assets earlier this year, but the vote in the senate was postponed amid speculation that the centre-right coalition partners, VVD and CDA, were poised to vote against the plans in the upper house.

The cabinet wants to change the income tax system so that investors and savers are taxed on the growth of their assets each year, a system favoured by D66 and backed by VVD and CDA in the lower house.

But the two parties’ senators want to replace box 3 with a capital gains tax, which would be paid on the actual profit made from selling shares or other assets such as real estate.

Right-wing opposition parties, including the BBB and JA21, also favour this option, meaning the bill in its current form would almost certainly be voted down.

The BBB has said it will force a vote in the upper house unless finance minister Eelco Heinen withdraws the plan altogether, which would mean starting from scratch.

Withdraw or vote

“It can’t be up to the cabinet whether or not we examine a law in the Senate,” BBB senator Bart Kroon told the upper house’s finance committee. “Withdraw it or we’ll put it to the vote.”

Heinen had hoped to amend the bill as part of the current budget settlement so that it could be passed and enacted before 2028.

The finance minister has already torn up the plans once after the proposed new system attracted international criticism amid concern that investors would be forced to sell shares in order to pay tax on unrealised returns.

A new bill would not make it onto the statute book before 2029, costing the Dutch treasury an estimated €3 billion a year in lost revenue in the meantime.

The cabinet has been trying to reform the mechanism since the Supreme Court ruled in 2021 that the current system, which taxes assets based on a notional growth rate, breached European human rights laws.

Since then it has implemented a stopgap system that still taxes assets at a fictional rate but gives savers the option of declaring their actual growth rate instead. They can still pay the fictional rate if it works out lower.

World.title: Police step up campaign to stop illegal fireworks at New Year
World.content:
Dutch police say they will take a “zero tolerance” approach to illegal New Year fireworks in the first year after a ban was imposed on most types of rockets and firecrackers.

A nationwide crackdown was launched after the ban came into force on August 1, including monitoring border crossings and checking vehicles that have been used in the past to import illegal firerworks.

“One of the conditions for introducing the fireworks ban was an extensive enforcement plan,” Ko Minderhoud, national fireworks co-ordinator for the Dutch police force, told the Telegraaf.

“We have a larger team than ever ready to go and we are starting earlier.”

MPs voted to ban all fireworks apart from the lightest category, F1, which includes sparklers and Roman candles, last year following a long campaign by doctors and emergency service workers.

The annual fireworks bonanza on December 31 is the busiest night of the year for police, ambulance and fire services.

Attacks on first responders in recent years prompted centre-right parties such as VVD and CDA to change their position and accept the need for a ban, even though many voters see New Year fireworks as a national tradition.

30% have fireworks stashed

The task facing the police is a daunting one. A survey by RTL found that nearly 30% of people who regularly set off fireworks said they still have some left over from before the ban, but just 4% are willing to hand them in.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by RTL Nieuwspanel (@rtlnieuwspanel)

Just seven people turned up on the first day of an amnesty in Terneuzen on September 1 to take advantage of an offer to dispose of their fireworks anonymously without risking a fine.

The amnesty runs until October 9, with police buses touring the country to collect fireworks that are no longer permitted such as rockets and fountains.

Minderhoud said the illegal fireworks trade has been taken over in recent years by criminal gangs and increasingly resembles the drugs trade. “It’s become a sideline for classic organised criminals, because there’s a lot of money to be made,” he said.

“We see armed men transporting container loads. It was a different story a few years ago.”

He urged consumers to play their part by not buying illegal fireworks at New Year. “Set a good example and abide by the law,” he said.

“It’s also very dangerous. Look at the recent incidents at football matches. If you buy fireworks despite the ban, you’re getting involved in a murky world with very dangerous stuff.”

World.title: Two arrested after Gaza protesters spray parliament building
World.content:

Two people have been arrested after protesters sprayed “Boycot Gaza” slogans on the windows of the Dutch parliament building and interrupted the weekly ministers’ question time session.

Demonstrators twice shouted slogans from the public gallery while Geert Wilders, leader of the far-right PVV party and a staunch supporter of Israel, was speaking in parliament on Tuesday.

Access to the building was closed to visitors, but people inside were allowed to leave while some MPs slipped out via the bike parking garage.

The protest group XR Justice Now later posted a messaged on its Instagram page saying it wanted to highlight what it called Dutch “complicity” in Gaza.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JUSTICE NOW! (@xr.justicenow)

One of the demonstrators shouted “blood on your hands” and “Free Palestine” as they were being led away during Wilders’ speech.

Parliamentary chairman Thom van Campen suspended the sitting after the second interruption and ordered the gallery to be cleared before the debate resumed.

World.title: Everyone’s tax bill is falling, except the top 10%: CBS
World.content:
The share of income going on income tax has fallen for all income groups over the past ten years, except for the top 10% of earners, according to the national statistics office CBS. The top tier pays 24.9% of its income in tax, while the very lowest pays nothing.

The typical household paid 12.3% of its gross income in income tax and national insurance contributions in 2024, down from 15.4% in 2011.

The figures do not include VAT, which hits the poorest hardest, or pension and unemployment insurance premiums. Including all taxes and premiums, the typical household paid 32.3% in 2024, against 35.2% in 2011.

The figures also don’t say anything about purchasing power. Consumer prices are more than a fifth higher than in 2021, and inflation was 3.3% in August, driven by rising energy costs.

Low earners

The highest earners paid 24.9% in 2024, slightly more than the 24.7% they paid in 2014. Every other group is paying less.

The biggest drop was for low earners. The second-poorest 10% of households now pay 2.3% of their income in tax, down from 6.7% in 2014. CBS said the employment tax credit was raised substantially over the period, particularly for lower incomes.

“You see a levelling trend here,” CBS chief economist Peter Hein van Mulligen told the Telegraaf. Whether income inequality has fallen as a result cannot be read from these figures alone, he said, and other CBS data show it has stayed broadly stable.

Singles pay most, self-employed more

Couples with two incomes pay far less than anyone else on the same income. On a household income of around €100,000, a couple with two salaries pays 11.9% in tax, a couple with one salary pays 19.4% and a single person pays 22.5%.

The self-employed are the only group paying more than a decade ago, up from 13.4% to 15.6%.

World.title: Polish school pupils second best at maths in EU
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish schoolchildren are the second best in the European Union at mathematics, the third best at reading comprehension, and the fifth best at science, according to the latest results from a major international study of pupils’ abilities. The Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) is carried out every three years by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and measures the performance of 15-year-olds. The latest instalment, based on tests taken in 2025, was published on Tuesday this week. It includes results from 91 countries and territories across the world. A total of 760,000 pupils were assessed, including 7,103 in 217 Polish schools. In maths, Polish pupils obtained a mean score of 484, which was the 12th highest in the world. The top seven places were taken by Asian countries and territories. But the only other European Union country to exceed Poland’s score was Estonia (508). Poland was just behind the United Kingdom (488) and Canada (485), but ahead of the likes of Finland (469), Germany (464) and the United States (463). In reading comprehension, Poland’s mean score of 482 was 14th in the world and third best in the EU, behind Ireland (500) and Estonia (499). Polish pupils performed slightly worse, in relative terms, in science, where their mean score of 495 was 18th in the world and fifth best in the EU. A number of Polish media outlets and Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrongly reported that Poland was third best in the EU for science. In fact, it was significantly behind Estonia (527) and Finland (504) and marginally below Ireland (500) and Austria (497). Poland’s latest results continue its recent history of performing strongly in PISA. In the 2018 instalment, Polish pupils were the third best in the EU in both maths and science, and fourth best in reading. In 2022 (when PISA took place a year later than planned due to the Covid pandemic), Poland was fourth in the EU in maths and fifth in both science and reading. In 2021, a separate assessment of reading comprehension among fourth-grade pupils – called PIRLS and carried out every five years by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement – found Poland had the joint best result among EU countries, equal with Finland Following the announcement of the new PISA data, Polish education minister Barbara Nowacka welcomed the fact that “Poland has maintained its high ranking among European Union countries”. However, she added a note of caution, pointing to the fact that, overall, test scores have been declining, both in Poland and globally. That shows “Polish education still has a lot of work ahead of it”. Nowacka said that her ministry’s efforts to reform the school curriculum had been based on results and recommendations from previous PISA reports. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has signed an agreement for a further $4 billion (14.8 billion zloty) from the United States Foreign Military Financing (FMF) programme, which provides grants and loans to fund the purchase of American military equipment. Defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called the development a “great honour”, because FMF is “granted only to the best allies”. The agreement is not only “another important step in the modernisation of the Polish armed forces” but also “strengthens the strategic partnership between Poland and the US”. The US embassy in Warsaw likewise hailed the agreement as “reaffirming the strength of the US-Poland partnership as we work together to strengthen NATO, deter aggression, and support peace and security in Europe”. .@UnderSecT took part in the signing of a $4 billion Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan guarantee—an important step in U.S.-Polish security cooperation. Poland’s significant investments in its defense capabilities and the U.S. defense industrial base reflect our shared… pic.twitter.com/Dz3huAp8pj — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) September 9, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has embarked on an unprecedented military procurement spree, with its defence budget rising to the highest relative level in NATO. Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was also the largest importer of arms in NATO. Around 44% of those purchases came from the US, including Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence batteries, and HIMARS rocket artillery. The new agreement marks the sixth time Poland has received funds through FMF, for a total of almost $20 billion. Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the latest financing would be used to “accelerate the implementation of existing contracts, including for Apache helicopters”. In 2024, Poland signed a $10 billion deal to buy 96 AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, along with a logistics and training package and a stockpile of ammunition and spare parts. It will make Poland the second-largest operator of Apaches in the world, after only the US itself. Thomas DiNanno, the US under secretary of state for arms control and international security, said that the new agreement “signifies our commitment to assistance, but also Poland’s commitment to ensuring security, building defence capabilities, and ensuring the security of NATO’s eastern flank”. “Poland is not only a trusted partner; it is not only an ally on the front line; it is a model ally of the United States,” he added, repeating recent remarks by US defence secretary Pete Hegseth. The terms of the financing have not been revealed, but Marta Postuła, vice president of Poland’s national development bank, BGK, through which the funds will be channelled, said it was “on more favourable terms than the last two [FMF] loan guarantee agreements”. This, she added, was “due to the subsidisation of a portion of the financing costs through a grant awarded for this purpose by the US government”. 💬 Obecna umowa została zawarta na korzystniejszych warunkach niż dwie poprzednie umowy z gwarancjami pożyczkowymi dzięki subsydiowaniu części kosztów finansowania w ramach grantu przyznanego w tym celu przez Rząd USA. To kolejny wyraz bardzo bliskiej, transatlantyckiej… pic.twitter.com/Ipd4cYDeFo — Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego 🇵🇱 (@BGK_pl) September 9, 2026 The issue of who Poland should buy military equipment from, and how such purchases should be funded, has become embroiled in domestic political disputes this year. President Karol Nawrocki and the right-wing opposition with which he is aligned have criticised the government for signing Poland up to the EU’s SAFE programme, which is providing €43.7 billion (188.7 billion zloty) in loans for defence and security spending. They argue that provisions requiring most of the money to be spent within Europe itself could damage Poland’s relations with the US and South Korea, who have in recent years been the main sources of military procurement. However, speaking today, Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the new loan agreement with the US shows that SAFE and FMF “do not compete with one another; they complement one another”. Amerykański sprzęt wojskowy ponownie wzmocni Wojsko Polskie i bezpieczeństwo Polaków! Właśnie zabezpieczyliśmy środki w wysokości 4 mld dolarów, czyli prawie 15 mld zł na jego zakup. Łącznie w ramach amerykańskiego programu Foreign Military Financing pozyskaliśmy już blisko 20… pic.twitter.com/hhzXcE1hoC — Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) September 9, 2026 While Nawrocki is a close ally of President Donald Trump, who endorsed him ahead of last year’s Polish presidential elections, the more liberal government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, has at times clashed with Washington. In May this year, the sudden and unexpected cancellation of the rotational deployment of almost 4,000 US troops to Poland raised concern in Warsaw. Shortly afterwards, Trump declared that he would deploy 5,000 additional troops to Poland. However, since then, no clear details of that plan have been announced, although Poland has formally submitted a request for the US to establish a new permanent US military base on its territory. On Wednesday morning, Polish deputy defence minister Paweł Bejda told broadcaster TVP that an American delegation was in Poland this week to visit potential locations for the base and discuss the issue further. World.title: “We remember where Germany in the hands of a far-right, pro-Russian party can lead,” says Polish FM
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s foreign minister has expressed concern over the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party at a time when Germany is rapidly rearming – suggesting that it has echoes of the build-up to World War Two. “We want Germany, under democratic leadership and as Europe’s largest economy, to play a strong role in ensuring our common security,” Radosław Sikorski told German newspaper Handelsblatt. “But we remember all too well where a rearmed Germany in the hands of a far-right, pro-Russian party can lead – and that is precisely what the AfD represents,” he added. Polens Außenminister Sikorski: „Wir wollen, dass Deutschland (…) eine starke Rolle bei der Sicherung unserer gemeinsamen Sicherheit spielt. Aber wir erinnern uns nur allzu gut daran, wohin ein wiederbewaffnetes Deutschland in den Händen einer rechtsextremen, prorussischen Partei führen kann (…)“ [image or embed] — Andreas Prause (@andreas-prause.eu) 8 September 2026 at 21:05 Poland was, on 1 September 1939, invaded by Nazi Germany, marking the start of World War Two and over five years of brutal occupation. The attack was launched in cooperation with the Soviet Union, which invaded Poland from the east two weeks later. After Hitler was defeated, Germany had no major far-right party for decades. However, that has changed in recent years. In 2024, the AfD came first in the Thuringian state election, with 33% of the vote. Last Sunday, it won in Saxony-Anhalt, with 44%. The party also came second in the federal elections of 2025, with 21%, making it the main national opposition. Opinion polls now show that the AfD is the most popular party nationally, with support of around 28%, well ahead of Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU), on 21%. The AfD’s growth has been watched with particular concern in Poland, a country that suffered enormously under Nazi-German occupation. Some senior AfD figures have sought to downplay the significance of the Nazi era. In 2025, when the German parliament approved plans for a memorial in Berlin to Polish victims of World War Two, the AfD was the only party not to vote in favour. The AfD’s sympathy towards and links with Russia have caused further disquiet in Poland. Last year, AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla said he “does not see any current threat to Germany from Russia” and that, in fact, “Poland could also be a threat to us”. This year, another senior AfD figure, Kay Gottschalk, called for Poland to pay his country €1.3 billion as reparations for its “complicity” in the sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines that used to bring Russian gas to Germany through the Baltic Sea but were damaged by explosions in 2022. Germany’s parliament has passed a motion calling on the government to establish a permanent memorial in Berlin to Polish victims of the German-Nazi occupation. The measure was supported by all parties apart from the far-right AfD https://t.co/8dk0ZSpmjJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 3, 2025 In the wake of the AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that “only idiots or traitors” in Poland would celebrate an AfD victory. He claimed there were some such people in Law and Justice (PiS) and Confederation (Konfederacja), the two main right-wing opposition parties. However, PiS’s reaction to AfD’s rise has been mixed. On Tuesday, PiS MP Małgorzata Golińska told Polskie Radio that it represents a “kind of browning” of politics in Germany – a reference to the brown shirts of Hitler’s SA paramilitary forces that helped bring him to power in the 1920s and 1930s. “A return to very dangerous thinking is taking place there and we must observe in which direction it will all develop,” added Golińska. “From Poland’s perspective, we should not overreact with any particular emotion, but we also cannot be naive [in thinking] that nothing is happening there.” By contrast, another PiS MP, Jarosław Sellin, told Onet Radio that PiS and the AfD “say similar things” when it comes to EU climate and migration policies. But he added that “this does not mean we have to like what the AfD says about history, relations with Poland, and Russia”. Polish PM @donaldtusk has condemned as “idiots or traitors” right-wing opposition figures who have welcomed the far-right AfD's election victory in Germany However, the response from the Polish right to the election result has so far been relatively muted https://t.co/goSWlbeGA8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 7, 2026 Responses from Confederation have likewise been mixed. The group is actually made up of two main factions, one of which, a libertarian party called New Hope (Nowa Nadzieja), is allied with the AfD in the European Parliament. New Hope’s spokesman, Wojciech Machulski, told the Fakt daily that they are “united [with AfD] in our opposition to EU migration and climate policies” but at the same time “we do not accept the anti-Polish statements”. Krzysztof Mulawa, an MP from the National Movement (RN), which makes up the other half of Confederation, told the newspaper that “several of the AfD’s demands are unacceptable from the Polish perspective”. But he said that there were areas of shared interest, such as abolishing the euro. A number of figures from PiS and Confederation have also expressed hope that the AfD’s rise at the expense of establishment parties can herald a similar development in Poland, which, like Germany, is ruled by a pro-EU coalition ranging from centre-left to centre-right. Europa się budzi, a establishment wpada w panikę. Wynik AfD pokazuje, że ludzie mają dość dyktatu Brukseli, Zielonego Ładu i niszczenia państw narodowych przez nielegalną imigrację. Polityczne trzęsienie ziemi dopiero się zaczyna. Piękna, biała Europa narodów wkrótce powróci. — Włodzimierz Skalik (@Wlodek_Skalik) September 7, 2026 One party that has been unambiguously positive in its response to AfD’s victory is the Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), a radical-right, pro-Russian group that broke away from Confederation last year and is currently polling support of around 9% “Europe is waking up, and the establishment is falling into panic,” wrote KKP’s deputy leader, Włodzimierz Skalik, on social media. “A beautiful, white Europe of nations will soon return.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Robots “protest” in Warsaw to demand regulation of AI and automation
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Around 30 robots protested outside Poland’s digital affairs ministry on Monday, calling for tougher regulation of artificial intelligence and robotisation. The human organisers say there needs to be greater public debate over the impact of new technologies on the labour market. Digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski met with the demonstrators, telling them that his department is working on regulations. However, one of the organisers said that plans currently being discussed by parliament contain insufficient protection for workers. Around 30 robots joined a protest in front of Poland’s digital affairs ministry, calling for stronger AI regulations. The demonstration was organised by campaigners to spark debate on how AI and robots could replace workers. pic.twitter.com/QEbvchb2RS — Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) September 7, 2026 Standing in several rows, the robots waved Polish flags and chanted slogans such as “We want regulations, we want rules, we want law” and “Don’t wait, regulate, protect jobs”. The organisers, a group called Democratism, said the event was intended to highlight the need for debate and legislation before automation has a more profound impact on employment. “Some people will benefit from new opportunities, while others may need to retrain or adapt to completely different roles,” they wrote. Society needs to discuss “who is responsible for preparing people for these changes, how workers should be protected during the transition and how reskilling should work”. Democratism appears to have been launched shortly before the protest, with the announcement about the demonstration among the first material published on its social media accounts. The initiative was launched by Delta Robots, a company that rents robots for events. However, a website they have set up to gather support for greater debate over the impact of AI and robotisation has so far only obtained signatures from 61 people. Grzegorz Kuliś of Delta Robots admitted to news website Gazeta.pl that their “campaign also has public relations value” for the company. However, he added that, “even though we’re deploying robots, we’re also humans, and we have a whole host of concerns that, if we don’t regulate this, we’ll soon find ourselves in an unprecedented situation that no human being will be able to cope with”. “We are constantly debating the impact of migrants on our society, whilst the vast majority of ‘migrants’ will arrive either via undersea cables across the Atlantic in the form of AI agents, or as humanoid robots in shipping containers from China,” he warned. Gawkowski, who went out to address the organisers, said the ministry’s objectives were aligned with the protesters’ concerns. “People come first, and that is what matters most to us,” he said, quoted by broadcaster Eska. The minister also announced plans to establish a committee on AI development and safety as well as to introduce so-called sandboxes, where companies will be able to test AI solutions before deploying them more widely, reports local news website O!Polska. Kuliś, however, told Gazeta.pl that a draft law on AI systems currently being considered by the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament, contains too little practical protection for workers affected by automation. A Polish radio station that launched a channel run almost entirely by AI – including its presenters – has decided to end the project after less than a week The head of the station admitted they were "surprised by the level of emotion" the idea had caused https://t.co/9iMlRVamSF — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 28, 2024 The rapid development of AI and robotics has sparked debate around the world on how such technologies will impact humans, including to what extent and in what ways they will replace human labour. However, a number of recent reports have found that the impact of AI on jobs has so far been smaller than many previously predicted. Analysis by the Institute of Economic Policy Research at Stanford University, published in July, found that “AI’s effects on overall employment are likely small”. A further concern has been the prospect of AI “going rogue” by starting to act without or beyond human control. Those fears were strengthened after it emerged in July this year that some of OpenAI’s AI agents had autonomously hacked Hugging Face, another AI company. The incident prompted more than 100 companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Hugging Face, to sign an open letter calling on companies and governments to step up cybersecurity efforts amid emerging threats. A recent rise in unemployment in Poland has raised concern. But that headline figure does not tell the whole story, with experts arguing that the Polish labour market is actually in good shape, writes @AlicjaPtak4 https://t.co/Pk4y7BqGrs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 24, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. The candidate of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), one of Poland’s main political groups, has been disqualified from Kraków’s mayoral election after over 2,000 of the signatures from local residents collected in support of his candidacy were found to be invalid. One of Confederation’s leaders, Sławomir Mentzen, admitted that the situation was an “embarrassment” and “catastrophe”. He responded by dismissing the candidate, Bartosz Bocheńczak, as head of his party’s local structures in Kraków and launching an investigation into how the blunder occurred. Podobnie jak i wielu naszych działaczy, wolontariuszy, sympatyków i wyborców, czuję się bardzo zawiedziony brakiem rejestracji kandydatury Bartosza Bocheńczaka w Krakowie. Przyczyną braku rejestracji było to, że spośród około 5000 zebranych podpisów, ponad 2000 były błędnych.… — Sławomir Mentzen (@SlawomirMentzen) September 7, 2026 Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, is holding a mayoral election this month after the previous incumbent, Aleksander Miszalski, was removed mid-term in a rare recall referendum earlier this year. Over a dozen potential candidates announced plans to stand. But, in order to be registered, they had to collect at least 3,000 signatures from residents of the city supporting their candidacy, then submit them to the municipal electoral commission by 3 September. Twelve candidates made such submissions, after which the commission began assessing all signatures to ensure that each candidate had at least 3,000 that were valid. On Monday, reports began to emerge that, although Bocheńczak had submitted just over 4,600 signatures, the commission had found that fewer than 3,000 of them were valid. That evening, the candidate himself confirmed the news. Mentzen, who is leader of the far-right libertarian New Hope (Nowa Nadzieja) party that makes up one half of Confederation, revealed that over 2,000 signatories had listed their address as their place of residence rather than where they are officially registered as living. In Poland, it is common for people to live somewhere different from where they are officially registered. That is particularly the case for young people, who are often registered at their parents’ address while residing elsewhere. Confederation is particularly popular among young people, and Kraków has a large student population. Moja kandydatura na Prezydenta Krakowa nie została zarejestrowana. Zabrakło ważnych podpisów. Nie będę snuł teorii spiskowych, szukał winnych ani przerzucał odpowiedzialności na kogokolwiek. Uważałem, że złożenie niemal 5000 podpisów zapewni nam wystarczający margines… — Bartosz Bocheńczak (@BBochenczak) September 7, 2026 Mentzen said that the regulations regarding collecting signatures for candidates are “absurd”, yet admitted that Bocheńczak’s campaign should have done a better job of complying with the rules. There must now be “consequences from this embarrassment”, said Mentzen, who announced that Bocheńczak had been dismissed as New Hope’s local leader in Kraków and that a party commission would “determine responsibility for this disaster”. Confederation also faced scrutiny last year when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected its financial report for the 2024 European elections after it found irregularities. The party also failed to submit the required documents on time. As a result, it lost access to state subsidies. The Supreme Court has rejected an appeal by the far-right Confederation against the electoral commission's decision to reject its financial report for last year's European elections due to irregularities. The group will now lose access to state subsidies https://t.co/hNGu2Zvzii — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 14, 2025 Bocheńczak is not the only candidate who has struggled with collecting signatures. Last week, just days before the deadline, it emerged that over 3,000 signatures collected in support of the favourite in the elections, Łukasz Gibała, an independent, were invalid because the word “Kraków” was missing from the form. Gibała – a perennial candidate in mayoral elections who finished runner-up to Miszalski in 2024 – quickly scrambled to collect more signatures, and his team managed to gather an additional 9,000 in three days. On Monday this week, it also emerged that three other independent candidates, Marian Banaś, Stanisław Kułach and Marta Ratuszyńska, had failed to gather enough signatures. All three have taken up their right to appeal against the commission’s decision to reject their candidacies. Dziś złożymy dodatkowe podpisy do komisji wyborczej – ponad 9 tysięcy (oprócz wcześniejszych 5,5 tys.). Skala Waszego zaangażowania i pomocy była bezprecedensowa – w 3 dni zebraliśmy więcej podpisów niż którykolwiek z naszych rywali przez 3 tygodnie 💪 Bardzo Wam dziękuję i… — Łukasz Gibała (@LukaszGibala) September 3, 2026 Six candidates have so far been accepted, including Gibała; Monika Piątkowska, who is supported by the centrist Civil Coalition (KO) and Polish People’s Party (PSL); Michał Drewnicki of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS); Aleksandra Owca of the left-wing Together (Razem); and Michał Klimek of the radical-right Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP). Two candidates, Daria Gosek-Popiołek of The Left (Lewica) and Sławomir Pietrzyk of Social Democracy of Poland (Socjaldemokracja Polska), are still awaiting confirmation from the electoral commission that they submitted enough valid signatures. A decision is due to be announced today. The first round of the election will take place on Sunday 27 September. If any candidate receives over 50% of the vote, they will become mayor. If not, a run-off between the top two candidates will take place on 11 October. There has been little polling on support for candidates, but one survey by the Opinia24 agency for Polityka Insight two weeks ago showed Gibała with 25.2%, ahead of Piątkowska (15.3%) and Gosek-Popiołek (8.7%). Bocheńczak was in sixth with just 3.2%. Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland wants the European Union to deny the right to asylum for migrants who cross EU borders in organised, aggressive groups, just as Poland has itself done on its border with Belarus. “This is about depriving people who illegally cross the border in organised groups, using violence or destroying border security measures, of the right to international protection,” Maciej Duszczyk, the deputy interior minister who oversees migration policy, told broadcaster RMF. Polska zabiega o to, by Unia Europejska przyjęła jej interpretację przepisów dotyczących ochrony międzynarodowej. „Chodzi o pozbawienie prawa do ochrony międzynarodowej osób, które nielegalnie przekraczają granicę w zorganizowanych grupach, z użyciem przemocy albo niszcząc… — Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) September 6, 2026 The station reports that, at a meeting of the European Council next month, Poland will propose expanding the interpretation of article 33 of the United Nations’ Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees. That section outlines the principle of “refoulement”, under which states are barred from expelling or returning refugees to places where their life or freedom would be threatened. The article includes a clause saying that the principle does not apply if “there are reasonable grounds for regarding [a refugee] as a danger to the security of the country” in which they have arrived, or if they have a criminal conviction that makes them “a danger to the community of that country”. Poland wants that clause to be applied in situations where someone applies for asylum after being part of an organised and aggressive border crossing. Since last year, Poland has itself banned asylum claims from people who illegally cross the border from Belarus. Since 2021, the Belarusian authorities have encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants, mainly from Asia and Africa, to try to irregularly – and often aggressively – enter the EU. Poland’s asylum ban, which has exceptions for certain vulnerable categories of people, was introduced as a temporary measure in March 2025 but has been repeatedly renewed since then. Warsaw now wants a similar interpretation of international refugee law to be applied across the EU Its proposals come in the wake of July’s incident in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, where tens of thousands of migrants irregularly entered from Morocco. Soon afterwards, Poland urged the EU to adopt tougher measures, including making migrants who enter the bloc illegally ineligible for obtaining residence rights. Prime Minister Donald Tusk was also one of 22 EU leaders who signed a letter expressing “serious concern” at the situation in Ceuta and warning that the EU “cannot allow uncontrolled mass border crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration, or other hybrid threats to create the impression that illegal entry…is possible”. After last week's migration crisis in Ceuta, Poland has called for tougher EU measures, including an automatic ban on residence for anyone who enters illegally. It pointed to its own experience of dealing with "weaponised" migration from Belarus https://t.co/2VHn5ZUJx7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 5, 2026 Poland has long argued that the situation on the Belarus border is an example of how migration has been “weaponised” by Russia and its allies to sow social discord in EU countries. In response, Poland has invested billions in strengthening physical and electronic barriers along the border, has deployed thousands of additional officers there (and granted them expanded rights to use firearms), and has banned asylum claims. In 2021, Poland recorded almost 40,000 attempted illegal crossings from Belarus, and the figure remained as high as 30,000 in 2025. However, in the first half of this year, only 235 attempted crossings were recorded, which the Polish government has hailed as evidence of the success of its tough measures. However, Poland’s human rights commission recently raised concern at how long the technically “temporary” asylum ban has been in place. Some Polish courts have also ruled that Polish border guards acted unlawfully when forcing migrants back into Belarus. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
