NEW DELHI: When the 'Flying Kremlin' and other ultra-secure aircraft touch down in Delhi this weekend, they won't just bring Russian President Vladimir Putin and other high-profile world leaders to the Brics Summit, they will land with a fully autonomous fortress-on-wheels featuring personal food-testing labs, decoy dignitaries and armoured limousines built to survive landmines and chemical attacks.As Delhi transforms into an impenetrable, multi-layered defensive grid, security personnel are bracing for a high-stakes security operation where AI-aimed snipers scan rooftops, gesture-recognition cameras spot human posture shifts, commandos slither down ropes from hovering helicopters and anti-graffiti strike teams patrol the streets 24/7, guarding against everything from high-tech threats to stealth protest tactics.The capital, sources said, hasn't seen security this tight since the 2023 G20 summit, and preparations this time are even more extensive. Unmanned aerial vehicles have been categorised as one of the most potent threats, and systems that can jam drone signals or shoot them down have been installed at several locations.Every dignitary or their hotel or carcade has been assigned a code name or call sign to ensure they are guided smoothly between locations without any overlap or security glitches.Intelligence inputs have hinted at the possibility of flash protests and spray-painting of inflammatory slogans near the venues, targeting some foreign leaders. Cops have formed anti-graffiti teams for round-the-clock patrolling to thwart any such attempts.President Putin's security grid comprises a sophisticated protective shield managed jointly by Russia's Federal Protective Service (FSO) and Indian counter-terrorism forces. Ground mobility will be centred around his custom-made, heavily armoured Aurus Senat limousine, often referred to as a "rolling bunker". Transported directly from Moscow, the state car is built to withstand chemical attacks, landmines and sniper fire, complete with run-flat tyres and an independent emergency oxygen supply.Up in the air, the Russian leader travels in a specially modified Ilyushin IL-96-300PU aircraft, known as the "Flying Kremlin", which operates alongside decoy jets, advanced missile-defence countermeasures and secure command systems. On the ground, the innermost protective layer comprises elite officers from Russian Presidential Security Service (SBP), supported by advanced FSO teams that sanitise every scheduled and potential itinerary venue. The Russian delegation manages its own strict logistics, travelling with personal chefs, portable testing laboratories for food and drink, and measures to collect biological waste, alongside deploying dummy dignitaries in select hotels to boost operational security.Securing the designated summit hotels in central Delhi, Aerocity and Gurgaon presented one of the most formidable logistical challenges for intelligence and law enforcement agencies. Every hotel is being managed as an independent secure zone under its assigned DCP venue commander, supervised by special commissioner-rank officers overseeing broader zones.Within each hotel, two rooms have been repurposed into operational command posts: a primary security control room linked directly to Delhi Police's central C4i command node and a secondary contingency room dedicated to emergency management.To prevent unauthorised access, advanced AI cameras equipped with posture-detection and intrusion-alert software monitor perimeter walls and hallways, capable of flagging unusual physical movements like crawling or wall-scaling. Hotel staff have undergone rigorous multi-round background checks conducted by special branch and special cell, with movement restricted strictly to assigned floors using specially programmed digital keycards.

World.title: Cyber fraud worth 5,044 crore prevented: Govt
World.content: NEW DELHI: India is increasingly stopping cyber fraud before money leaves a victim's account. A telecom-led risk system has helped banks and payment platforms prevent suspected fraudulent transactions worth Rs 5,043.7 crore in 15 months, govt said, marking a shift from tracing stolen money to intercepting payments in real time, reports Aabhas Sharma.The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), launched by the department of telecommunications in May 2025, assigns mobile numbers medium, high or very high risk ratings. The alerts are fed directly to banks and UPI platforms, allowing them to warn customers or block risky payments.Experts said the system's biggest achievement was making fraud operations costlier.However, fraudsters could turn to SIMs obtained through fraudulent KYC or virtual numbers. An expert said criminals could also evade mobile-number risk scores by obtaining fresh or "aged" SIM cards.

World.title: Kolkata’s Cheenapara Heritage Gallery preserves the city’s 248-year-old Chinese history
World.content:
The newly inaugurated Cheenapara Heritage Gallery sits on Kolkata’s Blackburn Lane alongside the hum of Central Avenue, in the deep folds of Tiretta Bazar. It shares a wall with the old Chinese restaurant Sei Vui.

Inside, under warm yellow lights, objects from Kolkata’s Chinese past fill the rooms. Outside, September rain draws a grey curtain across the afternoon.

Between the two is a portrait, more than five feet tall, of Sun Yat-sen — physician, revolutionary and founder of the Republic of China. A street near Tiretta Bazar’s Poddar Court is named after him.

On September 5, the glass over his portrait caught the shifting reflections of visitors and members of Kolkata’s Chinese community as they moved through the gallery. In this old Chinatown, where a community’s history survives in street names, restaurants and memory, the image was difficult to miss: the present moving across the face of the past.

A building that remembers

The building had been holding memories long before it became a gallery. At 17 Blackburn Lane stands the Huining Huiguan, a native-place association and temple established in 1908 by Chinese migrants from Sihui, or Sei Vui, and neighbouring Guangning in Guangdong province. Its name brings the two ancestral places together.

A huiguan could be a hostel, guild hall, temple and meeting place. For newly-arrived migrants, it offered a bed, a newspaper, financial help, familiar speech and familiar gods. More than a century later, one part of the old association houses Sei Vui restaurant. Another now holds the Cheenapara Heritage Gallery.

Tansen Sen, professor of History and director, Centre for Global Asia at NYU Shanghai, believes the building itself explains why Tiretta Bazar cannot be reduced to the convenient phrase “old Chinatown”. The temple inside belongs to a religious tradition associated with a particular part of Guangdong and is unlike other Chinese temples in India.

“This place used to be a club where people who migrated from the Guangdong region stayed. Sei Vui is the place where the Chinese migrants who built this place came from,” says the professor. Looking ahead to 2028, when Kolkata marks 250 years of its association with the Chinese community, Tansen says that the aim is to create a similar gallery in Tangra’s Chinatown.

The lives inside ordinary things

The history of the community survives in objects that might otherwise seem unremarkable. Wooden chairs, vases, cymbals, incense sticks, sauce bottles, mahjong sets, abacuses, tools used by people who worked with their hands and built their lives in a new city.

Placed together, these objects begin to speak.

“The exhibition looks at the multiple waves of migration through the 1800s and then moves into economic specialisation. Different Chinese communities that came to the city began specialising in particular trades,” says Sohini Pyne, who designed and curated the exhibition. Those trades gave Chinese Calcutta a distinct economic geography.

Cantonese migrants became closely associated with carpentry. Hakka families with shoemaking and, later, the tanneries of Tangra. Migrants from Hubei with dentistry. Those from Shandong with the silk trade. Laundries, beauty parlours and restaurants cut across some of these divisions.

By the 1950s, more than 300 Cantonese carpenters were working on ships at the Hooghly docks. More than 20 Cantonese-owned carpentry factories operated in Calcutta.

A shoe-making implement inside the gallery is therefore more than an old tool. It belongs to a city where stretches of central Calcutta were lined with Chinese shoe businesses.

An abacus recalls shops and workshops where accounts were kept by hand.

Finding a place in the city

The associations helped hold the community together. Migrants arriving from the same regions of China formed native-place organisations. These could contain a temple, a school and spaces for social life. Huining Huiguan was one among several such associations in the city.

“When the Chinese came from their native places on the mainland, they formed associations here. These could have a temple and sometimes a school. They became important institutions for the community,” says Sohini.

Tansen hopes the Blackburn Lane gallery will eventually become one chapter in a larger archive scattered across Kolkata. There are about seven such associations, he says, each carrying a different history. Tangra tells another story one of tanneries, leather and restaurants, shaped particularly by its Hakka community.

“We hoped that each of these clubs, including those in Tangra, would have these galleries or museums in it. The Tangra Chinese community has its own historical aspect,” says Tansen

Names brought back to life

Some histories in Cheenapara had been present all along but remained unread by much of the city.

Chinese inscriptions survive within the association and temple. With the help of scholars, several have now been translated. The exhibition also contains rubbings from temple inscriptions, including a donation record whose names can once again be read.

“We have religious objects, but also objects from daily life. Together they allow us to look at different aspects of Chinese life here,” notes Sohini.

Before Chinatown became a memory

Kolkata’s Chinese history is commonly traced to Yang Dazhao, better known as Atchew, the Chinese trader who received land near Budge Budge from Warren Hastings in 1778. He established a sugar mill there and brought Chinese workers to Bengal. The settlement that grew around it became Achipur.

Research, however, indicates that the Chinese were already present in Bengal before Atchew. The familiar description of him as the first Chinese settler is therefore more complicated than it first appears.

Successive migrations created a community that, by the middle of the 20th Century, was woven into the working life of Calcutta.

Chinese carpenters worked for shipping and railway companies before establishing workshops of their own. Shoemakers built businesses around Bentinck Street. Dentists practised across the city. Laundries multiplied during the 1940s and 1950s.

Restaurants would eventually become the community’s most visible legacy, even as many of its other occupations faded from public memory.

Then came 1962. The India-China war tore through much of this social and economic world.

Chinese Indians were interned or deported. Dockworkers lost jobs on security grounds. Businesses closed. Many families later left India for North America, Europe, Australia and elsewhere.

Restaurateur Miranda Liu, whose family is associated with Beijing and Tung Fong, remembers the period as the beginning of the great thinning out. Families left in search of work and security. Today, Miranda estimates Kolkata’s Chinese population at roughly 2,000.

A neighbourhood still alive

The gallery is not trying to recreate a vanished Chinatown behind glass. Its photographs resist that temptation.

The final section moves between festivals and ordinary life: streets, people and moments in Cheenapara recorded across decades.

“These are extremely evocative photographs,” says Sohini of the images clicked by photographer Bijoy Chowdhury who is associated with the community for more than 50 years. Some are photographs of festivals in Cheenapara, but others show regular, normal, everyday life in this part of the city.

Chen Yaohua, president of the Huining Huiguan, helped execute the project from within the community.

Its ambitions, however, extend beyond Blackburn Lane. Sohini hopes the gallery will prompt other communities to look at what they have inherited before the objects, and the stories attached to them, disappear.

At the inauguration, Barun Ray, Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Tourism, described turning into Blackburn Lane and feeling as though he had “gone back in history, gone back in time”. He also assured the community of the government’s support for initiatives that preserve the neighbourhood as a living experience.

The gallery shows you what remains: the heat and noise of Sei Vui’s kitchens, incense burning in the temple, the worn halls of the Chinese community and visitors moving across Sun Yat-sen’s face in the glass.

World.title: ‘Rahman wants to visit India, but agenda has to be set first’
World.content:
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is keen to visit India at the earliest but is concerned about take away points and achievements that he will have to produce before his audience back home after a visit of this nature, said a diplomatic source of Bangladesh to The Hindu on Wednesday (September 9, 2026)

The official said that Prime Minister Rahman might have skipped the multilateral BRICS summit for which he was invited by India, but that does not mean that he is trying to avoid an immediate and important neighbour like India which has contributed and sacrificed immensely during Bangladesh’s Liberation War of 1971. PM Rahman is aware that he may have to visit Delhi in a bilateral framework by November or early December, as the Ganga Water Treaty needs to be renewed at the earliest as it will otherwise lapse by the end of December, said the official.

Also Read | The trust deficit in India-Bangladesh ties

The official said that Mr. Rahman’s visit requires setting of the agenda through intensive meetings between the officials of the two sides that are yet to begin. But Dhaka believes that apart from the Ganga Water Treaty which is a “rolling achievement” as it is expected to be renewed after having survived for 30 years, there is a need to look at other areas where the bilateral relationship is stuck.

“For example, in case of restarting full scale visa facilities, lifting of trade restrictions that were imposed during the interim government in Dhaka, and usage of land ports, and restarting of full scale commercial relationship are some of the areas where there is possibility of setting up some solid goals for achievement,” said the official.

He also pointed out that one area where India could send a positive message is in the field of energy as Bangladesh is suffering from an acute crunch in energy supply. “It will be a confidence building measure if India can assist Bangladesh in dealing with this challenge,” said the official who indicated that Bangladesh is looking at commercial and consular issues separately from hard political issues like Sheikh Hasina’s presence in India.

The official described the Ganga Water Treaty as a success of bilateral diplomacy that was sealed in 1996 during Sheikh Hasina’s first prime ministerial stint, and subsequently functioned in BNP years in 2001-’06. “Failing to renew this treaty before the year end will reflect negatively on the relationship,” said the official noting that delaying this renewal is counterproductive as already there are voices in India like that of JD(U) MP Sanjay Jha who have started opposing renewal of the treaty citing that the treaty does not benefit Bihar. “Prolonging this process will encourage such critics of this treaty to come forward,” he said.

A visit by PM Rahman, he said, has to be designed in such a way that it will kick start the India-Bangladesh relationship to its fullest potential. “Only then Prime Minister can return home with a substantial achievement in hand from Delhi,” said the official who added that PM Rahman is personally committed to holding dialogue with India at the highest level.

The official noted that India’s High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi has been holding rounds of discussions in Dhaka with multiple high-level officials including with the newly elected President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir but the bureaucrats-level talks are necessary to create an agenda for PM Rahman’s visit. “We are open minded about building an agenda for a visit by our Prime Minister. On some issues there can be relaxation of our positions and on certain issues we would prefer the relation to move ahead,” he said.

Also Read | Sheikh Hasina’s media event can hurt ties with India: Bangladesh

The Hindu was told that Bangladesh expects India to be mindful of the fact that Sheikh Hasina’s accusations against Tarique Rahman are not rational as Mr. Rahman is an elected leader. “However, we are satisfied by the fact that a fresh press event featuring members of Sheikh Hasina’s party and her supporters was prevented by India. That is a constructive message from India and we have taken note of it,” said the official.

In this connection, he said that BNP leaders remember that in 2018, India denied entry to Lord Alexander Carlile, legal adviser to Bangladesh Nationalist Party’s then Chairperson Khaleda Zia. Lord Carlile was expected to address a press conference against Sheikh Hasina , who was Prime Minister of Bangladesh at that time.

Prime Minister Rahman was invited to attend the BRICS summit in Delhi as the head of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) between September 12-13 and bureaucrats-level consultation was ongoing between the two sides over the visit when deposed PM Sheikh Hasina addressed a press conference at the Foreign Correspondents Club here on August 5. Bangladesh’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in response accused Hasina of committing violent crimes and expressed “outrage” over the event.

World.title: PIL in Delhi HC against ‘infinite scroll’, ‘autoplay’ in social media apps
World.content:
A petition has been filed in the Delhi High Court seeking the constitution of an expert committee to examine engagement-maximising and addiction-causing design features on social media platforms like infinite scroll and autoplay.

The public interest litigation (PIL) came up for hearing before a bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia.

Justice Karia, however, recused from hearing the plea, which will now be heard next week before another bench.

Petitioner Vikas Kathuria, a professor of law at BML Munjal University, said the fulcrum of the issue is not what content social media platforms carry, but how such platforms are architecturally designed to cause addiction through infinite scroll, autoplay, algorithmically curated and personalised feeds, notification systems and variable-reward engagement metrics, such as “likes”, to capture, retain and repeatedly re-stimulate the attention of the user.

The plea said the concern assumes significance in the Indian context as statistics reveal that Indian youths aged 18-24 spend more than 120 minutes on average every day on social media.

It has been clinically proven that long hours on social media have been linked to suicide and depression among adolescents, the petition said.

The plea sought the court’s direction to the central government and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights to restrict, prohibit, or regulate the use of infinite scroll, autoplay, algorithmically curated feeds and persistent notifications.

World.title: West Bengal by-elections to test Trinamool rival groups’ claim over party symbol
World.content:
With by-elections for two Assembly constituencies in West Bengal -Nandigram and Rejinagar- scheduled on October 6, both factions of Trinamool Congress -one led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Ritabrata Banerjee- have decided to field candidates on both the seats.

However, the question is making rounds in the political circles: who will get the “ grass and twin-flowers’ symbol of Trinamool Congress in the upcoming by-elections.

“We will contest the by-polls. At the time of filing nominations, we will state that our candidates are from the Trinamool Congress and claim the twin-flower symbol. If the Election Commission does not allot the symbol to us by the deadline, our candidates will contest as independents,” Opposition Chief Whip in the West Bengal Assembly Akhruzzaman said on Wednesday (September 9, 2026).

Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman and the majority of the MLAs of the Trinamool Congress had moved away from Mamata Banerjee weeks after the 2026 Assembly poll debacle. 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress were elected to the 18th West Bengal Assembly on May 4, 2026, and more than 65 of them have turned rebels and have cut ties with Mamata Banerjee. Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman and other leaders of the rebel faction have made representation to the ECI seeking a claim over the party symbol.

The Mamata Banerjee faction will not let the opportunity to field candidates in the by-elections go, particularly when it has only a handful of MLAs in the State Assembly. Sources in the Mamata Banerjee group say that the party will field candidates. Mamata Banerjee loyalists say that the party symbol of grass with twin flowers remains with them till the ECI decides otherwise.

There are some speculations that the party chairperson may contest from either of the two seats, though there is no official word on it. Ms. Banerjee lost to Suvendu Adhikari by a narrow margin of 1526 votes in 2021 from the Nandigram Assembly seat. Rejinagar in Murshidabad has a majority of the electorate from the Muslim community, and if all opposition parties support the Trinamool Congress chairperson, she might find her way back into the State assembly.

The by-elections have been necessitated by Suvendu Adhikari, who won from Bhabanipur and Nandigram, giving up Nandigram and Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) leader Humayun Kabir, who won from Naoda and Rejinagar, giving up Rejinagar. Suvendu Adhikari had won the Nandigram seat in the 2026 Assembly polls by a margin of 9,665 votes while Humayun Kabir had won Rejinagar seat by a margin of 58876 votes.

Mr. Kabir’s son, Golam Nabi Azad, on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) filed his nomination as a candidate for the AJUP. The last date of filing nomination for the by-elections is September 16.

World.title: Over 919 hotels in Kolkata receive temporary closure notice over fire safety violations
World.content:
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation has issued a temporary closure notice to 919 hotels and guest houses for violating fire safety norms in the city. Out of the 960 establishments that were inspected, only 41 of them have made the final cut for fire safety measures.

Reacting to these closures, Kolkata Municipal Corporation Commissioner Smita Pandey said that the safety of people is non-negotiable. “There is nothing to do here. There is a bare minimum mandate, they have to have fire entry exits

The inspections of hotels and guest house over fire safety measures got stricter after a fire at a hotel called Shikha Inn in Kolkata’s Mirza Ghalib Street killed at least nine people, including seven Bangladeshi nationals. The incident raised major fire safety concerns in the city, especially in the area which houses hundreds of small hotels.

Over the past few weeks, many of these hotels have seen locks on their doors, with some of their shutters down. Many of the tourists who throng to this part of Kolkata in Park Street and Esplanade area are from Bangladesh who are in the city for medical tourism. Many have complained that the prices for the remaining few open hotels have shot up drastically.

“Some of us have been running these hotels for 40-60 years but the buildings are over 100-150 years old. The fire department is asking for the original building plan to give us fire safety recommendations or further plan of action. We do not have any issue with that, but we are renting these places from the owners, we do not have access to such old documents of building plans,” Mantosh Kumar Saha, a local hotel owner in Mirza Ghalib Street, told The Hindu on Wednesday (September 9, 2026).

However, Mr. Saha also added that none of the hotel owners will do any business outside the rule of law and have closed their shutters till they get any form of go-ahead to open for business. The lack of accessibility to building plans has left many of the hotel owners in a limbo.

Fire audits in malls

During the increased vigilance of the State government on fire safety, authorities have also started to conduct simultaneous audits on shopping malls and complexes.

Some of the major shopping malls in Kolkata and its adjoining areas saw fire safety audits on Wednesday (September 9, 2026). Popular shopping malls like South City, Mani Square, Star, Hiland Park, Acropolis, and others saw fire safety checks.

World.title: Ex-officials say Census data must be confidential amid concerns over potential NPR, NRC links
World.content:
The Union government’s decision to advance the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 in four poll-bound States, coupled with the introduction of several new questions in the Census schedule, has prompted some former Census officials to raise concerns regarding the quality of data that is to be collected and the potential links between the Census, the National Population Register (NPR) and, ultimately, the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

There is a precedent for Census data having been used to prepare the NRC. Records show that this took place in 1951, during Independent India’s first Census, when the NRC was prepared across the country by "copying" data from the Census schedules. However, for unspecified reasons, a countrywide NRC was never published, except in undivided Assam, which at the time also included Manipur and Tripura.

Speaking to The Hindu, former Deputy Registrar General of India K. Narayanan Unni stressed that any link between the Census and population-registration activities remains speculative. However, some of the information being sought in the latest Census questionnaire resembled data collected during previous NPR updation exercises.

The NPR, first created in 2011 and initially proposed to be updated with the first phase of the now-scrapped Census 2021, has been put on the back burner due to stiff opposition from political parties and civil society groups, who had expressed concern that the data could be used to create a countrywide NRC amid allegations that the process could lead to a large number of people being left out of citizenship.

Mr. Unni said, “NPR is generated under the Citizenship Act, and data is supposed to be published. However, Census data is confidential and can only be used for statistical purposes. But in 1951, Census data was used to prepare the NRC in Assam...” He added that even though Census data is confidential, this doesn’t mean that the 1951 exercise of using it to prepare NRC won’t be repeated.

On August 14, 2026, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) notified a set of 40 questions to be asked during the Population Enumeration phase, or the second phase, of the Census, adding 13 new questions or data fields that were not part of the 2011 Census questionnaire.

Some of the additional questions, such as particulars of a person’s parents, including their names, religion, place of birth, Aadhaar number, mobile phone number, voter ID and driving licence details, mirror those asked in the rehearsal form of the NPR in 2019.

The NPR had been updated in 2015 and already has the family-wise database of 119 crore residents.

The 1951 exercise

The 1951 Census report by R.B. Vaghaiwalla, the Superintendent of Census Operations for Assam, Manipur and Tripura, shows that the NRC was conceived primarily as a Census and administrative tool rather than a citizenship-verification exercise.

“An important innovation of this Census was the preparation of the NRC, in which all important Census data was transcribed from the Census slips. The Register uses the same symbols and abbreviations and is a copy of the Census slips,” the 1951 report said.

Missing NRC entries were copied from Census slips, and missing Census slips were recreated from NRC entries under a special reconciliation exercise undertaken by Vaghaiwalla. This took place even though there had been countrywide instructions from the Registrar General to limit such checks “in the interest of economy of time and money”.

According to Vaghaiwalla, the register was intended to be maintained permanently and updated by village officials, thereby providing continuity between Censuses. Though Section 15 of the Census Act, 1948 ensures confidentiality and says that “records of census [are] not open to inspection nor admissible in evidence”, the NRC was prepared using the data, establishing a precedent of using Census data to prepare the register.

A former Census official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the NPR and the Census were legally distinct exercises governed by different laws. The official pointed out that the updation of the NRC in Assam in 2019 was not based on NPR data and required a separate data collection exercise.

Undercounting concerns

On September 5, the RG&CCI advanced the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 in the poll-bound States of Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Goa, while deferring the exercise in violence-hit Manipur. The Census will also be the first in Independent India to enumerate castes beyond Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Mr. Unni said that the decision to conduct the Census in four States ahead of the rest of the country could lead to under-enumeration of migrant workers, particularly from Uttar Pradesh.

“Census dates were traditionally fixed around March 1 because migration was relatively low during that period. Advancing the exercise in States that are due to hold Assembly elections may mean that several migrant workers return home to vote and are not available where they ordinarily reside. By the time they reach their home State, enumeration there may already be over, creating the possibility that some migrants are not counted at either place," he said.

Other than these four States, as well as Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir, population enumeration in the rest of the country will take place in February 2027 with a reference date of March 1, 2027. Snow-bound areas have traditionally been counted before the rest of the country.

India follows a de facto system of enumeration, under which a person is counted where he or she is present during the Census period. Mr. Unni said that even a small increase in undercounting could affect data quality because past Censuses have already recorded some degree of under-enumeration.

On the government’s decision to defer the Census in Manipur, he said that conducting the enumeration without public cooperation would compromise data quality. However, he argued that postponement could deprive the State of demographic evidence relevant to claims about migration and population change.

‘Respondent fatigue’

Mr. Unni questioned the utility of some of the new questions, particularly those relating to identity documents and vaccination history. “Many of these details are already available in administrative databases. It is not clear what statistical purpose some of these questions will serve,” he said.

He also cautioned that a lengthy questionnaire could increase “respondent fatigue” and create practical difficulties for enumerators, most of whom are government school teachers.

“If a household is required to answer dozens of questions for every family member, it will increase the time taken per household and may lead to resistance, particularly in urban areas where enumerators are often unknown to residents,” he said.

The other former Census official raised questions over the inclusion of Aadhaar details in Census 2027, noting that the collection of Aadhaar numbers may require changes to existing legal provisions.

World.title: BJP MLA runs illegal ‘PG mafia’, alleges AAP; party refutes charges
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) alleged that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from RK Puram Anil Sharma runs an illegal paying guest (PG) “mafia” in the Satya Niketan area, days after a building collapse there claimed seven lives.

The party demanded that any demolition drive against illegal PGs should begin with Mr. Sharma’s property. The allegation came as AAP and the BJP traded blame over illegal constructions in the national capital.

Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters, AAP MLA Sanjeev Jha showed a video of a building allegedly owned by Mr. Sharma. He alleged that the building had been constructed with 100% coverage, whereas building norms require at least 25% of the space to be left for utility purposes. “[Chief Minister] Rekha Gupta has spoken about sealing the fourth and fifth floors, so the sealing should begin here itself so that an example can be set,” he said.

AAP national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda said, “A racket of illegal PGs was operating in the area under Anil Sharma and his team.”

However, Mr. Sharma refuted the allegations. “The building shown in the photograph [by the AAP] has a stilt parking level, along with the ground, first, second and third floors. There is no fourth floor,” he said, adding that he would file a defamation suit if AAP did not withdraw the allegations.

Meanwhile, the BJP attributed the city’s infrastructure issues to “criminal negligence” by successive Congress and AAP governments. Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra said while promising to turn Delhi into London or Paris, the parties reduced the Capital to “a slum”.

He added, “AAP and Congress leaders who are blaming our party every day must explain why, between 1998 and 2025, they failed to formulate any safety policy for the thousands of coaching centres, PG accommodations, guest houses and hotels that mushroomed across Delhi.”

World.title: Keralam’s multiplex pricing debate: SC order in 2023 permits cinema hall owners to fix food prices
World.content:
The prices of food items sold at multiplexes would continue to be set by traders with no scope for any governmental intervention in the price-fixing mechanism.

A Supreme Court order had termed cinema halls as private properties of its owners, who were entitled to “stipulate terms and conditions so long as they are not contrary to public interest, safety and welfare.” The court also noted that the owners were entitled to “determine the business model to be followed and to regulate the terms on which such sale should take place” in the K.C. Cinema vs State of Jammu and Kashmir case in 2023.

The issue of multiplexes charging “exorbitant prices” for snacks, including popcorn, had become a raging topic of discussion in Keralam with Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V. V. Rajesh flagging it. The officials of the Legal Metrology department in Keralam had held inspections in various movie halls and multiplexes across the State following the public resentment against the pricing.

Joint inspections by officials from the Legal Metrology, Civil Supplies and Food Safety departments were recently carried out in a few malls across the State on an instruction from Anoop Jacob, Minister for Food and Supplies, following the complaints.

At the multiplex in Kochi, a 90 g serving of regular salted popcorn costs ₹340, while the cheese and caramel variants are priced at ₹380 each. A 180 g serving of salted popcorn costs ₹420, and the cheese and caramel variants ₹460 each. A 240 g serving of salted popcorn is priced at ₹570.

A 90 g serving of nachos starts at ₹340, while a 170 g burger costs ₹260. A 540 ml bottle of cold beverage is priced at ₹290, and a vegetable sandwich costs ₹240.

“The MRP can be independently fixed by the manufacturers, and the law does not permit any governmental intervention in the process. We cannot insist on fixing the price of any products. All that the Legal Metrology Department (LMD) can do is to check whether the packaged products are sold at the MRP and the prescribed weight,” said Rajesh Sam, Controller, LMD.

The department can also insist that non-packaged products are sold at the price and weight as displayed in the menu cards, he said.

The Supreme Court, in a Bench comprising the then Chief Justice of India, Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, and Justice P.S. Narasimha, upheld the prohibition on carrying food and beverages from outside into the precincts of a movie hall, holding that it was not “contrary to public interest, safety or welfare.” The finding worked in favour of cinema hall owners, much to the chagrin of movie buffs.

The court observed that a movie hall also “doubles up as an eatery when food and beverages are sold within its premises.” “Patrons of a movie hall cannot demand to bring their own food to eat there when a condition to the contrary is enforced by the cinema hall owners. This would be akin to permitting a customer who visits a restaurant to carry their own food to that restaurant and eat it within the premises of that restaurant,” the court held.

The Bench also directed that hygienic drinking water be supplied free of cost within the precincts of the cinema hall. It further held that, in the case of an infant or young child, a reasonable quantity of food or beverages may be carried inside the hall.

World.title: PM to highlight efforts to end US-Iran war at UNGA
World.content:
• Bangladesh assumes presidency as General Assembly formally opens in New York

• Trump to speak on opening day; PM Shehbaz’s speech on 25th; Pezeshkian’s attendance ‘not yet confirmed’

• Renewal on the cards as tenure of panel monitoring Iran sanctions expires during UNGA session

WASHINGTON: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is due to arrive in New York later this month for the UN General Assembly, where he is expected to highlight Pakistan’s efforts to find a peaceful solution to the ongoing US-Iran war.

PM Shehbaz is slated to address the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly on Sept 25, where the Gulf conflict is expected to overshadow much of the high-level debate.

The official theme of the 81st session is ‘Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All’, and the UNGA debate is expected to run from Sept 22 to 26, with a final sitting on Sept 28.

However, ongoing fighting between Washington and Tehran is expected to feature prominently in discussions among world leaders, particularly over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, regional stability and the possibility of finding a diplomatic way out of the confrontation.

The participation of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is also emerging as a key question ahead of the high-level week.

Iran is listed on the tentative speakers’ schedule as the fifth speaker on Sept 23, the second day of the UNGA debate, but a final decision on whether he will travel to New York or not, has not yet been made.

Iranian officials have indicated that Tehran is still assessing the level of participation and attendance, citing what they describe as “illegal conditions” imposed by Washington on the Iranian delegation’s travel and attendance.

US President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the General Assembly on Sept 22, the opening day of the high-level debate, following Brazil, which traditionally opens the general debate.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is also expected to attend reception hosted by President Trump on the same day.

Israel, the other party to the conflict, is scheduled to speak on Sept 24, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu representing his country.

India, meanwhile, is only sending its foreign minister, who is scheduled to address the General Assembly on Sept 26.

According to diplomatic sources, Pakistan is expected to use the forum of the UN General Assembly to underline its position that the conflict should be resolved through negotiations rather than prolonged military confrontation.

The prime minister is also expected to highlight Islamabad’s contacts with countries involved in efforts to de-escalate the situation.

The Iranian issue is already occupying a prominent place on the UN agenda ahead of the arrival of world leaders.

The Security Council is scheduled to vote on Sept 17 on renewing the mandate of the panel of experts monitoring sanctions on Iran. The panel’s mandate expires on Sept 26, during the General Assembly’s high-level week.

The proposed renewal is expected to produce another confrontation between the United States and its Western allies on one side and Russia and China on the other.

Moscow and Beijing have opposed continuation of the monitoring mechanism, arguing that the Security Council no longer has the authority to pursue the matter in its present form.

The dispute is linked to the restoration of UN sanctions on Iran under the “snapback” mechanism after Britain, France and Germany concluded last year that Tehran was not complying with its obligations under the 2015 nuclear agreement. Iran has rejected allegations that it is seeking nuclear weapons.

The Sept 17 vote will therefore come just days before heads of government begin arriving for the General Assembly and could further sharpen the diplomatic divisions surrounding Iran.

For Pakistan, the situation carries additional urgency because of its geographical proximity to the conflict and its economic and security interests in the Gulf region.

The prime minister will be accompanied by a high-level delegation, including senior members of the government, and is expected to hold a series of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the General Assembly.

The UN session formally opened on Wednesday, with Bangladesh’s Khalilur Rahman assuming the presidency of the 81st General Assembly. Mr Rahman has placed peace and security, restoration of trust in multilateral institutions and UN reform among the priorities of his presidency.

The session also comes ahead of a major change in the UN hierarchy, as it would be the last for current Secretary General Antonio Guterres, whose term ends on Dec 31, 2026.

World.title: Govt hikes petrol price by Rs3.40, diesel by Rs6.72
World.content:
The government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol by Rs3.40 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.72 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs367.75 per litre while HSD will cost Rs392.67 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 10 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Islamabad extends rare greeting to Pyongyang
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Wed­nesday made an unusual public diplomatic gesture towards North Korea, with President Asif Ali Zardari and the Foreign Office extending greetings to Pyongyang on the 78th anniversary of the country’s founding.

In a letter to DPRK President Kim Jong Un on the 78th founding anniversary of the republic, President Zardari referred to the two countries’ “cordial relations based on mutual trust and goodwill” and expressed the hope that bilateral ties would continue to grow in the interests of both countries.

The Foreign Office also issued a public message on X, extending its “warmest felicitations” to North Korea and tagging Pakistan’s diplomatic mission in Pyongyang, which as per its own website is closed.

Such public exchanges have been relatively uncommon in recent years as relations between the two countries have remained largely constrained.

The Foreign Office, however, played down any unusual significance attached to the latest exchange. “Exchange of felicitation messages are a common practice,” FO spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan said in reply to a question from Dawn.

Pakistan and North Korea established consular relations in 1968 and upgraded them to ambassadorial level four years later, but their relationship over past two decades has remained low key, particularly since international sanctions were imposed on Pyongyang over its nuclear and missile programmes.

While Pakistan’s mission in Pyongyang is currently closed, North Korea continues to maintain its embassy in Islamabad and hosted its national day reception on Tuesday.

Islamabad has been implementing UNSC sanctions against Pyongyang, including restrictions on trade and commercial dealings, suspension of Air Koryo flights, monitoring of North Korean diplomats’ activities and bank accounts, and stringent visa requirements even for diplomatic personnel.

World.title: 'Trump dividend': US president offers $5,000 to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he would pay every American adult a $5,000 “Trump dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress in November’s midterm election, an extraordinary attempt to persuade voters to back his party.

Trump made the proposal at his Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention, but it was not immediately clear how the payments would work or whether they would be legal. With approximately 270 million US adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion.

During a primetime address that lasted an hour, Trump boasted of completing “the greatest two years in the history of the presidency,” putting himself squarely at the centre of the election despite his deepening unpopularity.

But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump’s party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran.

“We hand America’s future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet,” he said.

“Vote Republicans and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come.”

The two-day Dallas gathering, where Trump will also deliver the closing remarks on Thursday after Vice President JD Vance’s keynote address, underscores the extent to which Republicans’ fortunes are tethered to Trump and serves as a showcase for their strategy ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

The event was so centred on the president that Republican National Committee Chairman Joe Gruters informally dubbed it “Trumpapalooza,” a nod to the popular Lollapalooza music festival.

The focus on Trump amounts to a risky bet that he can mobilise the voters who carried him to the presidency two years ago, despite public polls showing his approval ratings have hit an all-time low. The president vowed to pay multiple visits to battleground states and districts in the eight weeks until Election Day.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot,” Trump said, a line that may have pleased Democratic campaign strategists just as much as MAGA voters.

The convention presented a tough choice in particular for Republicans facing difficult elections who may need to distance themselves from the president to broaden their appeal but cannot afford to alienate Trump’s most committed supporters.

Many such Republicans skipped the convention, including Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan, Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska and Senator Susan Collins of Maine, all facing strong Democratic challengers this fall.

Some, however, elected to travel to Dallas. At least 16 candidates in competitive House and Senate races were scheduled to speak, according to the RNC schedule.

Among those who spoke on Wednesday were Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a close Trump ally who is locked in a tough Senate race with Democratic lawmaker James Talarico, and Ohio Senator Jon Husted, who faces former Senator Sherrod Brown.

Though Trump insisted the 21,000-seat arena was “packed,” the upper sections remained largely empty during his speech capping Wednesday’s program.

Democrats portrayed as ‘socialists and communists’

While Republican officials had described the convention as an opportunity to tout Trump’s policies, most of the early speakers focused largely on attacking Democrats as extreme on topics such as transgender women in sports and border security—political red meat for the base.

Issues that voters have consistently cited as top concerns, the Iran war and the cost of living, received comparatively less attention.

Alabama state Representative Ernie Yarbrough, a convention attendee, said Trump needs to give voters a clearer sense of how long the war in Iran could last and what the administration’s aims are.

“People want to feel like we’re not getting stuck in an endless cycle,” he said.

Trump defended his decision to attack Tehran, saying he acted to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. He also promised that oil prices would drop “as soon as we win the war with Iran,” which he vowed would happen soon.

But the conflict shows little sign of ending more than six months after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, and analysts have said Iran’s nuclear program has not been eliminated. Iran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.

Before Trump took the stage, a parade of speakers called Democrats “socialists” and “communists,” echoing one of Trump’s favorite attack lines following a handful of victories by democratic socialists in Democratic primary elections.

Democrats are “dangerous, radical and weird,” said Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the party’s Senate campaign arm.

Wednesday’s program also featured a surprise pretaped video from Democratic US Senator John Fetterman, who introduced his fellow senator from Pennsylvania, Republican Dave McCormick, as his “great friend” while declaring he would work with Trump to protect the state’s steel industry.

Fetterman’s extraordinary participation appeared likely to emphasise the ideological divides plaguing the Democratic Party ahead of the midterms. Fetterman, who has increasingly clashed with left-wing Democrats, has denied speculation that he may leave the party.

The convention’s stakes are high for both parties. With the elections less than two months away, Republicans face the prospect of losing control of at least one chamber of Congress, with public polling showing Democrats more motivated to vote and Trump’s approval ratings deeply underwater.

The event faced stiff competition for viewers with the start of the NFL season, with opening night coinciding with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks.

Still, after months of negative headlines over the Iran war and inflation, many Republicans see the gathering as their best chance to promote candidates, draw contrasts with Democrats and energise a Republican electorate expressing less enthusiasm about voting than Democrats, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.

World.title: New provinces not only way to improve governance: Gohar
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Calling for caution in decisions regarding the creation of new provinces, PTI Interim Chairman Barri­ster Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday war­ned that any step taken in haste and without consensus could harm the federation.

“Good governance is needed in every province. But the creation of new provinces is not the only solution to improve governance, there are other ways, too. It should not be done in haste, and without consensus. It’s very good to have a discussion on this issue,” he said, while speaking to the media at the Peshawar High Court.

“However, making hasty decisions, going against the will of the people, imposing own decisions [on them], bulldozing such decisions through parliament or new constitutional amendments in such times of turmoil will only add to the problems people are facing instead of resolving issues. Therefore, this should be avoided,” he said.

Commenting on PTI’s planned march on Islamabad on Sept 27, Barrister Gohar said it would be peaceful and solely a “justice march”.

Expects JUI-F to join Sept 27 march; says no state resources will be used for PTI protest

“The PTI’s march on Islamabad will not be a casual march. There will be no chaos, and state resources will not be used,” he said.

He said PTI workers would demonstrate during the march that they were peaceful people. He added that the party had invited other opposition parties to join the protest.

“We expect Maulana Fazlur Rehman and the entire joint opposition to join us in the September 27 march,” he said.

Barrister Gohar said people wanted change through democratic means, with the rights of all citizens protected, and called for fresh elections.

“Like the Treaty of Hudaibiyah, there should be a treaty named ‘Peace of Pakistan’, in which everyone’s rights are protected, all stakeholders are included, people are given relief and political stability is ensured,” he said.

He said such a Pakistan would certainly progress and its people would prosper, adding that the public was now tired of political tension and division.

He also condemned a recent statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, where she reportedly said Punjab faced a greater threat from neighbouring provinces than from neighbouring India.

“Our core committee and political committee, in a recent meeting, demanded that the Punjab chief minister withdraw her remarks,” he said.

Barrister Gohar said Pakistan’s narrative was that India and its intelligence agency, RAW, were behind terrorism in the country.

“We only say that she should not support Pakistan’s enemies through her statements,” he said.

Commenting on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi’s recent visit to different cities in Sindh, the PTI chairman said the chief minister had received a warm public welcome during his street campaign.

“The enthusiasm among the people of Sindh regarding the upcoming protest march has boosted our morale,” he said, adding that it showed people wanted to get rid of the status quo.

He said the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government was following the principles of PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan “in letter and spirit”.

Asked about alleged police violence against students of a nursing college in Hayatabad, the PTI chairman said he was deeply saddened by the incident.

He said the senior vice president of the Nursing Association had contacted him following the incident, after which he immediately approached provincial ministers Meena Khan and Khaliqur Rehman for action.

Meanwhile, the PTI has submitted a list of six party leaders to the Adiala jail administration to allow them to meet incarcerated party founder Imran Khan on Thursday (today).

The list, submitted by Advocate Awais Younas Chaudhry, includes Sajjad Hussain Shah, Qaiser Abbas Maan, Saqib Meraaj, Malik Shakeel, Zeeshan Mohsin and Daniyal Kiyani.

World.title: Senate panel orders FIR over Pims nursery fire
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights on Wednesday directed authorities to register an FIR over the fire at the nursery of Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), in which 14 newborn babies died and initiate criminal proceedings against those responsible.

The committee, chaired by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, expressed serious concern over the failure to register a case despite the prime minister’s directions for action against officials allegedly responsible for the tragedy.

During the meeting at Parliament Lodges, Pims officials informed the committee that no FIR had so far been registered. Dr Iqbal Durrani confirmed the position when questioned by the chairperson.

Senator Syed Masroor Ahsan pointed out that the prime minister had ordered the termination of services of eight employees and registration of criminal cases against those responsible, asking why no action had been taken.

Committee seeks criminal proceedings against those responsible for deaths of 14 newborns

Senator Zehri directed the immediate registration of an FIR concerning negligence and loss of life. She also called for criminal proceedings against responsible officials, attachment of their assets and placement of suspended officials’ names on the Exit Control List (ECL).

The committee also reviewed the Jaranwala incidents of Aug 16, 2023, and was informed that 389 people had been arrested, while proceedings in several cases were either pending trial or had been concluded.

The chairperson expressed concern over the prolonged pendency of the cases, stressing that the matter involved a minority community and required urgent resolution. She directed authorities to properly assess the losses suffered by affected families, particularly damage to their houses, and provide compensation accordingly.

A representative of the chief secretary said an assessment committee would evaluate the losses in the presence of community representatives. The government planned to distribute Rs2 million to each affected family.

Families, however, told the committee that the compensation did not correspond to their actual losses. Senator Zehri directed authorities to take the affected people into confidence and determine compensation on the basis of verified losses.

The committee also examined the case of Zeeshan, a sanitary worker associated with a third party and deputed to the Suthra Punjab office. Officials said he had initially been engaged in 2025 and later assigned duties as a naib qasid in the office’s IT room before being dismissed for misconduct.

The committee sought all relevant documents and directed that the family members of the deceased be invited to the next meeting to present their position.

On the target-killing case of Ahmed Javed, the committee was informed that the main accused had been granted bail by the high court. The complainant alleged that the accused appeared at hearings with 40 to 50 people, creating an atmosphere of intimidation. The committee recommended that an application be moved before the court to prevent such practices.

Child begging in Islamabad was another major issue discussed. Senator Quratul Ain Marri called for a permanent rehabilitation centre, with education and skills-development programmes for children.

The committee also reviewed the Hina Javed, Hina Zareef and Mir Raza cases and sought detailed reports from police authorities. In the Mir Raza case, the committee recommended the arrest of the SHO concerned over alleged mishandling of the crime scene. It directed all departments to submit the required reports and documents at the next meeting.

PML-N, ANP senators spar

A meeting of the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights turned acrimonious on Wednesday as PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali and Awami National Party (ANP) chief Senator Aimal Wali Khan clashed over the questioning of Suthra Punjab officials in connection with the death of a Gujranwala Waste Management Company (GWMC) worker.

Chaired by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, the committee was reviewing the death of the employee, who allegedly died by suicide after receiving only half of his salary and facing termination of his contract.

Tensions rose when Senator Khan pressed officials with tough questions. Senator Ali interrupted, objecting to his tone.

“Listen to them, you are conducting an inquiry and asking questions as if you are sitting in a police station,” he said.

When another member suggested that the cameras be switched off, Ali said he had “nothing wrong to say”.

“Speak properly,” he told Khan.

“I am speaking properly, you speak properly too,” Khan responded.

Senators then intervened to defuse the situation.

World.title: Apple debuts passport-shaped foldable phone, called Duo
World.content:
Apple on Wednesday unveiled a foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company’s flagship product.

The Duo is sized and shaped like a passport, with rounded edges. It opens into a horizontal, wide screen that can also be viewed vertically. There is a smaller single screen on the front when the phone is folded. When open, it is Apple’s thinnest phone, the company said.

The folding phone event, the first with new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus at the helm, is the most noticeable overhaul of Apple’s flagship product since it removed the physical home button from the iPhone X in 2017.

The iPhone brought in $209.6 billion, or just over half of Apple’s sales, in its most recent fiscal year.

Former CEO Tim Cook handed over the leadership baton to Ternus with a video about how to start the presentation that ended with a close-up of Cook, who said, “Not me. That’s your guy,” pointing back toward Ternus.

Ternus touted the iPhone as a personal AI hub that focused on privacy, saying that others wanted to collect and store personal data. “Honestly, trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control,” he said. “That’s why Apple Intelligence runs on device whenever it can.”

People look at the new foldable iPhone Duo devices on display during Apple’s event at the Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, California, the US on September 9, 2026. — Reuters

Apple’s Lilian Rincon, who oversees AI products for the iPhone maker and was recruited from Google earlier this year, described an updated Siri assistant that will work with 300,000 apps at release.

Executives also showed off the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max handsets that are the latest versions of Apple’s well-known line, which do not fold. Pricing for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starts at $1,199 and $1,299, up $100 from the starting prices of the 17 Pro and Pro Max.

Apple also unveiled a feature aimed at addressing growing concerns over AI-generated and manipulated images.

It introduced a new standard it calls “Apple Reference Image” to prove the authenticity of the images taken with the new iPhone 18 Pro cameras and said it will also support the emerging SynthID standard for identifying images that have been created or edited with AI. The Apple Reference Image feature will not be available in the EU or China.

The iPhone 18 Pro will also include the new A20 Pro chip, which brings improvements to help advanced AI models to run directly on iPhones.

Apple CEO John Ternus speaks as Apple holds an event at the Steve Jobs Theater on its campus in Cupertino, California, the US on September 9, 2026. — Reuters

“Apple Intelligence and Siri are front and centre. Apple is using its biggest strength, the sheer scale of its hardware base, to make AI an integral part of the everyday experience across devices,” PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore said. Shares were down about one per cent during the Apple presentation.

The company also said a new version of AirPods would start at $129 with noise cancellation, a first for its budget line of earbuds, and that a $149 version will be available with extra features such as wireless charging and on-stem volume control that will allow users to adjust the volume by swiping up or down on the stem.

Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, positioning them as major health-focused upgrades. That includes a redesigned sensor system that collects heart rate more frequently than before and powers new features that gauge recovery and fitness.

The company said the watches use new Apple silicon and improved sensors to deliver what it called the most accurate heart-rate tracking in a wearable.

Premium pricing challenge

Ternus previously served as Apple’s hardware chief but has kept a low public profile aside from a handful of product introductions and sustainability initiatives.

It will fall to Ternus to persuade Apple’s customers that they need a foldable device that analysts believe could cost more than $2,000, a new high for a global brand that has defined mass luxury.

While Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold folding phones since 2019, the devices have remained a niche among tech enthusiasts.

But even with a steep price tag, analyst firms such as International Data Corporation expect Apple to sell every foldable iPhone it can produce and secure a 40pc share of the lucrative niche by the end of next year.

Wednesday’s event is also expected to mark a major change in Apple’s annual product schedule.

While analysts expect Apple to show off new watches, they anticipate the company will hold off on updates to its more affordable iPhone models until next spring and instead focus only on the new folding device and its iPhone Pro and Pro Max lineup.

The move is aimed at smoothing out Apple’s annual sales cycle, which typically shows a large bump in revenue during the year-end holiday quarter for the US and Europe.

World.title: ECP bars three ex-MNAs from contesting elections
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday again declared three former lawmakers — Zartaj Gul, Sahibzada Hamid Raza and Abdul Latif — ineligible to contest any election for failing to submit their statements of assets and liabilities for the financial year 2024-25.

The commission said the three ex-members of the National Asse­mbly would remain disqualified “till submission of the requisite Statement of Assets & Liabilities (Form-B) for financial year 2024-25” in compliance with Section 137 of the Elections Act, 2017”.

“The commission vide Order dated 07.08.2026 has declared the delinquent ex-members of the National Assembly ineligible to contest any general election, by-election, Senate election and local government election,” it said.

Zartaj Gul, Sahibzada Hamid Raza and Abdul Latif ineligible over failure to submit asset details

The ECP had first disqualified Ms Gul and Mr Raza in the first week of August 2025. Mr Latif was disqualified on July 29, 2025, from NA-1, Upper and Lower Chitral.

In July 2025, an antiterrorism court in Faisalabad sentenced more than 100 PTI leaders and workers, including key opposition figures, to up to 10 years in prison.

Among those sentenced to the 10-year rigorous imprisonment were former opposition leader in the National Assembly Omar Ayub Khan, opposition leader in the Senate Shibli Faraz, Zartaj Gul, Hamid Raza, Sheikh Rashid Shafique, Kanwal Shauzab, Farah Agha, Rai Haider Kharal and Muhammad Ahmad Chattha.

Under Article 63(1)(h) of the Constitution, a person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude and sentenced to imprisonment of not less than two years stands disqualified from being a member of parliament for five years from the date of release. The ECP had subsequently notified the disqualification of the lawmakers convicted in the case.
