World.title: Can VR Capture the Power of China’s Ancient Caves?
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018985/Can VR Capture the Power of China’s Ancient Caves?
World.content:
Under the blazing July sun, Zhang, a high school teacher from northern China, stood outside the Digital Exhibition Center of the Mogao Grottoes, a modern building designed to resemble the surrounding dunes. A shuttle bus would soon take him and other tourists to the foot of Mingsha Mountain, where they would see the original Mogao Grottoes: 492 caves containing Buddhist murals and painted sculptures spanning more than a thousand years, now strictly protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Zhang had just watched two introductory films at the center, “A Thousand Years of Mogao Caves” and “The Splendor of Buddha’s Palace,” the latter screened in its dome theater. His eyes sparkled with excitement. “It is so spectacular that I am speechless! I hope other heritage sites in China can be presented like this.”

The Mogao Grottoes in Dunhuang, northwestern China’s Gansu province, are the product of more than a millennium of cultural exchange between East and West along the historic Silk Road. Renowned for the extraordinary aesthetic and cultural value of their cave art, they attract large numbers of tourists. Yet the grottoes are intrinsically fragile, threatened by both the surrounding desert and the carbon dioxide and humidity generated by visitors.

To reduce pressure on the caves and ensure their long-term preservation, the Dunhuang Academy, which manages and researches the site, has been developing the Digital Dunhuang project since the late 1980s. More than 200 caves have been documented through photography, image stitching, and laser scanning, with the material transformed into online and on-site experiences spanning films, virtual and augmented reality, and museum exhibitions. These digital experiences have become an increasingly prominent part of visiting Mogao.

Putting “cultural heritage” and “digital technology” together creates an immediate tension. Heritage looks backward, toward the past and the old; technology looks forward, toward the future and the new. When the two are brought together, digital representations exist alongside the physical heritage itself, raising questions such as: what qualities of the original are irreplaceable, and to what extent can they be reproduced or conveyed digitally?

I conducted a year of fieldwork at the Mogao Grottoes between 2024 and 2025, spending long periods in both the physical caves and digital exhibitions and talking with visitors. While physical and digital exhibitions at heritage sites can tell separate stories, at Mogao they are closely intertwined. The tension between heritage and technology highlights both their differences and how they complement each other, as visitors often observed.

Among the visitors I spoke with was a middle-aged British artist traveling with her partner. The two had sharply contrasting reactions. She was fascinated by the distinctive smell inside the caves, a mixture of dust, moisture, and history that would be difficult to reproduce digitally. Her partner, by contrast, was perfectly content with the digital exhibitions. “I really got my fix! I could just go with the digital,” he said. He drew parallels with Lascaux Cave in France, where replicas receive visitors while the original, closed to the public since 1963, is preserved.

For some caves, digital representations are the only way visitors can experience their fragile artworks. Cave 285, built during the Western Wei period and containing inscriptions dated to 538 and 539, is one of Mogao’s most important early caves, renowned for its rich murals and diverse artistic styles. It is currently closed to the public for conservation, but a virtual reality exhibition immerses visitors in the stories depicted on the murals and even lets them use handheld controllers as drumsticks to play music alongside mythological beings.

Wang, visiting from the southern city of Shenzhen with her young child, told me: “I like it very much, and it is also child-friendly. The VR shows real scenes from the cave while telling the stories in detail. It even surpasses the real cave!”

For visitors like Wang, VR not only reproduces the physical cave but creates a space of its own, allowing them to experience it in a playful, multisensory way impossible inside the original. “I am so touched that I almost cried,” another visitor told me. “I know Cave 285 is not open to the public, so I am very grateful for the opportunity to see it up close.”

For caves that remain open, experiencing both their physical and digital versions can offer a more nuanced perspective on the art. Cave 61 contains the largest surviving Buddhist historical landscape painting at Mogao. Based on the geography of the Tang dynasty (618–907), the mural depicts pilgrimage routes leading to the sacred Mount Wutai, over 2,000 kilometers east of the caves. It is also featured in “The Splendor of Buddha’s Palace” in the center’s 360-degree dome theater.

Later, on a poplar-shaded path, a college student, Xiaoyang, reflected on the contrast. “When I saw the mural from Cave 61 on the big screen, it was so bright. It really looked real, but I knew it wasn’t. I couldn’t feel the traces of time. But when I actually stood inside the cave and faced the mural, I began wondering how ancient cartographers had trudged through Mount Wutai and how painters had depicted the scene on the wall.”

Her response points to what digital reproductions can lose even as they make the art more visible. On-screen, details are easier to see, but this digital representation weakens the power of age and decay that connect viewers to the mural and the people who created it centuries ago. The digital image shows what can be difficult to see inside the cave, while the physical mural confronts visitors with the passage of time. Together, they encourage visitors to consider both the image and the history behind it.

Another crucial component of Digital Dunhuang is the digital repatriation of manuscripts and artifacts now held overseas. In the early 20th century, the discovery of more than 70,000 manuscripts, paintings, and other objects in the Library Cave, or Cave 17, opened a new chapter in Mogao’s history. Most were removed amid the era’s turmoil. Now dispersed around the world, they are being brought together digitally through collaborations between the Dunhuang Academy and international institutions.

Adjacent to Caves 16 and 17 is a museum housing the exhibition “Treasure in Caves,” which recounts the artifacts’ dispersal and virtual reunification. Replicas of objects now scattered among collections worldwide stand side by side in rows of glass cases.

Visiting the caves and exhibition offers complementary experiences, making this place marked by loss feel slightly more complete. A woman in her 50s discussing Cave 17, a memorial cave containing a statue of the Tang-dynasty monk Hong Bian, said: “Cave 17 is a physical place that has endured these historical events. The exhibition tells their story and shows the artifacts, so I can hear the echoes of history and finally breathe a sigh of relief.”

Like these visitors, I have found my own answers to questions about the authenticity. Now writing about Dunhuang from afar, I often revisit photographs from my fieldwork. Yet when I close my eyes, I can still recall the original caves: their warmth, their solemnity, and their sense of history.

The tension between the digital and physical does not necessarily have to be resolved in favor of one or the other. Digital representations can make inaccessible caves available, reveal otherwise difficult-to-see details, and reunite objects that have been physically dispersed. But they can also erase the traces of time and distance that give the originals much of their power. At Mogao, the two forms are most effective not when one substitutes for the other but when they work in tandem to deepen the experience.

By presenting the grottoes from multiple perspectives while carefully controlling access to the physical caves, the Dunhuang Academy shows how digitization can expand our understanding of authenticity rather than simply imitate the original. Perhaps another thousand years from now, the Mogao Grottoes will still move us, both through their carefully preserved physical form and through the digital versions that capture, interpret, and transmit them.

According to research guidelines, all names in this article are pseudonyms.



Portrait artist: Wang Zhenhao.

World.title: Ex-Sandiganbayan justice among first witnesses in Sara Duterte unexplained wealth case
World.content:
Members of the prosecution listen to a ruling during Day 22 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 7, 2026.

The prosecution accuses Vice President Sara Duterte of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution over her unexplained wealth

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution team in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte seeks to present a former anti-graft court justice, as well as representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), as its first witnesses in its unexplained wealth case against her.

Prosecutor Terry Ridon told the media on Thursday, September 10, that they have requested from the impeachment court the issuance of subpoenas to the following individuals:

Retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang

Office of the Ombudsman Records Division Officer-in-Charge Karen Batu

SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo del Rosario

Play Video

Ridon said Cabotaje-Tang will be asked to discuss the principles governing public accountability and integrity, as well as mechanisms for addressing undisclosed wealth.

Batu will testify on specific details about Duterte’s Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), while Del Rosario will authenticate the company records associated with the Vice President, Ridon added.

The list of intended prosecution witnesses is still subject to the approval of the impeachment court. The trial resumes on Monday, September 14.

Prosecutor Joel Chua previously said that their team may present up to 25 witnesses for the second impeachment article, alongside 1,800 financial documents.

Duterte is accused of culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust when she supposedly amassed unexplained wealth, highlighted by supposed inconsistencies between the Vice President’s large bank transactions and her net worth declarations.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council had said that according to the banks, the accounts named under the Vice President and her husband, Mans Carpio, were the subject of covered transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports amounting to P6.77 billion from 2006 to 2025.

Duterte’s legal team questioned the presentation of the AMLC numbers, saying an aggregate of inflows and outflows over two decades would naturally yield a bloated number.

Despite the billions of pesos in bank transactions over the years, Duterte’s net worth averaged P42 million in 15 years, peaking at P88 million in 2024.

What’s more notable is that she made zero cash and cash declaration deposits from 2019 to 2024, and modest cash on hand and cash in bank declarations during years she was in elective office between 2007 and 2018. – Rappler.com

World.title: Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?
World.content:
LIVE

The panel discussion starting at 12:30 pm on September 10 brings together stakeholders to identify safety gaps and develop community-led solutions to protect children

MANILA, Philippines – Concerned about your child’s safety and how you can ensure a more secure environment for them?

Watch the live panel discussion as Rappler’s civic engagement arm MovePH launches “Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?” This will be streamed on Rappler’s YouTube channel live from the Rappler Civic Hub in Pasig City on Thursday, September 10.

Organized in partnership with CyberGuardiansPH and Mental Health Youth Hub, this pilot initiative tackles rising school violence and digital risks by turning community discussions into concrete, multisectoral solutions.

Rappler head of community Pia Ranada moderates the conversation with key decision-makers and child protection advocates:

Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte shares local government strategies on community governance, child protection policies, and campus safety.

Police Capt. Wallen Arancillo, spokesperson for the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group, addresses online grooming, cyberbullying, and digital protection in off-campus hotspots.

Dr. Princess Gairanod, child protection specialist from the Philippine Pediatric Society, discusses student mental health, psychosocial care, and health safeguarding protocols.

Razzel Anne Requesto, Director IV at the Department of Education (DepEd) Office of the Assistant Secretary for Governance and Support Services, discusses institutional safety protocols and learner protection guidelines.

After the panel discussion and Q and A, participants joining on-site can take part in a hands-on workshop to collectively develop concrete and actionable responses to threats facing children and schools across four Civic Circles:

Campus security and physical safety

Psychosocial care and mental health

Policy, governance, and accountability

Digital safety and off-campus hotspots

The solutions generated during the session may be featured on Rappler to encourage a broader discussion and possible adaptation by local governments, schools, families, and communities.

Bookmark this page to watch Rappler’s live broadcast.

To join the conversation, download the Rappler App on iOS or Android, tap the Chat tab, and enter the Education chat room while watching the stream. – Rappler.com

World.title: Three telltale signs you have dry eyes
World.content:
No more tears left to cry? It could be more than that.

Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by Eye Mo and was produced by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the production of this piece.

It’s easy to forget about the importance of eye care especially as we go through our busy daily routines. Many of us spend over eight hours each day looking at screens for work and during our downtime.

You could be dealing with dry eyes already. Why not give your eyes a break?

What are signs of dry eyes?

Remember the saying that goes “at the end of the day, you’re all you have?” That holds true for our eyes, as they do the work to protect themselves – eyes produce tears to lubricate themselves. When our eyes are dry, it means they’re not producing good quality tears, or the tears they produce just aren’t doing their job. This can end up causing irritation and even damage to the surface of our eyes.

TL;DR: our eyes need to stay moist to be healthy.

Here are three common symptoms of dry eyes—perhaps a cry for help from your eyes.

Burning or stinging sensation (mahapding mata) – This discomfort happens when your eyes don’t produce enough tears, or when the tears evaporate too quickly, leading to an itchy or stinging sensation.

– This discomfort happens when your eyes don’t produce enough tears, or when the tears evaporate too quickly, leading to an itchy or stinging sensation. Eyes feel rough ( magaspang na mata) – When your eyes are dry, it feels as if dust or a foreign object is stuck in them and won’t come out.

– When your eyes are dry, it feels as if dust or a foreign object is stuck in them and won’t come out. Tired eyes (pagod na mata) – Are your eyes still feeling sleepy even after a full eight hours of sleep? It’s a sign from your eyes telling you it’s time to moisturize!

If these symptoms are often ignored, your eyes don’t just stay dry – they get irritated.

When dry turns to red

Ignore dry eyes long enough, and every blink starts to feel like a sandpaper scratching the surface of your eye. That constant friction causes your eyes to get irritated, leaving the tiny vessels in your eyes swollen. This turns that dryness into noticeable redness.

Combine the scorching Philippine heat and humidity with a grueling Metro Manila commute packed with dust, smoke, and pollution, our eyes end up taking a constant beating. Maybe it’s the reason why some of us step out of the MRT or carousel bus looking like they’ve just cried.

Taking care of your eyes

It’s hard to lessen your screen time especially during work hours, but make sure to give your eyes a break. A 20-20-20 rule can help by focusing your eyes on something else that’s about 20 feet away for 20 seconds, and do that every 20 minutes. For a longer break, take a quick walk, talk to a friend, or even stand up and stretch your body, as long as your eyes are not staring at your screen or reading anything for a while.

Blinking often also helps as it aids tear production. Meanwhile, drinking water and being hydrated is also a must!

Whatever feeling your eyes might have – itchy, burning, and has a sandy-like texture, refrain from scratching and touching them as it would damage your eyes further.

And even when you’re out of tears, it’s okay to seek help from artificial tears! Using eye drops to combat and relieve chronic dry eyes.

Soothe your eyes

So which Eye Mo matches your eyes’ needs today?

If your eyes are starting to feel dry, help restore moisture with Hypromellose (Eye Mo Moisturizing Formula). Containing 3 mg of Hypromellose, just 2 to 3 drops in each eye help lubricate and moisturize the eyes.

If heat and your daily commute leave your eyes looking red, cool your eyes down with the new Tetrahydrozoline HCl (Eye Mo Cool Red Eyes) which contains Tetrahydrozoline HCl and a cool menthol sensation to help relieve eye redness and refresh your eyes.

Hypromellose (Eye Mo Moisturizing) formula and Tetrahydrozoline HCI (Eye Mo Cool Red Eyes) can be bought without a prescription, so there should be no excuse for taking better care of your eyes. #MoistUrEyes #REFRESHandRECHARGE #CoolngEyeMo

Give your eyes the rest they need after a long and tiring day! Even the famous English playwright and poet William Shakespeare knows the importance of the eyes – as his famous quote goes – “The eyes are the window to the soul.”

World.title: Trump offers $5,000 to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
World.content:
With approximately 270 million US adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion

DALLAS, USA – US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday, September 9, he would pay every American adult a $5,000 “Trump dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress in November’s midterm election, a striking attempt to persuade voters to back his party.

Trump made the proposal at his Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention, but it was not immediately clear how the payments would work or whether they would be legal. With approximately 270 million US adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion.

During his primetime address, Trump boasted of completing “the greatest two years in the history of the presidency,” putting himself squarely at the center of the election despite his deepening unpopularity.

But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump’s party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran.

“We hand America’s future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet,” he said. “Vote Republicans and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come.”

The two-day Dallas gathering, where Trump will also deliver the closing remarks on Thursday, September 10, after Vice President JD Vance’s keynote address, underscores the extent to which Republicans’ fortunes are tethered to Trump and serves as a showcase for their strategy ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

The event was so centered on the president that Republican national committee chairman Joe Gruters informally dubbed it “Trumpapalooza,” a nod to the popular Lollapalooza music festival.

The focus on Trump amounts to a risky bet that he can mobilize the voters who carried him to the presidency two years ago, despite public polls showing his approval ratings have hit an all-time low. The president vowed to pay multiple visits to battleground states and districts in the eight weeks until Election Day.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot,” Trump said, a line that may have pleased Democratic campaign strategists just as much as MAGA voters.

The convention presented a tough choice in particular for Republicans facing difficult elections who may need to distance themselves from the president to broaden their appeal but cannot afford to alienate Trump’s most committed supporters.

Many such Republicans skipped the convention, including Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan, Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska and Senator Susan Collins of Maine, all facing strong Democratic challengers this fall.

Some, however, elected to travel to Dallas. At least 16 candidates in competitive House and Senate races were scheduled to speak, according to the RNC schedule. Among those who spoke on Wednesday were Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a close Trump ally who is locked in a tough Senate race with Democratic lawmaker James Talarico, and Ohio Senator Jon Husted, who faces former Senator Sherrod Brown.

Though Trump insisted the 21,000-seat arena was “packed,” the upper sections remained largely empty during his speech capping Wednesday’s program.

Democrats portrayed as ‘socialists’ and ‘communists’

While Republican officials had described the convention as an opportunity to tout Trump’s policies, most of the early speakers focused largely on attacking Democrats as extreme on topics such as transgender women in sports and border security – political red meat for the base.

Issues that voters have consistently cited as top concerns, the Iran war and the cost of living, received comparatively less attention.

Alabama state Representative Ernie Yarbrough, a convention attendee, said Trump needs to give voters a clearer sense of how long the war in Iran could last and what the administration’s aims are.

“People want to feel like we’re not getting stuck in an endless cycle,” he said.

Trump defended his decision to attack Tehran, saying he acted to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. He also promised that oil prices would drop “as soon as we win the war with Iran,” which he vowed would happen soon.

But the conflict shows little sign of ending more than six months after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, and analysts have said Iran’s nuclear program has not been eliminated. Iran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.

Before Trump took the stage, a parade of speakers called Democrats “socialists” and “communists,” echoing one of Trump’s favorite attack lines following a handful of victories by democratic socialists in Democratic primary elections.

Democrats are “dangerous, radical and weird,” said Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the party’s Senate campaign arm.

Wednesday’s program also featured a surprise pretaped video from Democratic US Senator John Fetterman, who introduced his fellow senator from Pennsylvania, Republican Dave McCormick, as his “great friend” while declaring he would work with Trump to protect the state’s steel industry.

Fetterman’s extraordinary participation appeared likely to emphasize the ideological divides plaguing the Democratic Party ahead of the midterms. Fetterman, who has increasingly clashed with left-wing Democrats, has denied speculation that he may leave the party.

The convention’s stakes are high for both parties. With the elections less than two months away, Republicans face the prospect of losing control of at least one chamber of Congress, with public polling showing Democrats more motivated to vote and Trump’s approval ratings deeply underwater.

The event faced stiff competition for viewers with the start of the NFL season, with opening night coinciding with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks.

Still, after months of negative headlines over the Iran war and inflation, many Republicans see the gathering as their best chance to promote candidates, draw contrasts with Democrats and energize a Republican electorate expressing less enthusiasm about voting than Democrats, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. – Rappler.com

World.title: Sara Duterte trial barely registers in BARMM campaigns as election nears
World.content:
Sara Duterte remains popular in the Muslim-majority region, as she does in many parts of Mindanao, yet her ongoing impeachment trial has barely figured in the campaign for seats in the Bangsamoro parliament

CAGAYAN DE ORO, Philippines – The ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has become one of the country’s biggest political showdowns, but in the Bangsamoro, where voters head to the polls next week, it appears to have become something many of its politicians would rather not talk about.

With Duterte still retaining a relatively strong national following and the impeachment proceedings putting her at odds with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and groups seeking her removal, politicians and political parties in the Bangsamoro region have largely avoided making the trial an issue in the region’s first parliamentary election, set for Monday, September 14.

Instead, candidates and political operators have mostly kept their options open, content to watch from the sidelines as the impeachment trial and the fight between the pro- and anti-Duterte camps unfold, at least until the votes are counted.

‘Playing safe’

“Not much on the politicians, parang playing safe sila (it seems they are playing safe),” said Drieza Lininding, chairman of the Lanao del Sur-based Moro Consensus Group (MCG).

He said that some, like Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Adiong, are outspoken Duterte critics, “but many tend to wait and see how the impeachment will turn out.”

Adiong, a spokesman for the prosecution team in Duterte’s impeachment trial, is one of the more prominent exceptions. But his position has not necessarily translated into a broader political alignment in his province, including Marawi City, and across the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The congressman is not running for a post in the BARMM regional government but his nephew Abdul Raul is seeking a seat in Lanao del Sur’s 3rd District, while another Adiong, Rashdi, is campaigning for a similar position in the 9th District.

The Adiongs, who supported what became the successful presidential bid of Marcos in 2022, have fielded candidates in the various parliamentary districts in Lanao del Sur and elsewhere in the BARMM through the Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party (SIAP).

Rappler sought comment from Adiong and three other politicians from competing political parties in the BARMM on Wednesday, September 9. None responded by the time of posting.

For Lininding, the bigger question may come after the September 14 vote.

If political forces aligned with Marcos lose, he said, some could blame the president and subsequently look to Duterte.

“The losing parties might blame PBBM (Marcos) and lean on VP Sara to exact political revenge,” Lininding said.

That suggests political fights at the national level do not necessarily dictate political choices in BARMM. It remains to be seen, but past elections have shown that predominantly Muslim areas in Mindanao are not politically uniform, and Duterte’s popularity may not automatically translate to votes for candidates in the parliamentary election.

Unlikely factor

Liezl Bugtay, deputy executive director of Climate Conflict Action Asia (CCAA), said the ongoing impeachment trial appears to have largely been absent from political discussions among voters, candidates, and parties in the BARMM.

“The ongoing impeachment trial won’t likely factor in the outcome of the BARMM elections,” Bugtay told Rappler. “It seems like it’s a non-issue in the region at this time.”

Candidates, she said, have generally not been tackling the impeachment in their campaign sorties, while voters appear to regard Duterte’s trial as separate from the election of the Bangsamoro parliament.

That distinction matters because the BARMM election is taking place against a political history in which national alliances have not always mapped neatly onto regional loyalties.

The political fault lines in the Bangsamoro looked different in 2022.

The contrast was striking. Take, for instance, Abdulraof Macacua, then a senior BARMM minister and head of the MILF’s armed wing, who is said to have backed Marcos in the 2022 elections. Yet his superior at the time and predecessor, then-interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, openly supported former vice president Leni Robredo.

When the votes were counted, Murad and the MILF’s open endorsement did not translate to a Robredo victory. Marcos won with more than one million votes in the BARMM, more than twice Robredo’s total.

Duterte, Marcos’ running mate in 2022, also won in the BARMM by a landslide, including Sulu, which was then still part of the region.

Macacua, currently the interim chief minister, is running for a parliamentary district seat in Maguindanao del Norte under the Bangsamoro Federal Party (BFP), while Murad is the top nominee of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), the political arm of the MILF.

Both played key roles in the MILF’s decades-long struggle for Bangsamoro autonomy and self-determination. If they make it in the September 14 polls, they could find themselves competing directly for the post of chief minister, bringing into the electoral arena a rivalry rooted in their long transition from armed struggle to political power.

Still, the Duterte factor

The lesson from the upcoming election may not be that Duterte’s popularity is irrelevant. Rather, her popularity alone may not determine how BARMM voters cast their ballots on Monday.

Traditional politicians in the region have often aligned themselves with the administration in power. Many of those political networks remain focused on local alliances, family interests, and access to government resources rather than political battles playing out hundreds of kilometers away in Manila.

Still, the Duterte factor endures.

Lininding said many Meranaw in Lanao del Sur openly support Duterte, a sentiment he sees in many online political discussions.

He also pointed to Senator Robinhood Padilla, a hard-line Duterte supporter and the Senate’s only Muslim member.

Padilla’s political prominence gives the Duterte camp a foothold among Muslim voters in the national legislature. A former convict who converted to Islam and was granted an absolute pardon during the presidency of Sara’s father, Rodrigo Duterte, Padilla became the first Muslim senator since the late Santanina Rasul, who left office in 1995 after becoming the first Muslim woman elected to the Philippine Senate in 1987.

Not taking sides – yet

The disconnect is striking given that Sara Duterte remains popular in the Muslim-majority region, as she does in many parts of Mindanao, yet her ongoing impeachment trial has barely figured in the campaign for seats in the Bangsamoro parliament.

That could change, however, after the votes are counted next week.

Monday’s election will be the first parliamentary contest since the Bangsamoro region was created in 2019, determining who controls the legislature and who becomes its first elected chief minister.

But, for now, BARMM’s politicians and parties appear less interested in taking sides in the battle over the vice president’s fate than in ensuring their own political survival. – Rappler.com

World.title: Cayetano siblings left Philippines, BI confirms
World.content:
(2nd UPDATE) The Bureau of Immigration confirms that senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano have left the country amid photos posted on social media showing them in Singapore the night before

MANILA, Philippines – Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano have left the Philippines, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed Thursday, September 10.

The BI’s confirmation came amid photos posted on social media showing the Cayetano siblings arriving in Singapore on Wednesday evening, September 9. A separate social media post also alleged that Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano, Alan’s wife, flew to Singapore early Thursday.

“Based on BI records, there were no hold departure orders or derogatory records against the two senators, as of departure date, that would legally prevent them from leaving the country,” the BI said.

The agency declined to provide details about their travel, including their itinerary and other related information, citing the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

The Cayetanos’ departure comes as the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) prepares to recommend to the Department of Justice the filing of cases over alleged irregularities in the Philippines’ hosting of the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games.

Alan served as chairperson of the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), the nonprofit organization tasked with organizing and managing the country’s hosting of the 2019 SEA Games. He was also House speaker at the time.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag, however, said Cayetano was not identified as PHISGOC chairperson in the organization’s corporate records and financial documents, and the lack of a paper trail linking the senator to the alleged irregularities has hampered the investigation.

‘Personal, health reasons’

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian did not confirm the Cayetanos’ trip but said senators traveling abroad for personal reasons are not required to seek travel authority.

“Kapag personal trips, hindi na kailangan mag-abiso ang mga senador,” Gatchalian said. (Senators do not need to seek travel authority for personal trips.)

Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri said Alan’s trip with his wife was for personal and health reasons.

“Mayor Lani has been trying to conceive a baby. They’re there for personal reasons. I wish them well,” Zubiri said, echoing Gatchalian’s remarks that senators do not need to seek travel authority for personal trips.

Alan and Lani were married in 2004. When the senator turned 49 in 2019, he said his birthday wish was to have children, and that he was “praying for twins, soon.” They have remained childless.

Alan is turning 56 in October while Lani is turning 45 in October.

Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson also said the Cayetanos’ departure was not an issue at this point. He also urged the public to allow Alan to “take a break from the stress caused by issues that he himself created.”

“For all we know, Sen Alan and his wife’s trip has something to do with reproductive health, which Singapore is known for. If it is simply health related, I sincerely wish him well despite our animosities,If it’s simply health-related, I sincerely wish him well despite our animosities,” said Lacson.

In July, Lacson submitted evidence on alleged irregularities in flood control projects in Taguig City to the Office of the Ombudsman for review. The allegations involved projects linked to Alan, who had denied the claims.

The departure of the Cayetanos from the country brings to three the total number of senators who are currently abroad. Senator Loren Legarda is on extended medical leave in France until September 16. – Rappler.com

World.title: Owner appeals for rescue of dog missing in Palawan ferry fire
World.content:
A golden retriever is missing after a fire broke out aboard the ferry MV June Aster in the waters off Coron town, Palawan, on Wednesday evening, Sept. 9, 2026. Screenshot from video by Nics Ramos

PUERTO PRINCESA CITY—A golden retriever is among the passengers missing after a fire broke out aboard the ferry MV June Aster in the waters off Coron town, Palawan, on Wednesday evening.

In a Facebook post, Nics Ramos is appealing for his dog “Ali” to be included in the search and rescue operations.

“Sana ma-rescue po ang Ali namin na isa sa mga passenger sa nasunog na barko (MV JUNE ASTER). Pls po sana maisama po siya sa rescue kahit hindi na po mabalik sa amin, basta po safe siya. Please po, mabait na baby po namin ito at sumasama talaga sa tao,” Ramos said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Search on for missing passengers of vessel off Palawan

(I hope our Ali will be rescued, as he is one of the passengers of the burnt ferry. Please include him in the rescue, and even if he is not returned to us, just as long as he is safe. Please, our baby is good, and he always goes with people.)

“Wala po akong makuhang contact sa kasama po niya sa barko, kaya wala po kaming update. Jerick po yung pangalan ng kasama niya sa barko. Please po sana ma-rescue po si Ali namin,” he added.

(I could not reach those who were with him in the boat; that’s why we don’t have any update. Jerick is the one with him in the boat. Please, I hope our Ali is rescued.)

At least five people were killed, and 87 remain unaccounted for after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan. /coa

World.title: Hontiveros ‘no reason to be scared’ amid libel charge from Quiboloy
World.content:
Sen. Risa Hontiveros and Apollo Quiboloy. INQUIRER FILE PHOTOS

MANILA, Philippines – Sen. Risa Hontiveros asserted on Thursday that she has no reason to be scared in comparison to Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) founder Apollo Quiboloy, who is wanted by the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation for alleged human and sex trafficking of children among others.

Hontiveros remarked after Quiboloy’s legal counsel, Ferdinand Topacio, announced that the pastor will file libel and cyber libel charges against the senator and two other lawmakers.

“Kung talagang naniniwala si Quiboloy sa hustisya at sa Diyos, harapin niya ang mga paratang laban sa kanya. Managot na lang sya, imbes na baligtarin ang usapan. Dahil ako? Wala akong kailangang ikatakot,” Hontiveros said in a statement.

Article continues after this 

(If Quiboloy truly believes in justice and God, he should face the charges against him. He should just answer, instead of turning the tables. Because me? I have nothing to fear.)

READ: Cendaña to Quiboloy camp: Better libelous than sex trafficker

She then enumerated the charges Quiboloy is facing.

“Si Quiboloy ang wanted ng FBI. Si Quiboloy ang akusado sa mga matitinding krimen. Siya ang may kasong human trafficking, sexual abuse, at child abuse. Siya ang itinuro ng mga biktima na nagtulak sa kanilang manlimos para siya ay yumaman. Siya ang itinurong sexual abuser ng mga babae at menor de edad,” the senator stressed.

(Quiboloy is wanted by the FBI. Quiboloy is accused of serious crimes. He is charged with human trafficking, sexual abuse, and child abuse. He is the one the victims have accused of forcing them to beg so that he can get rich. He is accused of being a sexual abuser of women and minors.)

Article continues after this 

Further, Hontiveros reiterated her promise of protecting Quiboloy’s victims.

“Ang dapat nating protektahan ay ang mga biktima at kababayan nating naglakas-loob magsalita at lumantad laban kay Quiboloy. Hangga’t humihingi sila ng hustisya, tatayo ako sa tabi nila,” she added.

Article continues after this 

(What we must protect are the victims and our countrymen who dared to speak out and stand up against Quiboloy. As long as they demand justice, I will stand by them.)

As head of the Senate panel on women, children, family relations, and gender equality, Hontiveros led the probe into Quiboloy’s alleged involvement in human trafficking, sexual abuse of minors, forced labor and rights violations.

Quiboloy is currently detained at the Pasig City Jail, as he faces qualified human trafficking case before the Pasig City Regional Trial Court (RTC) and sexual abuse and maltreatment before the Quezon City RTC.

READ: DOJ to study US request for Quiboloy extradition

World.title: DND chief: Sara Duterte yet to request security withdrawal but she may
World.content:
Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro – Screengrabbed from video of Noy Morcoso / Inquirer

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has yet to request the withdrawal of her security detail, but she may do so, according to Defense Secretary Gilbert “Gibo” Teodoro.

Teodoro made the statement in an ambush interview on Thursday, amid Duterte’s pronouncements that she no longer had trust in those assigned to her security.

“Nasabi ko na na karapatan naman niyang i-request na i-withdraw,” he said.

Article continues after this 

(I’ve already said that she has the right to request their withdrawal.)

Asked if he had received any such requests from the Vice President, Teodoro said, “Wala akong natatanggap.” (I have not received any)

The issue over Duterte’s lack of trust in her security stemmed from her concerns raised while she was at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court to post bail for her grave threats case.

That time, Duterte said she could no longer trust even her own security detail because she believed they had been picked for the job by the Marcos administration.

READ: Sara Duterte posts bail: ‘I don’t trust the court’

Article continues after this 

Before she entered the premises, Duterte made a show of her apprehension, saying she did not feel safe and did not trust the court or the police.

Despite her lawyers’ attempts to persuade her to go inside, the discussion lasted about 40 minutes before her lawyer Michael Poa finally convinced her to enter the building.

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, when asked if Duterte could choose her own security personnel if she requested the withdrawal of those assigned to her, Teodoro answered in the affirmative.

“Well, yeah, because, you know, provision of AFP security is a courtesy and a privilege. You can ask for them to be withdrawn if there is a loss of trust and confidence,” he said.

Asked again whether Duterte could choose from among AFP or Philippine National Police personnel who would be assigned to her, Teodoro said, “Normally, ako nga, hindi ko pinipili ’yung mga nakatalaga sa akin. Gano’n ang tiwala ko sa sundalo ng Pilipinas.”

(Normally, I don’t choose the people assigned to me. That’s how much I trust the soldiers of the Philippines.)

“Kasi ang sundalo naman, nasabi ko na nga, mission-trained ’yan. Wala namang personalan ’yon eh,” he added.

(Because our soldiers, as I’ve already said, they are mission-trained. There’s nothing personal about it,)

World.title: Sandiganbayan: Some flood control cases may be resolved within the year
World.content:
Facade of the Sandiganbayan in Quezon City. INQUIRER PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan on Thursday said some flood control cases could be decided within the year as the anti-graft court pushes for the speedy disposition of corruption cases.

Sandiganbayan Presiding Justice Geraldine Faith Econg, during the Senate budget hearing for the judiciary’s 2027 planned spending, said that as of now, there were already 26 cases filed before the anti-graft court.

She said these include cases against some senators and congressmen.

Article continues after this 

READ: Sandiganbayan orders BJMP to take custody of Romualdez

“Of the flood control cases that were filed, the first of these cases was filed by the Office of the Ombudsman on Nov. 18, 2025. They are already on the defense side,” Econg told the senators.

“That means that in less than a year, we are already on the defense stage, so that was pretty fast,” she added.

Without naming names, Econg said that one of the earliest cases filed was archived because the accused could not be located.

“The other cases that have co-accused are already on the defense stage,” she said.

Article continues after this 

Asked by Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian if a resolution of that particular cases may happen soon, Econg said: “If we follow the Speedy Trial Act tat was enacted by the Supreme Court, we will see conviction within the year, or acquittal, within the year.”

“The disposition within the year, which may be a conviction or acquittal,” she added.

Article continues after this 

“We will no longer say what’s our preference,” Gatchalian said in jest. /mr

World.title: Cabotaje-Tang, Ombudsman exec among first witnesses for Article II
World.content:
Senate impeachment court (INQUIRER file photo / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA)

MANILA, Philippines — Former Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang is among the first three witnesses that the prosecution panel will call for Article II of the Articles of Impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said on Thursday.

During a press briefing on Thursday, Ridon announced the witnesses that the prosecution panel asked a subpoena for from the Senate impeachment court, for discussions on Article II or allegations of Duterte having unexplained wealth:

Cabotaje-Tang

Atty. Karen Batu, officer-in-charge, Office of the Ombudsman Records Division

Atty. Gerardo del Rosario, Director, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) – Company Registration and Monitoring Department

According to Ridon, Cabotaje-Tang will be asked to testify about the principles governing public accountability and integrity.

Article continues after this 

Batu, meanwhile, will discuss the details of Duterte’s Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

“Tatlo po ‘yong hiningan ng pag-issue ng subpoena ad testificandum, una po si former presiding justice ng Sandiganbayan, si retired Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang, pag-uusapan po niya ‘yong mga prinsipyo governing ‘yong usapin po ng public accountability, integrity in public office, at mechanisms for addressing undisclosed and unexplained wealth, and prohibited business interests,” he said.

(We have asked for a subpoena ad testificandum for three individuals, first is former Sandiganbayan presiding justice, retired Justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang, to discuss the principles governing discussions of public accountability, integrity in public office, and mechanisms for addressing undisclosed and unexplained wealth, and prohibited business interests.)

“Si Atty. Karen Batu, officer-in-charge, Records Division ng Office of the Ombudsman, tatalakayin po ‘yong mga partikular na detalye sa SALN ng atin pong pangalawang pangulo, partikular po ‘yong submissions,” he added.

(Atty. Karen Batu, officer-in-charge, Records Division ng Office of the Ombudsman, will also be asked to tesitfy for discussions on the particular details of our vice president’s SALN, especially her submissions.)

Article continues after this 

Ridon also said that del Rosario will be asked to testify about the records concerning the businesses owned by Duterte that are registered with the SEC.

“At panghuli, si Atty. Gerardo del Rosario ng Securities and Exchange Commission, Director, Company Registration and Monitoring Department, kung saan pag-uusapan po ‘yong pag-authenticate at pag-identify ng records no’n pong mga kumpanya ng atin pong pangalawang pangulo,” he said.

Article continues after this 

(Finally, Atty. Gerardo del Rosario of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Director, Company Registration and Monitoring Department, will be asked to authenticate and identify the records of the vice president’s companies.)

“So naghahanda na po ‘yong unexplained wealth team para po doon sa pagbubukas ng article po na ito. So hopefully in the next two to three weeks — particularly kung mahaba po ‘yong paglilitis matapos po namin hopefully before the middle of October or at the start of October, ito pong pagbubukas at pagsasara nitong unexplained wealth article,” he added.

(So the unexplained wealth team is preparing for the opening of this article. So hopefully in the next two to three weeks — particularly if we will have longer hearing days, hopefully we can finish before the middle of October or at the start of October, and close this unexplained wealth article.)

Batu and the SEC were both invited to the House of Representatives’ committee on justice which tackled the two impeachment complaints against Duterte.

However, this is the first time that Cabotaje-Tang will be affiliated with the impeachment proceedings.

READ: Ombudsman exec confirms Sara Duterte’s SALNs from 2007 to 2024

Cabotaje-Tang was appointed by then – President Benigno Aquino III to be the presiding judge of the Sandiganbayan in October 2013, following the mandatory retirement of Associate Justice Francisco Villaruz.

She was one of the junior justices appointed to ranking posts in the Judiciary during Aquino’s time, including former Supreme Court Chief Justice Maria Lourdes Sereno.

Prior to her appointment to the Sandiganbayan, Cabotaje-Tang was a former assistant solicitor-general. She had just been with the anti-graft court for a year before Aquino named her to the top spot.

READ: Aquino appoints new Sandiganbayan presiding justice

World.title: P7.1M in ‘smuggled’ cigarettes seized in Zamboanga del Norte
World.content:
CONTRABAND INTERCEPTED. Police officers inspect 1,853 reams of suspected smuggled cigarettes valued at P7.15 million seized at a checkpoint in Barangay Gatas, Kalawit, Zamboanga del Norte, late Tuesday night, Sept. 8, 2026. Photo by 2nd ZNPMFC

PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Authorities intercepted over P7.1 million worth of suspected smuggled cigarettes and arrested two suspects who allegedly attempted to bribe their way through a border checkpoint in Kalawit, Zamboanga del Norte, late Tuesday night.

In a police report, authorities identified the suspects as Elvin, 44, a driver, and Hussam, 49, a helper, both residents of Barangay Rio Hondo, Zamboanga City.

Elements of the 2nd Platoon, 2nd Zamboanga del Norte Provincial Mobile Force Company (ZNPMFC), alongside the Kalawit Municipal Police Station, flagged down a silver Nissan NV350 Urvan (GAN 7637) at a border control point in Barangay Gatas around 11:50 p.m. on Sept. 8.

Article continues after this 

READ: Central Luzon police net P960M in suspected smuggled cigarettes

During the inspection, officers noticed a modified compartment in the vehicle.

Suspicious of the occupants’ uneasy behavior, police questioned the duo about the hidden space.

Hoping to avoid arrest, the suspects admitted to carrying contraband and allegedly offered officers a P100,000 bribe to let them pass.

Police rejected the bribe and immediately searched the hidden compartment, discovering 1,853 reams of suspected smuggled cigarettes.

Article continues after this 

After inventory of the seized goods, Bureau of Customs (BOC) personnel valued the contraband at P7,152,580.

The suspects, the vehicle, and the confiscated cigarettes were brought to the Kalawit Municipal Police Station for proper disposition and the filing of appropriate charges./coa

World.title: Tensions flare as Marcos courts foreign investors for Luzon Corridor
World.content:
Photo courtesy of the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tensions erupted outside a hotel in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City, on Thursday, where President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was attending an event.

Protesters holding placards and banners staged a protest outside the Grand Hyatt Hotel in Bonifacio Global City, opposing the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) Investment Forum.

READ: Foreign investors coming to scout Luzon

Article continues after this 

The two-day event gathered international investors, industry leaders, and project developers to explore investment opportunities within the LEC, which spans Metro Manila, Clark, Subic, and Batangas.

Photo courtesy of the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association Facebook

In a statement, the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association (PPFA) said it “strongly condemns the Marcos Jr. administration for rolling out the red carpet to foreign investors.”

“The government presents the corridor as an ‘economic development program’, but its projects will involve land conversion, increased resource extraction, and the expansion of infrastructure for foreign and private investment. It also serves broader U.S. economic and strategic interests in the Philippines,” it read.

Photo courtesy of the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association Facebook

Launched in April 2024, the LEC is a trilateral infrastructure partnership among the Philippines, the United States, and Japan.

The Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas corridor is expected to create thousands of jobs, while stronger transport, energy, digital, and manufacturing links aim to boost economic activity and attract investments.

Article continues after this 

But for the PPFA, ordinary Filipinos will bear “many of the social and environmental costs,” while investors and large corporations stand to gain from the projects.

Turn pledges into reality

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, in his speech during the forum, Marcos urged investors to turn LEC commitments into funded and operational projects.

“The success of the LEC will not be measured by the number of meetings that we hold or projects that we announce,” Marcos said.

“It will be measured by what we finance, by what we build, what we place into operation—by the jobs, the enterprises, and the opportunities that we create for our people,” he continued.

He also said his administration is improving the movement of people and goods across the Corridor and expanding energy capacity to meet the needs of industries and communities.

The government is also developing renewable resources, strengthening the power grid, pursuing reliable energy technologies, and building the digital foundations of a modern economy by expanding secure connectivity and advanced computing infrastructure.

“We are strengthening cybersecurity and establishing safeguards for the responsible use of AI. The Philippines already has a strong base of digitally capable workers,” he said.

World.title: 4 arrested, 16 cops injured at rally outside Taguig City forum
World.content:
(Photo courtesy of the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association Facebook)

MANILA, Philippines — Four individuals were arrested during a rally outside a forum attended by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. at Bonifacio Global City (BGC) in Taguig City on Thursday, according to the Southern Police District (SPD).

“Pilit sila pumapasok. Pinagbabawal naman,” SPD Deputy Director for Operations Col. Robert Baesa said in an interview with reporters.

(They were forcibly trying to enter. It’s not allowed.)

Article continues after this 

“Kakasuhan yun. Illegal assembly. Bawal dito. Wala namang permit dito sa BGC mag-rally,” he added.

(They’ll be charged with illegal assembly. It’s not allowed here. They don’t have a permit here in BGC to hold a rally.)

READ: Pax Silica and the Luzon Economic Corridor: The capability test

Tensions reportedly flared outside the Luzon Economic Corridor Investors Forum as protesters voiced opposition to Pax Silica, a United States (US)-led coalition of 14 countries—including the Philippines—aiming to strengthen supply chains for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

Stakeholders and progressive groups have raised concerns related to the possible displacement of communities and environmental protection.

Article continues after this 

According to Baesa, at least 16 police officers were injured.

“Mga suntok. May mga gasgas-gasgas. May mga tama,” he explained.

Article continues after this 

(They were punched. Some had scratches. Some were hit.)

“Hindi kailanman nagsimula ang pulis talaga ng gulo… Lagi namang maximum tolerance kami,” he added.

(The police have never started trouble… We’ve always been for maximum tolerance.)

He noted that the four individuals arrested were taken to the Taguig City Police Station.

In a statement later on Thursday, however, the Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment said only three individuals had been arrested, identifying them as paralegals.

“This is an outrageous and scandalous act of harassment against human rights defenders simply doing their job,” the group maintained.

“We condemn this blatant attack on paralegals and the shrinking space for dissent against foreign-dominated infrastructure deals like the Luzon Economic Corridor,” it added.
